## 0. How to use this document

If you are an AI picking this up fresh:
1. Read **§1 (what this is)** and **§2 (the pivot)** — do not skip.
2. Read **§3 (architecture decisions)** — these are locked; do not re-litigate.
3. Read **§4 (UX principles)** — every piece of UI built must satisfy these; they are requirements, not guidelines.
4. Read **§5 (native app strategy)** — every frontend decision must account for future native app port.
5. Check **§11 (progress log)** — source of truth for what is done vs. planned.
6. Find the current phase in **§10 (roadmap)** and continue from the first unchecked item.
7. The full schema is in **§7**. Always check there before inventing table names or columns.
8. At the end of your session, **update §11** with what changed and tick off completed steps in §10.
9. **Before writing any frontend file from scratch, check §13 (source code snapshots)** — if a working version already exists there, read it first; don't regenerate from memory or re-ask the human to re-paste code that's already captured.
10. **After any migration or RLS/permissions change, run the cross-tenant isolation test suite in §9.1** — this is a required step, not optional, and is part of the Definition of Done for any session touching schema or RLS. The owner can also call for this suite directly at any time (e.g. "give me the isolation test" / "run the RLS check") — when asked, present the full §9.1 section, including its five embedded scripts, ready to copy into the Supabase SQL Editor.

I am building **Eduportal NG** — a multi-tenant SaaS school management platform for Nigerian schools (kindergarten, primary, secondary JSS/SSS, madrasas, and any other type). The master project plan is in `MASTER_PROJECT_PLAN.md` — read it in full before doing anything.

**Key facts to hold while working:**

**Stack:** React + Vite + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS. Backend: Supabase (shared multi-tenant Postgres + RLS + Auth + Edge Functions + Storage). Bulk files: Cloudflare R2. Hosting: Netlify (GitHub-connected auto-deploy). Dev device: Android phone with Termux. Workflow: AI generates code → paste into **micro** (Termux text editor) → `npm run dev` in Termux → test in phone browser → `git push` → Netlify auto-builds. **Note: editor is `micro`, not Acode — Acode cannot open Termux filesystem paths.**

**RLS is everything.** Every table has `school_id` scoped via `current_school_id()`. Every new table MUST have its RLS policy in the SAME migration. The unified identity model is `app_identities` — every authenticatable person (staff, guardian, student) has a real `auth.users` row regardless of login method. Login-code auth is handled by the `login-with-code` Edge Function using the service-role key server-side. The service-role key NEVER appears in client code.

**UX is the highest priority.** Every screen must: load under 1 second on 3G; work fully offline with optimistic updates; require zero training for daily tasks; be designed mobile-first. The primary users are Nigerian teachers marking attendance on cheap Android phones, parents checking fees on WhatsApp-generation phones, and admins who may not be tech-savvy.

**Schema (61 tables) is finalized** — all in §7 of MASTER_PROJECT_PLAN.md. Do not invent columns or tables not in the schema without flagging it. Key rules: no hard deletes, computed values are views not columns (fee balances, grades, positions, leave balances), money is `numeric(14,2)`, every table has `id uuid`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `school_id` (school-scoped) or explicit `[PLATFORM]` flag.

**Future native app:** every frontend decision must account for a future React Native port. Use platform-agnostic state management (Zustand or similar), keep business logic out of UI components, avoid browser-only APIs in shared logic, use design tokens for all colors/spacing/typography.

**The old madrasah app** (Dilimi Qur'an school, Supabase project `duqurodgelubbowtscix.supabase.co`) is live and untouched — do not touch it. **It is also, separately, a read-only design/pattern reference** for `PRD_updated.md`'s Tier 6 (its `index__17_.html` build is where the login-page/timetable design language, live-period widget, icon set, modal pattern, settings/alarm system, term-progress-with-holiday-extend concept, app shell/navigation chrome, and the Attendance/Students/Announcements module layouts were sourced from — read from it freely, never write to it). The port covers the reference app's whole structural/flow language, not just a short list of named widgets — see PRD §0.4's second-pass inventory.

**Current tactical execution plan lives in `PRD_updated.md`, not here.** As of Tier 0–5 (identity, onboarding, permissions, dashboards, module correctness) plus the expanded Tier 6 (design-system port, 11 problems: token/icon/login-timetable/live-widget/modal/settings-alarm/term-progress, plus app shell, Attendance, Students+Announcements, and a pattern-language pass over the 5 modules with no reference-app equivalent) and Tier 7 (public homepage + i18n), `PRD_updated.md` is the authoritative, session-by-session breakdown — read it in full alongside this document, not instead of it. This master plan remains the schema/architecture/UX-principles source of truth; the PRD is where "what to build next, in what order, and how to verify it" lives for the current phase of work.

**Locked decisions (never re-litigate):** unlimited-depth `class_nodes` tree; fully custom roles via `permissions` catalog; `uses_terms` flag for optional terms; `uses_ledger` flag for double-entry ledger; results are computed views; inter-school transfer is consent-gated with permanent history at releasing school; English is system default language; school name is never translated.

At the end of this session, update §11 of MASTER_PROJECT_PLAN.md with what was done.

## 1. What this project is

A **generic Nigerian school operating system** — a SaaS platform serving any school type: kindergarten, primary, secondary (junior and senior, including sub-classes like JSS 3A/3B), and madrasas (meeting once, twice, or irregularly per week). Every structural assumption — class hierarchy, calendar, subjects, grading, fees, roles — is **configuration the school sets for itself**, not baked into the code.

**One product, modular:** timetable, attendance, results management, fees/finance, HR/payroll, library, announcements, communications. Schools subscribe to the core and activate modules.

**Two user-facing surfaces:**
- A **pre-login public homepage** per school (their own subdomain, accessible to parents, the public, prospective families)
- The **main application** (admin/staff dashboard + guardian/student portal)

**Future surface (planned, not built yet):** native mobile apps (iOS + Android) — see §5.

**Market:** Nigerian schools primarily. Starting with Islamic/Quran schools (less saturated, known pain points), expanding to general schools. Key differentiators: Nigerian payment rails (Paystack/Flutterwave), Hausa/Arabic/English i18n, offline-first, mobile-first, price accessible to small schools.

**Current live system:** The previous single-file madrasah app is still live on Netlify serving Dilimi Qur'an Memorization School. It runs undisturbed while this rebuild is built. **Do not touch it.**

## 2. The pivot decision

### What came before
Seven sessions of iterative work on a single `index.html` PWA built for one Qur'an school. By session 7 it had: Supabase backend with RLS, DB-driven timetable, attendance, 3-language i18n, 30 dynamic-day fixes, generalized print functions, and the start of a `quran_module` flag.

### Why it was abandoned
The owner's full vision made the existing codebase the wrong foundation:
- Serve **all Nigerian school types** — not just madrasas
- **Unlimited class hierarchy** (JSS 3A/3B/3C, streams, arms — any depth)
- Proper **results management** (WAEC-style, CA, custom grading per school)
- **Full double-entry finance** (not just fee tracking)
- **Full HR/payroll** module
- **Physical + digital library** module
- True **modular architecture** — each module as a standalone route and table-set
- **Future native apps** — single-file HTML cannot grow into that

The existing `class_name` text field, hardcoded 2-day week, and timetable-first architecture could not accommodate this without becoming unmaintainable. Rebuild was the correct call.

### What carries forward as patterns (not as code)
- Supabase shared-tenant architecture + RLS
- `school_id` scoping on every school-owned table
- Offline-first read/write queue pattern (`cachedLoad`, `queueWrite`, `flushQueue`)
- Three-language i18n (English / Arabic / Hausa) with RTL/LTR
- Staff on Supabase Auth; students/guardians on flexible login methods
- Pricing and market research (see §6)

---

## 3. Architecture decisions (locked — do not re-litigate without documented reason)

### 3.1 Shared multi-tenant database
One Supabase project, all schools. Every school-scoped table has `school_id uuid not null references schools(id)`. RLS enforces isolation. Exception path (own Supabase project per school) only for a real, specific compliance need — priced as ~$10/mo add-on, never proactive.

### 3.2 RLS is the single point of failure
One helper function family covers every role and login method:
```sql
current_school_id()    -- returns school_id for any authenticated actor
current_actor_type()   -- returns 'staff' | 'guardian' | 'student' | 'platform_admin'
is_platform_admin()    -- returns boolean
```
Every new table gets its RLS policy in the **same migration that creates it** — never as a follow-up. Cross-school isolation is manually tested before onboarding school #2.

### 3.3 The login-code RLS gap is permanently closed
Every authenticatable person now has a real Supabase Auth identity regardless of login method. Login-code auth is handled by an Edge Function (`login-with-code`) using the Auth Admin API with the service-role key (server-side only, never shipped to client). The `app_identities` table (§7.2) is the unified lookup.

### 3.4 Unlimited class hierarchy — self-referencing tree
Classes are `class_nodes`, a self-referencing tree with unlimited depth. `node_type` is advisory only — no application logic branches on it. Only `is_leaf_enrollable = true` nodes can have students enrolled.

### 3.5 Subjects: default-plus-overrides
Default: everyone in a class/arm takes the same subject list. Two opt-in overrides: per-student elective overrides, and stream-based subject sets (modeled as child class_nodes with their own subject lists).

### 3.6 Calendar: optional terms
`schools.uses_terms` controls whether Session → Term structure is used. When false, `term_id` is null everywhere and everything scopes to the session directly. One schema serves both shapes.

### 3.7 Custom roles and permissions
Roles are data, not a code enum. Each school defines its own role names. `permissions` is a platform-defined fixed catalog that schools combine into roles. Staff can hold multiple roles; effective permissions are the union.

### 3.8 Results: computed views, never stored columns
Subject totals, grade letters, and class positions are views over raw scores — not columns that could go stale. The approval gate (`approved_at is not null`) is enforced at the RLS policy level, not just in app code.

### 3.9 Finance: dual system behind one flag
Fee collection always works. Full double-entry ledger activates per school with `schools.uses_ledger = true`. When on, payments and payroll auto-post to `journal_entries` via database trigger. When off, they still work — the trigger just doesn't fire.

### 3.10 Nothing is ever hard-deleted
Students get `alumni` or `transferred_out` status. Staff get `inactive`/`suspended`. Financial records are never touched. The audit log only grows — no update/delete on `audit_log` rows, enforced at RLS level.

### 3.11 Inter-school transfer is consent-gated
Export-then-import with a request/approval trail. History at the releasing school stays intact forever. The receiving school gets a new `students` row pre-filled from the exported snapshot. Two schools never share a live row.

### 3.12 Documents generated on demand, not stored
Report cards, receipts, and invoices are generated client-side for printing. No PDF storage cost. No `generated_documents` table.

### 3.13 File storage split
- **Supabase Storage:** small, auth-scoped files (student photos, documents)
- **Cloudflare R2:** bulk content (digital library PDFs, video/audio) — zero egress fees

### 3.14 Subdomain per school
Each school gets `{slug}.platformdomain.com`. App reads `window.location.hostname` at startup before any login. Unknown slug → generic "school not found" page, not a crash.

### 3.15 Two tiers of admin
- **School admin:** full control within their `school_id`
- **Platform admin (you):** cross-tenant access via `is_platform_admin()` for 3 platform-scoped tables (digital library, billing, audit cross-read). Not a `staff` row in any school.

### 3.16 `school_type` and `node_type` are inert labels — **amended 2026-07-13, see below**
No application logic ever branches on these. They exist for admin UI labeling and reporting only. If code says `if (school.school_type === 'madrasah')` — that is wrong. Behavior comes from configuration, never from a type string.

**Amendment (PRD Tier 8 / Problem 8.7, 2026-07-13):** this rule's stated future has arrived for `school_type` specifically, in one narrow, deliberate place. As of Problem 8.7 (higher-institution academic support), `school_type` is read exactly once, at the top of the academic-engine selection: to decide whether a school renders the secondary-school academic model (class membership, daily attendance, subject/term scoring) or the higher-institution academic model (course registration, per-course attendance, GPA/CGPA — see §7.27 below). This is a genuine, recorded exception to this section's rule, not a silent violation of it — everything *downstream* of that single branch point still follows the rule exactly as written: no further code anywhere branches on `school_type` a second time, and `node_type` remains fully inert with no exception at all. If a future contributor finds `school_type` being read anywhere else in the codebase, that is still wrong per this section and should be fixed, not treated as precedent. The higher-institution *category* sub-choice (University / Polytechnic-Monotechnic / College of Education / Other) introduced alongside this amendment is a config-defaults selector only (§7.27, Phase 0 Decision 1) — it pre-fills `grade_scales`/`cgpa_policy` values and is never itself branched on in application logic, so it does not create a second exception to this rule.

## 4. UX principles (non-negotiable — every UI decision must satisfy these)

User satisfaction is the highest priority at every point in this project. These are requirements, not aspirations. Every screen, flow, interaction, and piece of copy must be evaluated against these before it is considered done.

### 4.1 Speed above all
- Every screen a user visits daily (attendance, timetable, dashboard, fee summary) must feel instant — under 1 second perceived load on a typical Nigerian 3G connection.
- **Optimistic UI everywhere:** mark attendance, save a score, record a payment — the UI confirms immediately and syncs in the background. The user never waits for a server round-trip to see their own action reflected.
- **Offline-first:** the app continues working when offline. Changes are queued and flushed when connectivity returns. Users are never blocked by connectivity for any task they could complete without new data.
- **Aggressive caching on first load:** timetable, student list, class list, subjects, fee structure — data that changes rarely. Serve cache instantly; refresh in background. Use the same `cachedLoad`/`queueWrite`/`flushQueue` pattern established in the old app.
- **Lazy-load modules:** ship only the currently-needed module. Payroll, library, digital resources — don't bundle them for a teacher who only marks attendance.
- **Indexed queries:** any column used in a frequent `WHERE` clause gets an index. This is part of schema work, not an afterthought.

### 4.2 Mobile-first, always
- The primary device for every user type (teacher, admin, guardian, student) is a phone — likely mid-range Android, likely on 3G.
- Design every screen for a phone first (~390px viewport). Verify on tablet/desktop afterward.
- Touch targets: minimum 44×44px. No precision tapping.
- Forms are short. Multi-step flows (onboarding, fee assignment, score entry) show one logical task per screen.
- Keyboard-aware: forms must push content up when the soft keyboard opens, never hide the active input.
- Bottom navigation bar for primary routes — the most common actions are thumb-reachable.
- Swipe gestures supplement tap targets, never replace them.

### 4.3 Zero training required for daily tasks
- Every flow a teacher or guardian uses daily must be completable without reading any instructions.
- Labels describe what something does, not what it is. "Record today's attendance" not "Attendance module." "View your child's report" not "Results."
- **Empty states are actionable:** no blank screens. "No students yet — add your first student →" with a direct button.
- **Errors explain and guide:** "Can't save — check your connection, then tap Retry" not "Error 500." Never show a technical error message to any user.
- **Progressive disclosure:** the most common action is prominent. Advanced options (edit timetable, manage roles, configure grading) are one tap deeper, not on the main screen.
- **Confirmation dialogs only for irreversible actions.** Don't ask "Are you sure?" for marking attendance — do ask for deleting a student record.

### 4.4 Respect for every user type

**Admin:** needs overview and control without being overwhelmed. Dashboard shows what needs attention today — pending score approvals, upcoming fee deadlines, unread requests. Settings are organized by module and searchable, not a wall of options. Admin should feel in control, never lost.

**Teacher:** needs raw speed for daily tasks. Marking attendance for 30 students should take under 60 seconds. Score entry shows the class list pre-populated — the teacher just fills in numbers. No unnecessary navigation between tasks. Timetable is always one tap from anywhere in the app. Show the current lesson in the header.

**Guardian/Parent:** needs reassurance and clarity. They are checking on their child. Results, attendance, and fees in plain language — no jargon. Translate everything. Never show a number without context: "Absent 3 times" should also show "out of 45 school days (93% attendance)". Fee balance of ₦15,000 means nothing without showing what was billed and what was paid. First screen after login = their child's summary, not a menu.

**Student:** needs simplicity and a sense of progress. Results shown with grade context and class position. Attendance as a visual summary strip. Announcements and school calendar prominently. If a student doesn't yet have platform access, the guardian can see everything on their behalf.

### 4.5 Language and localization done properly
- **English is the system default.** Arabic and Hausa are first-class — not afterthoughts with missing strings.
- **RTL layout (Arabic) flips the entire interface** — icon positions, padding sides, swipe directions, navigation alignment, text alignment. Not just `dir="rtl"` on the body.
- **School name is NEVER translated or transliterated.** It always appears exactly as entered by the admin, in every language mode, in every component.
- **Numbers in Arabic mode** use Eastern Arabic numerals (٠١٢٣٤٥٦٧٨٩) — configurable per school, not assumed.
- **Dates** respect locale. Nigerian English: DD/MM/YYYY. Arabic: Hijri calendar option. Configurable per school.
- Every i18n key must exist in all three languages before a component is shipped. No fallback to English for missing keys in production.
- Language switcher shows only the languages the school admin has enabled for their school.

### 4.6 Onboarding that doesn't feel like homework
- The wizard is the first impression. It must feel like guided setup assistance, not form-filling.
- Each step is a **single, clear task** with a friendly heading ("What days does your school run?"), a short one-sentence explanation, and obvious controls.
- **Progress saved automatically after every step.** Admin can close the browser, leave for a week, return and resume exactly where they left off. Never lose work.
- **Sensible defaults pre-fill everything:** Mon–Fri week, standard 8-period day with a break, common Nigerian subject names as autocomplete suggestions, standard Grade A-F scale. Admin confirms or changes — never builds from nothing.
- Each step's output is available to the next. Order: school identity → language → calendar structure → week days & periods → subjects → class hierarchy → roles & permissions → staff. A step never asks for data that won't exist until a later step.
- **Skip and return:** some steps (e.g. class hierarchy for a school that is still organizing) can be skipped and completed from settings later. The wizard marks them incomplete and the dashboard surfaces a prompt to return.
- The wizard is also accessible as a "setup guide" from admin settings after onboarding — in case an admin wants to revisit their configuration methodically.

### 4.7 Consistency — one product, everywhere
- One visual language: same colors, same type scale, same button styles, same card layout, same loading skeleton, same error format — across all modules.
- Navigation in the same place and working the same way in every module. A user who learns to navigate attendance can navigate fees.
- **Action verbs are consistent throughout the app.** If adding a student is "Add student" here, it is not "New student" elsewhere and "Register student" somewhere else. Pick one, use it everywhere.
- **Status labels mean the same thing everywhere:** "Active", "Inactive", "Alumni", "Pending" — same meaning in every module.
- **Loading states are uniform:** skeleton screens (not spinners) for list/table data, a subtle top progress bar for navigation transitions.
- Toast notifications follow a single pattern: icon + short action description + (optional) undo link for reversible actions.

### 4.8 Performance on real Nigerian infrastructure
- Assume intermittent connectivity and 3G as baseline.
- **Bundle size:** lazy-load all module code. The initial shell (auth + routing + navigation) must be under 150KB gzipped.
- **Images:** never serve a full-resolution photo where a thumbnail suffices. Student photos compressed and resized at upload time.
- **Supabase queries indexed.** Every column used in `WHERE` on a frequently-queried table has an index. Flag any unindexed queries in code review.
- **Debounce search inputs.** Never fire a query on every keystroke.
- **Pagination or virtual scrolling** for any list that could exceed 50 items (student lists, score entry sheets, attendance registers for large classes).

### 4.9 Guardian and student portal — read-only, with context
What parents and students can see (from your decisions):
- Results (with grade, class position, component breakdown, teacher remarks if enabled)
- Attendance (percentage, count relative to total school days, visual calendar strip)
- Fee summary (what was billed, what was paid, balance, breakdown by fee head, payment history)
- Announcements (filtered to their audience)
- Session timeline, school calendar of activities
- Any additional items the admin enables per school

Every figure must have context. Provide comparisons, totals, and timelines, not isolated numbers. Make a parent feel informed, not confused.

### 4.10 Accessibility baseline
- Sufficient color contrast for outdoor sunlight reading (outdoor use is common in Nigerian school contexts). Minimum WCAG AA for all text.
- Text size respects device accessibility font-size settings (use `rem` units, never `px` for text).
- Interactive elements have visible focus states for keyboard/switch users.
- No information conveyed by color alone — always paired with text or icon.
- Motion reduced when the device has `prefers-reduced-motion` set.

### 4.11 Analytics and data visibility for admins
- The admin dashboard should surface actionable data, not just raw tables:
  - Attendance trends by class and by week
  - Fee collection progress (total billed vs. total received for the current term)
  - Score submission status (how many teachers have submitted vs. pending approval)
  - Leave requests pending review
  - Library books overdue
- These are not a separate "analytics module" — they are the default view of the admin dashboard, derived from existing data with no extra storage.
- Data visualizations should be simple, readable on a phone screen: bar charts for trends, progress rings for completion rates, simple tables for lists. Never complex interactive charts that don't work on a phone.

### 4.12 Data security as a felt experience
- Users should feel their data is protected, not just technically have it be so.
- Session timeouts with a clear "Your session has expired, log in again" message — not a silent failure.
- Role changes take effect immediately — if an admin removes a permission from a teacher, that teacher's next action using that permission should fail gracefully with a clear message.
- Audit log accessible to admins in the settings area — "View recent activity" — so admins can see who changed what. Not hidden.
- Password regeneration for staff is deliberately tucked away (one level deep in the individual staff member's settings), not on the main staff list. This is intentional friction to prevent accidental resets.

## 5. Native app strategy (future surface — design for it now)

A native mobile app (iOS + Android) is planned for the future. The web app is being built first, but every frontend decision must account for this future port. The cost of changing your mind here is high; the cost of designing for it from the start is low.

### 5.1 What this means in practice

**State management:** use **Zustand** (or similar platform-agnostic store). Never rely on URL-based state (`window.location`) for business logic — URLs don't exist in native apps. Route state goes through the router; application state goes through the store.

**Business logic out of UI components:** every data-fetching function, every transformation, every mutation should live in a service or store layer — not inside a React component. A component should only call a function and render what it gets back. This makes the logic portable to React Native without rewriting it.

**No browser-only APIs in shared logic:** `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, `window`, `document`, `navigator` — never in a function that does business work. Use an abstraction layer (`storage.get(key)`, `platform.openURL(url)`) so the native app can swap implementations. The offline queue especially must be backend-agnostic.

**Design tokens for everything:** all colors, spacing, border-radius, type sizes, shadows — defined once as design tokens. The web app uses CSS custom properties; the native app will use the same values in StyleSheet. This is the primary way to maintain visual consistency across platforms.

**Component structure:** organize components so that a "dumb" display component (no Supabase imports, no routing imports) is separate from a "smart" container (fetches data, calls mutations). Display components are directly portable to React Native.

**Supabase client:** the `@supabase/supabase-js` SDK is supported in React Native. The same Supabase functions work. No re-architecture needed for the backend connection.

### 5.2 What to NOT worry about now
- Don't write React Native code yet.
- Don't add a build step for multiple targets yet.
- Don't prematurely abstract everything — just apply the principles above as you build the web app.

### 5.3 Tech decisions that support the native future
| Decision | Reason |
|---|---|
| Zustand for state | Works identically in React Native |
| Supabase SDK | Same SDK for web and native |
| No CSS-in-JS (use Tailwind/tokens) | Tailwind has a React Native equivalent (NativeWind); tokens are framework-agnostic |
| Business logic in service files | Portable without rewriting |
| `@supabase/supabase-js` offline queue | Same pattern works in React Native with AsyncStorage |

## 6. Market and pricing context

### Competitors — Islamic/Quran schools
| Competitor | Known for | Gap |
|---|---|---|
| Ilmify | Hifz/Nazira tracking, 5-language support | No Nigerian/West African focus |
| Maktab | Word-level Hifz mistake tracking | No Hausa, no Paystack |
| MadrasaSIMS | Hifdh tracking, parent app | Unclear Nigeria presence |
| SchoolCues | Budget-friendly US maktabs | USD pricing, not ₦ |
| Dugsi | AutoPAY tuition deduction | Not Nigerian market |

**Uncontested gap:** no competitor offers deep Nigerian payment rails (Paystack/Flutterwave) + Hausa localization + offline-first for the Islamic school segment.

### Competitors — General Nigerian schools
- **Excel Mind:** dominant player, offline-first, WAEC/NECO/GCE-aligned, Paystack/Flutterwave, ~₦150,000–800,000/year
- Long tail of unverified smaller players

All confirmed competitors run shared multi-tenant SaaS — validates this architecture.

### Pricing tiers (validate directly with real schools before finalizing)
| Tier | Students | Suggested monthly price |
|---|---|---|
| Small | ≤ 50 | ₦8,000–12,000 |
| Medium | 51–150 | ₦15,000–25,000 |
| Large | 151–300+ | ₦30,000–50,000 |

**Infrastructure cost:** ~$25–35/month flat regardless of school count (Supabase Pro + Netlify free tier + Cloudflare R2 near-zero + domain ~$10–15/year). Healthy margin even at Small tier with one paying school.

## 7. Complete schema (61 tables across 7 modules, live; +12 proposed in §7.27 for higher-institution support, not yet migrated as of 2026-07-13)

### Conventions that apply to every table (no exceptions)
| Convention | Rule |
|---|---|
| Primary key | `id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid()` |
| School scoping | School-scoped tables: `school_id uuid not null references schools(id)`. Platform-scoped tables omit it (flagged explicitly). |
| Timestamps | `created_at timestamptz not null default now()` and `updated_at timestamptz not null default now()` on every table. `updated_at` maintained by shared `set_updated_at()` trigger. |
| Authorship | `created_by uuid references auth.users(id)` and `updated_by uuid references auth.users(id)` on every editable table. |
| Money | `numeric(14,2)`, never `float`. Always accompanied by `currency text not null default 'NGN'`. |
| Soft deletes | No hard deletes for people or financial records. Use `status` text columns with check constraints. |
| Arrays | Only for small, order-sensitive config lists (e.g. enabled languages). Anything needing its own RLS or referential integrity = junction table. |
| JSONB | Only for genuinely schema-less config. Never as a substitute for a foreign key relationship. |

### RLS shorthand
- **`[STD]`** — `for all using (school_id = current_school_id())` — the default
- **`[STD + role-gated]`** — school isolation + specific permission check (spelled out per table)
- **`[PLATFORM]`** — no `school_id` filter; `is_platform_admin()` for writes
- **`[SELF]`** — person reads/writes only rows resolving to their own `app_identities`

### Shared SQL infrastructure (run first, before any table creation)

```sql
-- Keeps updated_at current on every table
create or replace function set_updated_at()
returns trigger language plpgsql as $$
begin
  new.updated_at = now();
  return new;
end;
$$;

-- RLS helpers
create or replace function current_school_id()
returns uuid language sql security definer stable as $$
  select school_id from app_identities where auth_user_id = auth.uid()
$$;

create or replace function current_actor_type()
returns text language sql security definer stable as $$
  select actor_type from app_identities where auth_user_id = auth.uid()
$$;

create or replace function is_platform_admin()
returns boolean language sql security definer stable as $$
  select exists(select 1 from platform_admins where auth_user_id = auth.uid())
$$;

-- Audit trigger function (attach to sensitive tables individually)
create or replace function audit_row_change()
returns trigger language plpgsql as $$
begin
  insert into audit_log(school_id, actor_id, actor_type, table_name, record_id, action, old_data, new_data)
  values (
    coalesce(new.school_id, old.school_id),
    auth.uid(),
    current_actor_type(),
    TG_TABLE_NAME,
    coalesce(new.id, old.id),
    TG_OP,
    case when TG_OP in ('UPDATE','DELETE') then to_jsonb(old) else null end,
    case when TG_OP in ('UPDATE','INSERT') then to_jsonb(new) else null end
  );
  return coalesce(new, old);
end;
$$;
```

### 7.1 Schools & platform identity

```sql
create table schools (
  id                  uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  name                text not null,           -- never translated, never transliterated
  slug                text not null unique,    -- subdomain key: {slug}.platformdomain.com
  school_type         text,                    -- advisory label only for most purposes; ONE exception per §3.16's 2026-07-13 amendment — read once to select secondary vs. higher-institution academic engine (§7.27)
  logo_url            text,
  theme_color         text,
  default_lang        text not null default 'en' check (default_lang in ('en','ar','ha')),
  enabled_langs       text[] not null default array['en'],
  uses_terms          boolean not null default true,
  uses_ledger         boolean not null default false,
  status              text not null default 'trial'
                      check (status in ('trial','active','suspended','archived')),
  onboarding_complete boolean not null default false,
  created_at          timestamptz not null default now(),
  updated_at          timestamptz not null default now()
);
```
- **RLS:** `[STD]` (`school members read own school`), plus a second permissive policy — `"public can read school routing info"`, `for select to anon, authenticated using (true)` — added 2026-06-24 after Phase 1's documented "public view" carve-out turned out to have never been implemented. No column restriction: nothing in this table is sensitive, and the row-level policy is OR'd with `[STD]` rather than replacing it. This is what the pre-login homepage and the subdomain → school lookup in `App.tsx` actually read from; `App.tsx` needs `id` and `onboarding_complete` from this query too, not just `(name, slug, logo_url, theme_color, status)` as originally noted here. **2026-06-30 addition (PRD Session 5):** until this date, `schools` had no UPDATE policy for school-level admins at all — only platform-admin `ALL` and the two `SELECT` policies above — meaning no school admin could ever successfully write to their own `schools` row (this was the actual root cause of the onboarding-loop-on-reload bug; see §11). Added `create policy "school admins manage own school" on schools for update using (id = current_school_id()) with check (id = current_school_id());` — matches the naming/shape convention already used by every sibling table (`class_nodes`, `roles`, `sessions`, `staff_roles`, `subjects`, `role_permissions`, `school_public_config`).
- **Theme-color mechanism — read before PRD Tier 6 / Session 23:** `theme_color` is applied live via `document.documentElement.style.setProperty('--color-brand-600', ...)`, called both at `App.tsx` boot and on Settings save (confirmed working — see §11 2026-06-30 entry, and the Settings tab description in §13). **However**, a full grep confirmed `--color-brand-*`/`--color-neutral-*` are never actually declared as static custom properties anywhere in `index.css`'s `:root` block — every existing `var(--color-brand-*, #fallback)` reference across all ten module CSS blocks currently resolves off its hardcoded fallback value, not a real token, except where the JS-injected inline override happens to already be present on `documentElement` (see §11, Session 7b CSS entry). This means the token system is currently real only at runtime, not in the stylesheet itself. PRD Tier 6 Session 23 (token-architecture port) must resolve this explicitly rather than build on top of it silently: either (a) keep the JS-injection pattern but extend it to compute and inject the *entire* derived shade scale (not just `-600`) on boot/save, or (b) add real static `:root` fallback declarations for the full scale and have JS override only the brand-derived ones. Record the choice in §12 before Session 23 writes any CSS.
- `school_type` is advisory only, with one narrow, recorded exception — see §3.16's 2026-07-13 amendment and §7.27.

```sql
create table school_public_config (
  school_id         uuid primary key references schools(id),
  welcome_message   text,
  contact_info      jsonb,   -- {phone, email, address, social_links}
  show_announcements boolean not null default true,
  custom_fields     jsonb,
  welcome_post      jsonb,   -- {heading, blocks: WelcomePostBlock[]} — added 2026-07-11, PRD Session 34
  updated_at        timestamptz not null default now()
);
```
- **RLS:** Public read by `school_id` (no auth); write restricted to that school's admin role.
- **`welcome_post` (added 2026-07-11, PRD Session 34):** Upgrades the plain-text `welcome_message` above into a real structured post — `{heading: string, blocks: WelcomePostBlock[]}`, where each block is either `{type:'text', level:'p'|'h2'|'h3'|'h4', runs:[{text,bold?,italic?}]}` or `{type:'image', url, caption?}` (H1 deliberately excluded from the level union — reserved for the post's own heading/school name). Additive column: `welcome_message` is left completely untouched, still readable, and used as a fallback (`welcome_post → welcome_message → generic default`) by `publicHomepageService.ts` for any school that saved a plain message before this shipped. `normalizeBlock()`/`normalizeBlocks()` (in both `settingsService.ts` and `publicHomepageService.ts`, mirrored independently per this app's own convention, not shared) upgrade any older `{type:'paragraph', text}` block shape on read.

```sql
create table school_homepage_posts (
  id                uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  school_id         uuid not null references schools(id),
  heading           text not null,
  blocks            jsonb not null default '[]'::jsonb,  -- same WelcomePostBlock[] shape as welcome_post above
  always_expanded   boolean not null default false,
  sort_order         integer not null default 0,
  created_at        timestamptz not null default now(),
  updated_at        timestamptz not null default now()
);
```
- **Added 2026-07-11 (PRD Session 34), owner follow-up to `welcome_post` above.** A genuine one-to-many relationship (per-post `always_expanded` toggle, per-post ordering, future per-post publish/unpublish) that a singleton-per-school config row can't represent cleanly — deliberately a separate table, not a jsonb array bolted onto `school_public_config`. `always_expanded` (default `false`, i.e. collapsed-at-length) is the one durable, admin-controlled property; which post is currently expanded on a given visitor's page load is client-side UI state only, never written here. **RLS:** same shape as every other public-facing table in this PRD's Tier 7 additions — public read (`for select to public using (true)`), school-admin write scoped to `school_id = current_school_id()` via `current_is_admin()`, platform-admin full access. `set_updated_at()` trigger attached, matching every other table's convention. **Not migrated from `welcome_post`** — starts as an empty list per school; the singleton post stays exactly where it is, dormant if unused, same "start fresh, old data stays put" approach as `welcome_message → welcome_post` itself.

**Storage buckets (added 2026-07-11, PRD Session 34):**
- `school-homepage-images` — public bucket for images embedded in `welcome_post`/`school_homepage_posts` blocks. Path: `{school_id}/{timestamp}-{random}.jpg` (client-side resized to 1600px max dimension, JPEG). RLS: public read; school-admin write scoped to their own folder (`current_is_admin()` + `(storage.foldername(name))[1] = current_school_id()::text`); platform-admin full access.
- `school-logos` — separate public bucket for `schools.logo_url` uploads (kept distinct from the bucket above since a logo is school-identity content read by five separate consumers — see `SettingsModule.tsx`'s manifest row — not ad-hoc homepage-post content). Path: `{school_id}/logo-{timestamp}.png` (client-side resized to 512px max dimension, PNG to preserve transparency, `upsert:true`). Same RLS shape as `school-homepage-images`.
- Both buckets deliberately public, not the private+signed-URL pattern `student-photos` uses — these images render on the anonymous, no-auth public homepage and login page; a signed-URL round trip would cost an extra request on that high-traffic surface and can expire with no session available to refresh it. No confidentiality reason exists for content the school wants public, so this is a request-count/correctness choice, not a security tradeoff.

```sql
create table platform_admins (
  id            uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  auth_user_id  uuid not null unique references auth.users(id),
  full_name     text not null,
  created_at    timestamptz not null default now()
);
```
- **RLS:** `[PLATFORM]`. Bootstrap first row manually.

### 7.2 Unified identity and authentication

```sql
create table app_identities (
  id              uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  auth_user_id    uuid not null unique references auth.users(id),
  school_id       uuid not null references schools(id),
  actor_type      text not null check (actor_type in ('staff','guardian','student')),
  actor_record_id uuid not null,  -- points at staff.id, guardians.id, or students.id
  login_method    text not null check (login_method in ('email_password','phone_otp','login_code')),
  login_code      text,           -- only when login_method = 'login_code'
  phone           text,           -- only when login_method = 'phone_otp'
  is_active       boolean not null default true,
  created_at      timestamptz not null default now(),
  updated_at      timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (school_id, login_code)
);
```
- **RLS:** `[SELF]` for own row read; writes by school admin or Edge Functions (service role).
- `actor_record_id` is a deliberate loose UUID (one of two FK exceptions). A check trigger enforces correctness.
- Login-code issuance: `login-with-code` Edge Function — creates `auth.users` row via Auth Admin API (service role, server-side only).

### 7.3 Roles and permissions (fully custom per school)

```sql
create table roles (
  id            uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  school_id     uuid not null references schools(id),
  name          text not null,
  is_admin_role boolean not null default false,
  created_at    timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (school_id, name)
);

-- Platform-defined fixed catalog. Schools combine these into roles.
create table permissions (
  key         text primary key,   -- e.g. 'attendance.mark', 'fees.waive', 'results.approve'
  description text not null,
  module      text not null       -- 'academics','finance','hr','library','admin'
);

create table role_permissions (
  role_id        uuid not null references roles(id),
  permission_key text not null references permissions(key),
  primary key (role_id, permission_key)
);

create table staff_roles (
  staff_id   uuid not null references staff(id),
  role_id    uuid not null references roles(id),
  school_id  uuid not null references schools(id),
  primary key (staff_id, role_id)
);

-- Added 2026-07-01, PRD Tier 3 / Problem 3.1 / Session 8. Class-scoped permissions,
-- two layers, staff-level override always wins when present:
--
-- 1. role_permission_class_scope — role-level DEFAULT scope for a granted key.
--    Absence of any row for a given (role_id, permission_key) = unscoped/school-wide.
--    Only consulted when no staff-level override exists for that staff+key.
create table role_permission_class_scope (
  role_id        uuid not null,
  permission_key text not null,
  class_id       uuid not null references class_nodes(id),
  primary key (role_id, permission_key, class_id),
  foreign key (role_id, permission_key) references role_permissions(role_id, permission_key)
);

-- 2. staff_permission_class_scope — per-staff INDEPENDENT grant. If any row exists
--    for a given (staff_id, permission_key), that staff member holds the key
--    regardless of whether any of their roles grant it via role_permissions —
--    this table can grant a key the role doesn't have, by design (2026-07-01
--    owner decision). A row with class_id = NULL means "unrestricted" for that
--    key; one or more rows with real class_id values means "restricted to
--    exactly these classes." Presence of ANY row for a staff+key fully replaces
--    the role-level scope for that person — the two layers never merge/union.
--    NOTE: class_id can be NULL (the "unrestricted" marker), so it cannot be
--    part of a composite primary key (Postgres disallows NULL in PK columns) —
--    uses a surrogate id plus two constraints instead: a real-unique index over
--    non-null class_id rows, and a partial unique index enforcing at most one
--    NULL/"unrestricted" row per staff+key.
create table staff_permission_class_scope (
  id             uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  staff_id       uuid not null references staff(id),
  permission_key text not null references permissions(key),
  class_id       uuid references class_nodes(id),  -- NULL row = unrestricted grant
  school_id      uuid not null references schools(id)
);
create unique index staff_perm_scope_class_uniq
  on staff_permission_class_scope (staff_id, permission_key, class_id)
  where class_id is not null;
create unique index staff_perm_scope_unrestricted_uniq
  on staff_permission_class_scope (staff_id, permission_key)
  where class_id is null;
```
- **RLS:** `[STD]` on `roles`, `role_permissions`, `staff_roles`. `permissions` is `[PLATFORM]` read-only for all. **Corrected 2026-06-24:** the printed schema above was missing `school_id` on `staff_roles` — confirmed live in the database via `information_schema.columns` (`staff_id`, `role_id`, `school_id`, all `not null`). The `[STD]` policy noted here requires this column to exist at all, so it was correctly added when RLS was implemented; only this document had fallen out of sync. `role_permissions` does **not** have a `school_id` column (confirmed separately — its `[STD]`-style scoping is presumably enforced via a join to `roles` instead); don't assume the same drift applies there without checking first.
- Effective permissions (base, pre-class-scoping) = union across all roles a staff member holds.
- **RLS (class-scope tables):** `[STD]` on `role_permission_class_scope` (scope via join to `roles`, same pattern as `role_permissions`) and on `staff_permission_class_scope` (has its own `school_id`, scope directly).
- **Resolution order (`permissionsService.ts`, Session 8), staff-first:**
  1. Does `staff_permission_class_scope` have any row for this staff+key? → key is **granted**, scope = that row set (or unrestricted if a `class_id IS NULL` row is present). **Role is irrelevant once this fires — stop here.**
  2. No staff-level row → does any of the staff's roles grant this key via `role_permissions`? → key is granted, scope = `role_permission_class_scope` for that `(role_id, permission_key)` (or unrestricted if no scope row exists).
  3. Neither → key is not granted.
- Effective permissions (final) = union across all roles a staff member holds, exactly as before **plus** any staff-level override grants layered on top per the resolution order above.
- **Confirmed live 2026-07-07 (PRD Session 20 follow-on):** `role_permission_class_scope` and `staff_permission_class_scope` were designed here and referenced by code since Session 8, but a live check (`information_schema.tables`) during Session 20's storage-bucket work found neither table actually existed in the DB — only `roles`/`permissions`/`role_permissions`/`staff_roles` did. A retroactive migration (schema copied verbatim from above, RLS matching `roles`/`staff_roles`'s existing `[STD]`-style permissiveness) was run and confirmed. Both tables, their RLS, and their policies are now genuinely live, not documentation-only. Both are currently empty (no grants issued yet) — expected, not an error.

### 7.4 Academic calendar

```sql
create table sessions (
  id          uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  school_id   uuid not null references schools(id),
  name        text not null,
  start_date  date not null,
  end_date    date not null,
  is_current  boolean not null default false,
  created_at  timestamptz not null default now()
);

create table terms (
  id          uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  session_id  uuid not null references sessions(id),
  school_id   uuid not null references schools(id),
  name        text not null,
  sequence    int not null,
  start_date  date not null,
  end_date    date not null,
  created_at  timestamptz not null default now()
);
```
- **RLS:** `[STD]` on both.
- When `schools.uses_terms = false`: no `terms` rows are created. Every module treats `term_id` as nullable, falling back to `session_id`.
- **Resolved (2026-07-04, folded into Session 18 ahead of schedule — see §12 and §11):** the owner asked for a visible term-progress display whose end date auto-adjusts as school-day holidays (`school_calendar_days`, built this session) are inserted into or removed from a term's date range. **No `end_date_base`/`end_date_effective` column pair was added** to `terms` or `sessions` — per the confirmed decision, the effective end date is computed live via `getEffectiveTermEndDate()` in `attendanceService.ts`, never stored, keeping insert/delete symmetric for free. **Refinement over the original PRD Problem 6.7 spec, owner-directed:** extension is a *per-calendar-entry* choice (`school_calendar_days.extends_term`, boolean, default false), not a rule that uniformly applies to every school-day holiday — a single stray public holiday can be left non-extending while a planned multi-week break can be marked to extend. Session 29 (Tier 6, the visual `TermProgressCard`) can now build directly on this working computation rather than resolving the mechanism itself.
- **Amendment, SESSION 69, 2026-07-19:** two nullable columns added, `registration_opens_at timestamptz`/`registration_closes_at timestamptz` (`session69_registration_window_migration.sql`) — a real schema gap found while designing `course_registrations`' new student self-write RLS policy (§7.27.2's amendment): the policy needed to scope "which offerings a student may register into" to a real, enforceable fact, and no "open for registration" concept existed anywhere. Researched real registrar/SIS practice before proposing a shape (a per-term add/drop window is the near-universal real convention, not a per-offering flag an admin would have to toggle individually for every course). Both columns nullable, unset meaning unenforced — a school not yet using registration windows sees no behavior change.

### 7.6 Subjects, electives, and streams

```sql
create table subjects (

  school_id   uuid not null references schools(id),
  name        text not null,
  code        text,             -- optional WAEC code etc.
  created_at  timestamptz not null default now(),

-- Baseline: everyone in the class_node inherits this list
create table class_subjects (

  subject_id    uuid not null references subjects(id),
  school_id     uuid not null references schools(id),
  is_compulsory boolean not null default true,

-- Override 1: specific student's subject list differs from class default
create table student_subject_overrides (
```

### 7.7 Staff

```sql
create table staff (
  id          uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  school_id   uuid not null references schools(id),
  full_name   text not null,
  email       text,
  phone       text,
  status      text not null default 'active'
              check (status in ('active','inactive','suspended')),
  hire_date   date,
  default_password         text,          -- Session 10b — nullable, plaintext,
                                           -- written once by create-staff-account
                                           -- and overwritten by regenerate-staff-password.
                                           -- Never written or read by app-layer
                                           -- code directly against `staff` — see
                                           -- staff_default_password_view below.
  default_password_set_at  timestamptz,   -- Session 10b — paired with the above.
  created_at  timestamptz not null default now(),
  updated_at  timestamptz not null default now()
);
```
- **RLS:** `[STD]` (unchanged — school-boundary only, same permissive policy as every other staff column; `default_password`/`default_password_set_at` are **not** additionally restricted at the `staff` table's own RLS layer).
- Roles: via `staff_roles`. Teaching assignments: via `teaching_assignments` (§7.11).

**`staff_default_password_view` (Session 10b, admin-only read path):**
```sql
create view staff_default_password_view
with (security_invoker = false) as   -- runs as view owner, NOT the caller —
                                      -- deliberate, see note below
select id as staff_id, school_id, default_password, default_password_set_at
from staff
where current_is_admin();
```
- `security_invoker = false` is deliberate, not the default left untouched: `security_invoker = true` was tried first mid-session and correctly rejected (see §11 progress log, Session 10b entry) — `staff`'s own `[STD]` policy is permissive (any staff member can read any staff row), so an invoker-true view would have inherited that permissiveness and leaked every staff member's password to every other staff member. Admin-only gating is baked into the view's own `WHERE current_is_admin()` clause instead, independent of the caller's RLS on `staff`.
- `current_is_admin()` — new `security definer stable` helper (Session 10b), same naming/shape convention as `current_school_id()`/`current_actor_type()` (§3.2). Resolves whether the calling `auth.uid()` currently holds an admin role for their school, via `staff_roles` → `roles.is_admin_role`.
- This is the only exposure path for these two columns from the client SDK. A non-admin caller querying the view gets **zero rows**, not an RLS error — `hrService.ts`'s `loadStaffDefaultPassword()` treats that as `{ ok: true, data: null }`, not a failure.
- The two Edge Functions that write these columns (`create-staff-account`, `regenerate-staff-password`) use the service-role key, which bypasses RLS/the view entirely — the view is a read-side-only mechanism.
- **Known, named gap (not fixed, not silent):** the raw value still physically sits in `staff.default_password` until next overwritten — this view/RLS setup restricts *visibility*, not *storage*. Low-stakes per the Session 10b decision record (§12), not treated as a blocking security hole.

### 7.14 Scoring and grading

```sql
create table score_components (
  id          uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  school_id   uuid not null references schools(id),
  name        text not null,
  weight_pct  numeric(5,2) not null check (weight_pct >= 0 and weight_pct <= 100),
  sort_order  int not null,
  created_at  timestamptz not null default now()
  -- Application enforces: sum(weight_pct) per school = 100
);

create table grade_scales (
  id          uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  school_id   uuid not null references schools(id),
  min_score   numeric(5,2) not null,
  max_score   numeric(5,2) not null,
  grade_label text not null,
  remark      text,
  sort_order  int not null
);

create table scores (
  id                 uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  school_id          uuid not null references schools(id),
  student_id         uuid not null references students(id),
  subject_id         uuid not null references subjects(id),
  term_id            uuid references terms(id),
  session_id         uuid not null references sessions(id),
  score_component_id uuid not null references score_components(id),
  value              numeric(5,2) not null,
  entered_by         uuid not null references staff(id),
  approved_by        uuid references staff(id),
  approved_at        timestamptz,
  created_at         timestamptz not null default now(),
  updated_at         timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (school_id, student_id, subject_id, term_id, score_component_id)
);
```
- **RLS on `scores`:** `insert`/`update` only when a `teaching_assignments` row exists matching `staff_id = current_user`, `subject_id`, and the student's `class_node_id`. DB-level enforcement.
- Approval gate: `approved_by is null` = draft, invisible to guardians/students.
- Audit trigger attached.

```sql
-- Computed view — grade and position are never stored as columns
create view subject_results as
select
  s.student_id, s.subject_id, s.term_id, s.session_id, s.school_id,
  sum(s.value * sc.weight_pct / 100) as weighted_total,
  (select grade_label from grade_scales g
     where g.school_id = s.school_id
       and sum(s.value * sc.weight_pct / 100) between g.min_score and g.max_score
     limit 1) as grade_label,
  rank() over (
    partition by s.school_id, s.subject_id, s.term_id,
                 (select class_node_id from students st where st.id = s.student_id)
    order by sum(s.value * sc.weight_pct / 100) desc
  ) as position_in_class
from scores s
join score_components sc on sc.id = s.score_component_id
where s.approved_at is not null
group by s.student_id, s.subject_id, s.term_id, s.session_id, s.school_id;
```

### 7.14a Assessment Windows (Tier 8 / Problem 8.4 — Sessions 45–49; migrations s46/s48/s49 confirmed run live)

Net-new secondary-school assessment layer, designed with the owner 2026-07-12 (Problem 8.4's spec block) and built across Sessions 46–50. `score_components` is re-scoped from school-wide to **profile-scoped** (the table was confirmed empty platform-wide before altering, so nothing was lost); every grid/report number normalizes by each component's own `max_score`.

```sql
-- The shell: one round of assessment ("First Term 2026/2027").
create table assessment_windows (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  school_id uuid not null references schools(id),
  session_id uuid not null references sessions(id),
  term_id uuid references terms(id),          -- null = whole session (§3.6 duality)
  name text not null,
  scope text not null default 'whole_school' check (scope in ('whole_school','selected_classes')),
  status text not null default 'draft' check (status in ('draft','open','closed','finalized')),
  scores_open_at timestamptz, scores_submission_deadline timestamptz, scores_close_at timestamptz,
  created_by uuid references auth.users(id),
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(), updated_at timestamptz not null default now()
);

-- Per-window weighting formulas ("Primary weighting", "Secondary weighting").
create table score_component_profiles (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  assessment_window_id uuid not null references assessment_windows(id) on delete cascade,
  name text not null,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(), updated_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (assessment_window_id, name)
);

-- Which classes a window covers + per-class overrides.
create table assessment_window_classes (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  assessment_window_id uuid not null references assessment_windows(id) on delete cascade,
  class_node_id uuid not null references class_nodes(id),
  score_component_profile_id uuid not null references score_component_profiles(id),
  is_promotional boolean not null default true,
  sits_exam boolean not null default false,
  scores_open_at timestamptz, scores_submission_deadline timestamptz, scores_close_at timestamptz,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(), updated_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (assessment_window_id, class_node_id)
);
```

**`score_components` amendment (altered in place):** added `score_component_profile_id uuid NOT NULL references score_component_profiles(id)`, `max_score numeric(5,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 100`, and `updated_at` (the Phase-2 row lacked it against § conventions). RLS: reads `[STD]`; writes admin-or-`academics.assessment_windows.manage`. Known residual flagged in the migration header: Phase-2-era policies on this table were left untouched (permissive policies OR together; the trigger below is the operative gate) — owner follow-up to review `pg_policies` and drop stale write policies if any exist.

**`subject_results` recreated** with max_score normalization — weighted contribution is now `value * weight_pct / COALESCE(max_score, 100)` (identical numbers while max_score = 100, which is every row). Column set preserved exactly; all consumers verified against the seven documented columns.

**Scores gating trigger** `enforce_assessment_window_scores()` (BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE on `scores`, security definer): schools with ZERO windows keep legacy behavior; otherwise INSERT/value-changing UPDATE requires an OPEN window covering the student's class+session+term (whole_school scope covers everything; selected_classes requires an attach row); approval-only updates are permitted while open OR closed; draft/finalized reject all writes. Plain-English exception messages surface verbatim in the UI.


### 7.15a Scheme of work

**Added 2026-07-12, PRD Tier 8 / Problem 8.6 — net-new, owner request, grounded in research on Nigerian scheme-of-work norms and comparable SIS platforms (SchoolWorkSpace's SOW→coverage-tracking pattern) before proposing structure.** Numbered §7.15a (not §7.16) deliberately — §7.16 is already in live use throughout this document for Fees and payments; inserting here avoids a renumbering cascade across every existing §7.16 cross-reference in the file. Deliberately decoupled from §7.14's Assessment Window work (Problem 8.4): scheme of work governs *what gets taught, when* (content pacing); Assessment Windows govern *what gets scored, how weighted* (§7.14). No FK relationship between the two families — a school can have one without the other, and Session ordering (8.4 before 8.6) is a resourcing choice, not a technical dependency.

```sql
create table schemes_of_work (
  id                      uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  school_id               uuid not null references schools(id),
  teaching_assignment_id  uuid not null references teaching_assignments(id),
  session_id              uuid not null references sessions(id),
  term                    text,  -- nullable, per §3.6 optional-terms duality
  status                  text not null check (status in ('draft','submitted','approved','returned')) default 'draft',
  total_weeks             int not null,
  submitted_at            timestamptz,
  reviewed_by             uuid references staff(id),
  reviewed_at             timestamptz,
  review_note             text,  -- required by the UI when status is set to 'returned'
  created_at              timestamptz not null default now(),
  updated_at              timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (teaching_assignment_id, session_id, term)
);

create table scheme_of_work_weeks (
  id                    uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  scheme_of_work_id     uuid not null references schemes_of_work(id) on delete cascade,
  week_number           int not null,
  topic                 text not null,
  objectives            text,
  activities            text,
  resources             text,
  coverage_status       text not null check (coverage_status in ('planned','covered','partially_covered','not_covered')) default 'planned',
  coverage_note         text,
  coverage_marked_at    timestamptz,
  created_at            timestamptz not null default now(),
  updated_at            timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (scheme_of_work_id, week_number)
);
```

**Design decisions, flagged explicitly rather than silently defaulted:**
- **Anchored to `teaching_assignment_id`, not a raw `(staff_id, subject_id, class_node_id)` tuple** — reuses Problem 8.1's identity-resolution fix (`authStore.actorRecordId` → `teaching_assignments.staff_id`) with no new identity bug surface, and a scheme of work correctly follows a teaching assignment if it's reassigned mid-session.
- **`total_weeks` is teacher-set, not derived from `school_calendar_days`** (§ Tier 5.2) — surfaced as a suggestion in the UI ("your calendar has N teaching weeks this term"), not a hard constraint, since a teacher may deliberately plan a shorter/longer unit than the calendar's raw teaching-week count.
- **`status` lifecycle is `draft → submitted → approved`, with `returned` as the reject/revise-and-resubmit path** — not a terminal "rejected" state — matching the real submit→HOD-review→approve loop confirmed by research as standard Nigerian practice, not a one-shot gate.
- **Coverage tracking is per-week** (`coverage_status` on `scheme_of_work_weeks`, not a single blanket flag on the parent row) — this is what turns the scheme from a static submitted document into a live pacing signal admin/HOD can see across all teachers, matching the operational pattern researched in comparable platforms (create the SOW, break it into weeks, track coverage against it — not just archive it once approved).

**New permission keys (§7.3 catalog):** `academics.scheme_of_work.manage` (teacher: create/edit/submit own), `academics.scheme_of_work.approve` (HOD/admin: approve or return with note), `academics.scheme_of_work.view_all` (admin: read across all teachers, not just own assignments).

**RLS:** `[STD]` school-scoped read for all staff (so a covering teacher can see another's scheme, not just their own); insert/update restricted to the assignment's own `staff_id` unless the actor holds `academics.scheme_of_work.approve` (approval-only actors may update `status`/`reviewed_by`/`reviewed_at`/`review_note`, not the content columns).

### 7.16 Fees and payments

```sql
create table fee_heads (
  id              uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  school_id       uuid not null references schools(id),
  name            text not null,
  is_recurring    boolean not null default true,
  default_amount  numeric(14,2),
  currency        text not null default 'NGN',
  created_at      timestamptz not null default now()
);

create table fee_assignments (
  id                  uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  school_id           uuid not null references schools(id),
  fee_head_id         uuid not null references fee_heads(id),
  session_id          uuid not null references sessions(id),
  term_id             uuid references terms(id),
  target_type         text not null check (target_type in ('school_wide','class_node','student','programme_level')),
  class_node_id       uuid references class_nodes(id),
  student_id          uuid references students(id),
  programme_id        uuid references programmes(id),        -- added SESSION 70, higher-ed target_type='programme_level'
  programme_level_id  uuid references programme_levels(id),   -- added SESSION 70; travels with programme_id, matching course_offerings/programme_curriculum's own (programme_id, programme_level_id) pairing convention rather than the level FK alone
  amount              numeric(14,2) not null,
  due_date            date,
  created_at          timestamptz not null default now()
);
-- SESSION 70: one assignment row = one flat fee for everyone in that
-- programme/level for a given session/term — matches real Nigerian
-- university practice (flat per-session/semester, never per-course;
-- confirmed via research, see §12). Per-student variation (scholarships,
-- negotiated part-payments) is handled entirely through the existing
-- fee_discounts/installment_plans mechanism, not a per-row amount override.
-- Both new columns nullable, matching class_node_id/student_id's own
-- precedent — no DB-enforced cross-column check yet (app-layer only,
-- same as the existing target types); a trigger can be added later if
-- bad rows are ever found in practice.

create table fee_discounts (
  id                uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  school_id         uuid not null references schools(id),
  student_id        uuid not null references students(id),
  fee_assignment_id uuid references fee_assignments(id),
  discount_type     text not null check (discount_type in ('percentage','fixed_amount','full_waiver')),
  value             numeric(14,2),
  reason            text,
  approved_by       uuid not null references staff(id),
  created_at        timestamptz not null default now()
);

create table installment_plans (
  id                uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  school_id         uuid not null references schools(id),
  fee_assignment_id uuid not null references fee_assignments(id),
  student_id        uuid not null references students(id),
  created_at        timestamptz not null default now()
);

create table installment_schedule (
  id                  uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  installment_plan_id uuid not null references installment_plans(id),
  school_id           uuid not null references schools(id),
  amount              numeric(14,2) not null,
  due_date            date not null,
  status              text not null default 'pending'
                      check (status in ('pending','paid','overdue','waived'))
);

create table payment_methods_enabled (
  school_id  uuid not null references schools(id),
  method     text not null check (method in ('cash','bank_transfer','card','paystack','flutterwave','ussd','remita')),
  is_enabled boolean not null default false,
  config     jsonb,   -- SESSION 70: for method='remita', holds only { vault_secret_id, merchant_id } — the actual apiKey/apiToken/secret is never stored here in plaintext, only Vault's secret id. See the Vault decision below and §12.
  primary key (school_id, method)
);
-- SESSION 70 — per-school Remita credential storage, Supabase Vault:
-- each school owns its own Remita merchant account (owner decision, §12) —
-- money goes straight to the school's own account, the platform is never a
-- money-in-the-middle party. The school's real secret material
-- (apiKey/apiToken/merchant secret) is written once via vault.create_secret()
-- and only its returned uuid is stored in config.vault_secret_id above.
-- Ordinary staff/admin sessions (the 'authenticated' role) have
-- select revoked on vault.decrypted_secrets — only a narrow, service-role-
-- gated function (get_remita_credentials(school_id), security definer,
-- callable only by the Edge Function under the service-role key) can ever
-- read the decrypted value back. The admin-facing settings form is
-- write-only: an admin pastes the key in once, it is stored, and is never
-- redisplayed on reload — same "shown once" precedent as staff.default_password.
-- This does not defend against a compromised Edge Function itself (which
-- necessarily holds the plaintext at the moment it calls Remita, the same
-- trust boundary every payment integration has) — it defends against an
-- ordinarily-broad staff/admin read, an overly permissive RLS policy, or a
-- leaked read-only credential ever exposing the plaintext. See §12 for the
-- full tradeoff reasoning (Vault vs. envelope encryption vs. external KMS).

create table payments (
  id                      uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  school_id               uuid not null references schools(id),
  student_id              uuid not null references students(id),
  fee_assignment_id       uuid references fee_assignments(id),
  installment_schedule_id uuid references installment_schedule(id),
  amount                  numeric(14,2) not null,
  currency                text not null default 'NGN',
  method                  text not null,
  provider_reference      text,
  status                  text not null default 'completed'
                          check (status in ('pending','completed','failed','refunded')),
  received_by             uuid references staff(id),
  paid_at                 timestamptz,                   -- SESSION 70: made nullable, default now() dropped — a pending Remita RRR has no real payment timestamp until server-side verification succeeds; only set on genuine confirmation, never on insert
  notes                   text,                          -- added session 18: brief staff note on the payment
  created_at              timestamptz not null default now()
);
```
- **RLS:** `[STD + role-gated]` for staff write; guardians get `[SELF]` read. **SESSION 70 addition:** the Remita Edge Function inserts with `status: 'pending'`, `provider_reference: <RRR>`, `paid_at: null`; a separate verification step (webhook or manual "check status" re-trigger, since Remita's own status endpoint is polling-based) flips `status` to `'completed'`/`'failed'` and sets `paid_at` only on a genuine server-confirmed result — never trusts a client-side redirect. The school's Remita credentials used to call the initiate/verify endpoints are resolved via `get_remita_credentials(school_id)`, a Vault-backed, service-role-only function — see `payment_methods_enabled` above for the full storage design.
- Student fee balance = sum of resolved `fee_assignments` (net of `fee_discounts`) minus sum of `completed` payments. Computed as view, never stored.
- Audit trigger on `fee_discounts` and `payments`.

### 7.17 Double-entry ledger

Only active when `schools.uses_ledger = true`. Tables exist but stay empty for schools that don't use it.

```sql
create table chart_of_accounts (
  id                uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  school_id         uuid not null references schools(id),
  code              text not null,
  name              text not null,
  account_type      text not null check (account_type in ('asset','liability','equity','income','expense')),
  parent_account_id uuid references chart_of_accounts(id),
  is_active         boolean not null default true,
  created_at        timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (school_id, code)
);

create table journal_entries (
  id          uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  school_id   uuid not null references schools(id),
  entry_date  date not null,
  description text not null,
  source_type text,   -- 'payment','payroll_run','manual','fee_waiver'
  source_id   uuid,
  created_by  uuid references staff(id),
  created_at  timestamptz not null default now()
);

create table journal_lines (
  id               uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  journal_entry_id uuid not null references journal_entries(id),
  school_id        uuid not null references schools(id),
  account_id       uuid not null references chart_of_accounts(id),
  debit            numeric(14,2) not null default 0,
  credit           numeric(14,2) not null default 0,
  memo             text,
  check (debit = 0 or credit = 0),
  check (debit >= 0 and credit >= 0)
);
```
- **RLS:** `[STD]`, write restricted to `finance.ledger` permission.
- Balance trigger: `sum(debit) = sum(credit)` enforced on `journal_lines` per entry. Rejects unbalanced entries.
- Payment → ledger trigger fires on `payments.status = 'completed'` only when `uses_ledger = true`.
- Audit trigger on `journal_entries`.
