insert into students (id, school_id, full_name, student_code)
select (select val from _isotest_ids where key='student_b_id'),
       (select val from _isotest_ids where key='school_b'),
       'ISOTEST Student B', 'ISOB-001';

-- ── SECTION 4: link guardians to students ────────────────────
insert into student_guardians (student_id, guardian_id, school_id, has_platform_access)
select (select val from _isotest_ids where key='student_a_id'),
       (select val from _isotest_ids where key='guardian_a_id'),
       (select val from _isotest_ids where key='school_a'),
       true;

insert into student_guardians (student_id, guardian_id, school_id, has_platform_access)
select (select val from _isotest_ids where key='student_b_id'),
       (select val from _isotest_ids where key='guardian_b_id'),
       (select val from _isotest_ids where key='school_b'),
       true;

-- ── SECTION 5: create real auth.users rows first ─────────────
-- app_identities.auth_user_id has a real FK to auth.users, so we
-- can't use made-up UUIDs — Supabase Auth needs a real row there.
-- This inserts directly into auth.users (bypassing email/password
-- signup, since this is test-only data) with the SAME uuids we
-- already generated, so app_identities can reference them.
insert into auth.users (
  id, instance_id, aud, role, email,
  encrypted_password, email_confirmed_at,
  created_at, updated_at,
  raw_app_meta_data, raw_user_meta_data,
  is_super_admin, confirmation_token, recovery_token,
  email_change_token_new, email_change
)
select
  (select val from _isotest_ids where key='staff_a_auth'),
  '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000', 'authenticated', 'authenticated',
  'isotest-staff-a@example.invalid',
  crypt('isotest-password-not-real', gen_salt('bf')), now(),
  now(), now(),
  '{"provider":"email","providers":["email"]}', '{}',
  false, '', '', '', '';

insert into auth.users (
  id, instance_id, aud, role, email,
  encrypted_password, email_confirmed_at,
  created_at, updated_at,
  raw_app_meta_data, raw_user_meta_data,
  is_super_admin, confirmation_token, recovery_token,
  email_change_token_new, email_change
)
select
  (select val from _isotest_ids where key='staff_b_auth'),
  '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000', 'authenticated', 'authenticated',
  'isotest-staff-b@example.invalid',
  crypt('isotest-password-not-real', gen_salt('bf')), now(),
  now(), now(),
  '{"provider":"email","providers":["email"]}', '{}',
  false, '', '', '', '';

insert into auth.users (
  id, instance_id, aud, role, email,
  encrypted_password, email_confirmed_at,
  created_at, updated_at,
  raw_app_meta_data, raw_user_meta_data,
  is_super_admin, confirmation_token, recovery_token,
  email_change_token_new, email_change
)
select
  (select val from _isotest_ids where key='guardian_a_auth'),
  '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000', 'authenticated', 'authenticated',
  'isotest-guardian-a@example.invalid',
  crypt('isotest-password-not-real', gen_salt('bf')), now(),
  now(), now(),
  '{"provider":"email","providers":["email"]}', '{}',
  false, '', '', '', '';

-- ── SECTION 5b: app_identities — what current_school_id()/
--    current_actor_type() actually resolve against ───────────
insert into app_identities (id, school_id, actor_type, actor_record_id, auth_user_id, login_method)
select gen_random_uuid(),
       (select val from _isotest_ids where key='school_a'),
       'staff',
       (select val from _isotest_ids where key='staff_a_id'),
       (select val from _isotest_ids where key='staff_a_auth'),
       'email_password';

insert into app_identities (id, school_id, actor_type, actor_record_id, auth_user_id, login_method)
select gen_random_uuid(),
       (select val from _isotest_ids where key='school_b'),
       'staff',
       (select val from _isotest_ids where key='staff_b_id'),
       (select val from _isotest_ids where key='staff_b_auth'),
       'email_password';

insert into app_identities (id, school_id, actor_type, actor_record_id, auth_user_id, login_method)
select gen_random_uuid(),
       (select val from _isotest_ids where key='school_a'),
       'guardian',
       (select val from _isotest_ids where key='guardian_a_id'),
       (select val from _isotest_ids where key='guardian_a_auth'),

-- ── SECTION 6: one attendance record per school ──────────────

select gen_random_uuid(),
       (select val from _isotest_ids where key='school_a'),
       (select val from _isotest_ids where key='student_a_id'),

insert into attendance_records (id, school_id, student_id, date, status, marked_by)

-- STEP 2b: RUN AS SCHOOL A's STAFF MEMBER

<summary>Click to expand: <code>02c_test_as_guardian.sql</code></summary>

```sql
-- ============================================================
-- STEP 2c: RUN AS SCHOOL A's GUARDIAN
-- ============================================================
-- Run this AFTER 02b, as ONE single query execution (paste and
-- run the whole file at once — don't split into separate runs).
-- Guardians are a stricter actor type — should see even less
-- than staff. Also checks a guardian can't see OTHER families'
-- students within their OWN school.
-- ============================================================

-- Reset any leftover role from 02b first, in case this is the
-- same connection.
reset role;

select set_config(
  'request.jwt.claims',
  json_build_object('sub', (select val from _isotest_ids where key = 'guardian_a_auth')::text)::text,
  false
);

set role authenticated;

select 'students (cross-school, as guardian)' as check_name,
  (select count(*) from students where school_id = (select val from _isotest_ids where key='school_b')) as should_be_zero
union all
select 'attendance_records (cross-school, as guardian)',
  (select count(*) from attendance_records where school_id = (select val from _isotest_ids where key='school_b'))
union all
select 'payments (cross-school, as guardian)',
  (select count(*) from payments where school_id = (select val from _isotest_ids where key='school_b'))
union all
select 'scores (cross-school, as guardian)',
  (select count(*) from scores where school_id = (select val from _isotest_ids where key='school_b'))
union all
select 'students (OTHER family, SAME school A)',
  (select count(*) from students
   where school_id = (select val from _isotest_ids where key='school_a')
     and id != (select val from _isotest_ids where key='student_a_id'))
order by check_name;

reset role;

-- READ THIS: every "should_be_zero" value above MUST be 0.
-- The last row is the most important one to watch — it tests
-- that a guardian can't see a DIFFERENT family's child even
-- within their own school, which is a common, subtle mistake.
```

Fee-model foundation, Vault credential design, and two real wiring bugs closed this pass; the Remita Edge Function itself has not been built yet.)** Researched Remita's real integration shape before designing anything (RRR-based invoice flow, hash/OAuth auth generations, separate polling-based status-verification endpoint — full findings recorded in §12) and cross-checked against real Nigerian university fee-structure precedent (flat per-session/semester, never per-course) before locking the fee model. **Fee model, extending rather than paralleling the existing secondary-school schema:** `fee_assignments.target_type` gains `'programme_level'`, with `programme_id`+`programme_level_id` added together (confirmed via a live `information_schema.columns` read that `course_offerings`/`programme_curriculum` both already pair the two rather than using `programme_level_id` alone — matched that convention rather than guessing). Per-student variation handled entirely through existing `fee_discounts`/`installment_plans`, no new per-student override column. `payment_methods_enabled.method` gains `'remita'`; `payments.method` needed no migration (confirmed via `pg_constraint` that it has no check constraint at all, unlike the initial draft assumed). Migration recorded in §7.16, full SQL in `session70_migration.sql`. **Credential storage — Supabase Vault, reasoned through explicitly, not defaulted to the first idea:** compared Vault against application-level envelope encryption and an external KMS, on an honestly-stated threat model (nothing stops a compromised Edge Function either way, since it necessarily holds the plaintext to call Remita) — Vault chosen as the pragmatic no-custom-crypto option for this stack; `get_remita_credentials(school_id)`, a `security definer` function gated to the service role, is the only path to a decrypted secret; `select` revoked from `authenticated`/`anon` on `vault.decrypted_secrets` directly. Full reasoning and the payment-trigger research (student self-service only, matching every real institutional precedent found — OSU, Essex, Edinburgh, and vendor platforms) recorded in §12. **Two real wiring bugs found and fixed, the second more serious than the first:** (1) `App.tsx`'s `FinanceModule` call site was the one module missing `schoolType` (every sibling — `StudentsModule`/`ResultsModule`/`SettingsModule`/`CourseRegistrationModule` — already receives it), meaning `FinanceModule.tsx`'s own `isHigherEd` was always `false` regardless of any code changes — the direct cause of an earlier "npm built cleanly but the UI saw no changes" report. - **2026-07-15/16 (PRD Sessions 54–60c — Problem 8.7, Phase 4: GPA/CGPA computation, CA/exam component weighting, and per-course component overrides; reconstructed in full from pasted transcripts of prior unrecorded chats across three separate free-tier cutoffs, per the owner's explicit framing that each transcript is authoritative present context — ✅ Complete for Sessions 60/60a/60c as scoped; 60b (student transcript screen + PDF, plus an owner-directed publish-gate extension) now also ✅ Complete, closed 2026-07-16, see its own entry below)** — This entry closes a real, multi-session gap in this log: §13's file manifest already documented Sessions 54–60 in detail, but this narrative log itself had not been updated since Session 24/27 (2026-07-08) — all of Problem 8.7's actual build history existed only in the PRD until now, a housekeeping debt this entry resolves per §0 instruction 8.

  **Session 60 — GPA/CGPA computation core.** New `src/services/gpaService.ts` — deliberately pure computation with no Supabase calls and no knowledge of table shapes beyond a minimal `CourseAttempt` interface, so the GPA/CGPA math (§7.27.4) is unit-testable in isolation and has exactly one implementation to fix if the spec is revisited. Covers: grade-band lookup (`findGradeBand`/`scoreAttempt`, throws rather than silently defaulting to grade point 0 if a score matches no configured band); retake resolution for both `dilution` (every finalized attempt counts permanently) and `replacement` (only the most recent passing attempt per chain counts, chains grouped by walking `originalRegistrationId` back to root, ties broken by session order then input order); semester GPA grouped by `(sessionId, termId)` with `termId: null` correctly bucketing as one group for schools with `uses_terms = false`; and CGPA under both configured rollup methods (`weighted_all_attempts` vs `average_of_semester_gpas`, the latter excluding zero-unit semesters from the average rather than counting them as 0). `courseResultsService.ts` and `CourseResultsModule.tsx`/`ResultsModule.tsx` wired as callers — `ResultsModule.tsx`'s dispatcher correctly does not thread `schoolType` further down into `CourseResultsModule.tsx` since the higher-ed/secondary branch has already happened by that point (confirmed by design, not an oversight, when re-checked this session). `App.tsx`'s `schoolType` threading confirmed consistent across all three higher-ed modules. `SettingsModule.tsx`'s Grading tab gained grade-scale-band and CGPA-policy config, present and wired as documented. **Hand-verified this session, not merely code-reviewed:** a real score was finalized on-device end-to-end and the resulting `course_results`/`student_gpa_snapshots` rows were pulled directly via SQL — 37 quality points ÷ 8 units = 4.625, matching both the written semester-GPA row (`gpa: 4.625, cgpa: null`) and the running-CGPA row (`gpa: null, cgpa: 4.625`) from the same `computed_at` transaction. This was the one Definition-of-Done gate Session 60 itself had left unverified; it is now closed.

  **Session 60a — CA/exam component weighting.** Root cause of a live bug report (SESSION 60a's own admin UI and `CourseResultsModule.tsx`'s scoring grid disagreeing about which components exist for a course) traced to `score_components` (the secondary-school table) having no write path or admin UI anywhere in the codebase — confirmed by grep before designing anything, not assumed. New `course_result_components` table (`migration_session_60a.sql`, run and confirmed live): `name`, `weight_pct`, `sort_order`, school-scoped, admin-write-gated on the existing `academics.course_result_components.manage` permission key (no new key needed). New `course_result_component_scores` table, FK'd to `course_result_components(id)`. `courseResultsService.ts` gained CRUD for both tables plus `finalizeWeightedCourseResult()` — the real enforcement point for the "components must sum to 100%" rule, which is deliberately **not** a blocking client-side check (an admin can save "CA" alone at 10% while still building out the set); the finalize function is the only place that refuses to produce a grade against a set that doesn't sum to 100%, since a plain CHECK constraint can't express a by-name merge rule in SQL. `CourseResultsModule.tsx`'s scoring grid made additive/backward-compatible: schools with no configured components keep the original single-score-input path unchanged (a legitimate, common final-grade-only transcript format in its own right, not a placeholder state); schools with components get one input per component, a running weighted-total preview, and `finalizeWeightedCourseResult()` instead of the plain finalize path. `SettingsModule.tsx`'s Grading tab gained a matching "CA/exam components" admin section (list, add/edit/delete, non-blocking sum indicator), placed after the existing CGPA policy section per the file's established `FieldRow`/`Input`/`Skeleton`/`ErrorState`/set-sheet conventions. **Verification:** `esbuild` parse-clean and a real `tsc --strict --noUnusedLocals --noUnusedParameters` typecheck run against the actual sibling files (not hand-rolled stubs, after those proved too fragile to chain correctly across query shapes) — caught and fixed one genuine `TS6133` unused-import error before it shipped.

  **Session 60c — per-course component overrides, plus two real bugs found post-ship.** Scope: let a course override the school-wide CA/exam weight set, or add a course-specific component (e.g. "Practical") with no school-wide counterpart, merged by name.

  *Design correction mid-build (schema):* the first drafted migration created a separate `course_result_component_overrides` table, anchored to `courses(id)` (confirmed live via `settingsService.ts`'s existing `loadCourses()`, independently corroborating what had only been inferred from the FK). This table was actually applied live before a design bug was caught: `course_result_component_scores.course_result_component_id` references `course_result_components(id)` only — an override row in a second table has its own, disjoint id, which that FK cannot accept. Caught via reasoning about the scoring-write path before real data was ever written against it (confirmed: zero application code had shipped against the override table). **Corrected migration** (`migration_session_60c.sql`, superseding the first draft, run and confirmed live) folds the override concept into `course_result_components` itself via a nullable `course_id` column instead — `course_id IS NULL` = school-wide (Session 60a's original meaning, unchanged), `course_id IS NOT NULL` = course-specific override-or-addition for that course only. Every component now lives in one id-space, so `course_result_component_scores` needed no schema change at all. Two partial unique indexes replace a single plain `unique(school_id, course_id, name)`, which would have been wrong — Postgres treats `NULL` as distinct from `NULL` in a unique constraint and would have silently allowed duplicate school-wide rows of the same name. The now-abandoned `course_result_component_overrides` table was dropped in the same migration rather than left as an unused, live-RLS liability. No RLS policy changes were needed anywhere in this arc — existing `course_result_components` policies are scoped on `school_id` only, which is already correct whether `course_id` is null or set. `resolveCourseResultComponents()`/`mergeCourseResultComponents()` in `courseResultsService.ts` became the single by-name merge function, used by both the admin preview and the server-side finalize check, so the two can never disagree again.

  *Bug 1 (found on-device by the owner, real): school-wide components were not editable from the per-course override screen.* `mergeCourseResultComponents()`'s output rendered every component, school-wide and course-specific alike, but the Edit/Delete buttons were gated to `source === 'override'` only — a school-wide row rendered read-only, with no way to rebalance it to make room for a new course-specific component (e.g. adding "Practical" at 20% with no way to bring CA/Exam down from 40/60 to fit). Fixed by making both row types clickable from the same screen.

  *Bug 2 (found on-device by the owner, real, more serious): that same fix silently wrote to the real school-wide row from a per-course screen.* Concretely reported: school-wide CA/Exam at 40/60, adding a course override for "Lab" at 20% caused the school-wide set itself to become CA/40 Exam/40 — a global change made from what was ostensibly a single-course screen. Root cause confirmed by tracing the actual save/delete handlers, not assumed: `handleSaveOverride` wrote `courseId: null` (the real school-wide row) whenever the row being edited had `source === 'school'`, and `handleDeleteOverride` had the same flaw on the delete path — actually more dangerous, since it could delete the real school-wide component entirely from a per-course context. **Fix:** the per-course screen no longer ever writes to a school-wide row. "Editing" an inherited school-wide row from this screen now always creates/updates a course-specific row of the same name (`courseId: selectedCourseId`), which the existing by-name merge rule already shadows for that course only — exactly what an admin building a Lab/CA/Exam 20/40/40 set for one course actually wants, with the school-wide 40/60 untouched everywhere else. Delete is no longer offered on school-derived rows at all, since there is nothing course-specific to remove for a purely inherited value. Row labels changed from "Edit" to "Override for this course," and the dialog copy no longer claims (or risks) a global write. A genuine global edit to CA/Exam remains reachable only from the school-wide section higher up the same tab, unchanged.

  *Bug 3 (found via independent audit, not owner-reported — both `CourseResultsModule.tsx` and `CourseRegistrationModule.tsx` were shipping completely unstyled):* every prior "done" check on both files (parse-clean, typecheck-clean) had only ever verified TypeScript correctness — nothing had checked JSX classNames against `index.css`. A full bidirectional diff found `CourseResultsModule.tsx` using 28 distinct `crs-*` classes with zero defined anywhere, and `CourseRegistrationModule.tsx` using 27 `reg-*` classes, also zero defined — both had likely been rendering as unstyled HTML since they were first built. Fixed by adding both class families to `index.css`, modeled on already-shipped, working sibling patterns rather than invented from scratch: `.crs-*` mirrors `.res-*` (`ResultsModule.tsx`'s secondary-school grid — same shape: weighted-component table, score inputs, badges, finalize button, same `--color-primary`/`--color-text`/`--color-bg` token vocabulary), and `.reg-*` mirrors `.set-*`'s field-row/list-row/button primitives (closer match to registration's stacked-card/checkable-row shape than a table). Both confirmed 0 gaps in either direction after the fix. **Now re-verified on-device, 2026-07-15** — the owner confirmed both `CourseResultsModule.tsx` and `CourseRegistrationModule.tsx` render correctly styled at a real viewport; the static-analysis fix is fully closed, not just parse/typecheck-clean.

  **Session 60b — student transcript (screen + PDF), plus an owner-directed publish-gate extension beyond the original card. ✅ Complete, closed 2026-07-16.** Original scope per the PRD card: `loadStudentTranscript(studentId)` in `courseResultsService.ts` (every `course_registration` joined to `course_results`, grouped by session/term, plus cached semester GPAs and running CGPA from `student_gpa_snapshots` — read-only, no new computation); a student-facing transcript tab in `GuardianPortal.tsx`; an admin/registrar-facing equivalent (added to `StudentsModule.tsx`'s detail sheet as a new Transcript tab, higher-ed schools only); and a PDF export (`transcriptPdf.ts`, new `jspdf`/`jspdf-autotable` dependency, flagged rather than added silently — no existing PDF-generation library existed anywhere in the codebase, confirmed before adding one; renders directly to PDF bytes and triggers a real download, a deliberate departure from `printTimetable.ts`/`printStudentIdCards.ts`'s window-print-dialog pattern, per owner instruction).

  **Owner-directed extension, mid-session:** admin approval required before a finalized result reaches a guardian/student — not in the original 60b card, added on request once the transcript surfaced that no such gate existed. Root cause: `course_results` had no `published_by`/`published_at` concept at all (the file's own header comment already flagged this gap before this session); `loadStudentTranscript()` gated purely on `finalized_at`, so a lecturer finalizing a score made it instantly visible to guardians. Mirrored the already-working secondary-school precedent (`scores.approved_by`/`approved_at`, RLS-enforced, `academics.scores.approve`) rather than inventing a new pattern — used the already-catalogued-but-unused `academics.results.publish` permission key instead of colliding with the secondary-school key. Migration adds `published_by`/`published_at` to `course_results` and tightens the guardian/student RLS read policy to `published_at is not null`. `CourseResultsModule.tsx` gained per-row Publish/Unpublish (gated on `academics.results.publish`, kept deliberately separate from Finalize/Update rather than collapsed into one key, preserving the scorer/reviewer separation-of-duties the whole feature exists for) plus a bulk "publish all finalized" action. `StudentsModule.tsx`'s admin transcript tab shows drafts and published results together, explicitly marked, per the owner's "admin sees everything, drafts clearly marked" decision.

  **Real bugs found on-device by the owner and fixed, not caught by static analysis alone:**
  1. *Unpublishing/updating a result did not actually hide it from guardians.* Two compounding causes: (a) `student_gpa_snapshots` — the cached CGPA/semester-GPA table guardians read — was written by `recomputeAndCacheGpa()` keyed only on `finalized_at`, never `published_at`, and was never recomputed on publish/unpublish at all, only on finalize; (b) separately, `loadStudentTranscript()`'s own per-course query (feeding the letter grade/GP the guardian sees) *also* still filtered on `finalized_at` only — fixing the cached-snapshot path alone left this second, independent query still leaking drafts. Fixed by filtering both on `published_at`, recomputing the snapshot on every publish/unpublish (not just finalize), and explicitly handling the zero-attempts edge case (unpublishing a student's only published result must still clear the stale cached snapshot, not silently leave it — the original early-return skipped the clearing write when the attempt count hit zero).
  2. *A genuine, pre-existing, unrelated RLS hole surfaced during the investigation:* `course_registrations`' own staff policy checked `school_id` match only, never actor type — meaning a guardian's own `app_identities` row (which also carries a `school_id`) satisfied it, granting guardians unrestricted read/write on every registration in the school, one join upstream of `course_results`' own (correct) publish gate. Narrowed to a real staff-only check; added a properly scoped guardian read-only policy that hadn't existed before.
  3. *Publish/Unpublish required two clicks to take effect.* Root cause: the toggle handler read `published_at` off a row object captured in the render closure, one render behind the actual state on a fast double-tap. Fixed by re-reading the row fresh from live state by id at call time, not from the closure argument.
  4. *Once the guardian leak was closed, admin's own CGPA/GPA display broke instead* (reported as "CGPA and GPA blocked to admin view"). Root cause: `student_gpa_snapshots` is a single cache with only one variant — the guardian-safe, published-only rollup — so there was no draft-inclusive number for admin's `includeUnpublished=true` read path to fall back to. Fixed by having `loadStudentTranscript()` compute CGPA/semester-GPA **live**, on demand, straight from `gpaService.ts`'s real functions when `includeUnpublished` is true, rather than reading the guardian-only cache — nothing written or cached, admin's own view only.
  5. *Brand-color inconsistency, flagged by the owner alongside the above:* several pre-existing `.crs-*` rules (`Finalize` button, score-input focus ring, term-tab active state, offering-dropdown focus ring) were still hardcoded to the static `--color-primary` token rather than the per-school `--color-brand-600` token the new Publish buttons already used — fixed to the same `var(--color-brand-600, var(--color-primary))` fallback pattern app-wide across the module, not just the new buttons.

  **A real, twice-recurring `tsc -b` build failure, the last thing closed this session — flagged in detail since it was reported fixed twice before it actually was:** `loadStudentTranscript()`'s conditional query (drafts included vs. published-only, by `includeUnpublished`) first tried a mutable `let` reassignment (`courseRegsQuery = courseRegsQuery.not(...)`), which hit `TS2589` ("Type instantiation is excessively deep and possibly infinite") against the real project's strict `tsconfig` — a failure mode an isolated stub-based typecheck never reproduced, since the stub's looser Supabase typings didn't hit the same generic recursion depth. The first attempted fix (branching the `.not(...)` call inside a single ternary) was reported clean but was not actually re-verified against a real compiler — and the real `npm run build` caught the same `TS2589` again, unchanged in substance, just relocated to the ternary. Root cause: a ternary still forces TypeScript to unify both branches' independently-inferred `PostgrestFilterBuilder` generic chains into one result type, the same unification cost a `let` reassignment has. **Real fix:** each branch is now fully awaited inside its own `if`/`else`, assigned into one plainly-typed local afterward — nothing is ever unified across the two branches' query-builder types, only their already-resolved, simple result values. Verified this time against the real `@supabase/supabase-js` package (installed directly, not a hand-written stub) and the real `gpaService.ts`, isolated and as a full-file check — zero errors. **Owner subsequently confirmed both `npm run build` and full on-device testing clean**, covering the complete arc: guardian transcript view, admin `StudentsModule` transcript view with drafts marked, publish/unpublish toggling correctly on both sides, and PDF export.

Grounded both open UX questions in a real web search before building rather than asserting from memory: heading level is block-level and bold/italic are inline "marks" within a block (standard rich-text-JSON convention — matches WordPress's block model, Contentstack's `{text, marks}` shape), and a per-block toolbar (heading dropdown + separate B/I toggle buttons) is the standard pattern; adapted for this app's plain-textarea editor (no cursor-selection engine) as one run per block rather than true mid-sentence marks. `WelcomePostBlock`'s `{type:'paragraph', text}` shape extended to `{type:'text', level:'p'|'h2'|'h3'|'h4', runs:[{text,bold?,italic?}]}` (H1 deliberately excluded — reserved for the post's own heading/school name, matching standard heading-hierarchy guidance against duplicate H1s) plus `{type:'image', url, caption?}`, mirrored identically in both `settingsService.ts` and `publicHomepageService.ts` (their own established convention: independent mirrored types, not a shared import), with a `normalizeBlock()`/`normalizeBlocks()` migration shim so any post saved before this change still reads correctly. **Real bug found while wiring this, not something the owner had to report:** `SettingsModule.tsx`'s uploaded copy referenced a `HomepageTab` component that was never defined (`ReferenceError` on Settings open) and still had the pre-rich-text block editor — both fixed before any new feature work, since building on top of a broken file would have compounded rather than fixed the actual defect. Each text block gained a heading-level dropdown (Normal/H2/H3/H4) and Bold/Italic toggle buttons. Brand-color sweep across the public page: section-heading accent bars, brand-tinted left borders on post cards/contact/announcements sections, brand-colored contact labels, and a brand-colored ring around the header logo — deliberately accents-only, no background-color fills, per the owner's confirmed scope choice.

  **Part A — After-hours edit-window lock (attendanceService.ts, AttendanceModule.tsx):** Root cause of a reported retap bug traced to a stray `set_updated_at` trigger with no matching column (`migration_session_31_attendance_updated_at.sql`, run by the owner) — fixed at the schema level, separately from this feature. New `loadParentClassGroups()` added to both `attendanceService.ts` and `studentsService.ts` (`{ id, name, leafIds: string[] }[]`), read-modeled on `loadAllLeafClasses`'s own query shape. UX interaction model decided via explicit owner sign-off on two design questions before building (documented at the time): two-tier pills (parent row narrows a class row) over a native `<select>`/`<optgroup>` hybrid — reusing `StudentsModule.tsx`'s own already-shipped Session 12 pill pattern rather than inventing a second one — and a combined register (all leaf classes under a selected parent, one query, one list) grouped by arm with sub-headings, rather than either a fully flat merge (loses per-arm scannability at scale) or a fully separate per-arm view (extra taps for the common case). `loadStudentsForClass()`/`loadAttendanceRecords()`/`loadAttendanceHistory()` widened from `classNodeId: string` to `string | string[]` (`.in()` for arrays, `.eq()` for a single id) — every existing single-id call site unaffected. **Real write-path correctness issue found and fixed before it could ship silently wrong:** `handleStatusTap`/`handleBatchMark`/the history-strip loader initially still keyed writes off `selectedClass.id`, which is correct for a single-class register but wrong for a combined one (every student would have saved under the *parent's* id, not their own leaf class) — caught during design review, fixed to use `student.class_node_id` throughout (already present on the `Student`/loaded-row type, no new query needed). Single-class selection behavior is provably unaffected, since `student.class_node_id === selectedClass.id` in that case.

  **Part C — Phone space economy: collapse-on-select + search-within-register (AttendanceModule.tsx, StudentsModule.tsx, index.css):** Owner-reported: two pill rows plus a parent row consumed too much vertical space on phone before any student was visible, and there was no fast way to jump to one student in a large combined register. Fix: once a class/group/whole-school selection is made, both pill tiers collapse into a single compact summary bar (`{label} · Change ▾`), reopening on tap; defaults to expanded only on first load (nothing chosen yet). A genuine tri-state bug was found and fixed in `StudentsModule.tsx` specifically: `hasSelection` was originally derived from `filterClass !== '' || selectedGroup !== null`, which is indistinguishable from "All classes" (`filterClass === ''`) — the summary bar never collapsed for that explicit choice. Fixed with an explicit `hasChosen` boolean, set by every pill handler including the "All classes"/whole-school pills, distinct from the initial not-yet-picked state. Search-within-register: `AttendanceModule.tsx` gained a new search box (StudentsModule already had one from an earlier session) filtering the already-loaded student list client-side, no extra network round-trip per keystroke; works correctly against both the flat single-class view and the arm-grouped combined view (a matched student's arm heading still renders, empty arms don't); auto-clears on class/group change. Search icon and collapse chevron use the real `Icon` component (confirmed inventory-safe names, `search`/`chevron-down`) from the start in `StudentsModule.tsx`; `AttendanceModule.tsx`'s own first pass used plain unicode glyphs (icon module wasn't in context at that point) and was corrected to the real `Icon` component once availability was confirmed, per explicit owner instruction ("we don't use emojis anymore").

  **Part F — App-wide brand-token correctness sweep (index.css only, two passes):** Owner named this "item 2" from earlier in the session, initially mis-triaged as a reference to Tier 6's already-closed theming rows (23–30) before the owner clarified the actual ask: `AttendanceModule`/`StudentsModule` CSS had never been swept into the live `--color-brand-*` scale `applyBrandTheme()` maintains — both files were still reading the fixed, never-updated `--color-primary` (`#2563eb`), so every school looked identically blue in these two modules regardless of their real brand color. **First pass:** 171 sites converted (101 `att-*`, 70 `stu-*`) across `background`/`color`/`border-color`/`outline`/`border`/`border-bottom-color`/`text-decoration-color`, each given a `var(--color-brand-X, var(--color-primary...))` fallback chain matching the app's own established defensive pattern. A real contrast bug — the same class Session 24 already found and fixed for `.btn--primary`/the timetable day-header — was found and fixed at 6 sites (`.att-pill--active`, `.stu-add-btn`, `.stu-pill--active` ×2, `.stu-empty-action`, `.stu-save-btn`): solid `--color-brand-600` fills paired with hardcoded `color: #fff`, fixed to `var(--color-brand-on, #fff)`. **Second pass (owner follow-up, reporting the parent pills specifically still hardcoded blue):** confirmed the miss — `.att-pill--parent.att-pill--active` had been *added* by Part E's own later edit, after the first brand sweep had already run, so it was never caught; fixed the same way (`--color-brand-600`/`--color-brand-on`).

  **Part G — Sparkline overflow fix (index.css only):** Owner-reported: the whole-school attendance analytics bar chart extends beyond the screen on some views. Root cause: `.att-sparkline` had no `width`/`max-width`/`overflow` constraint at all, and `.att-sparkline-bar` used `flex: 1` with a `min-width: 3px` floor that flexbox will not shrink below regardless of container width — fine for a day/week view (a handful of bars), but `attendanceService.ts`'s own `dailyPresentTrend` can produce 100+ points for a `session`-scope trend, especially once combined with Part D's whole-school view. Fixed per researched best practice for many-bar CSS-only bar charts (web search performed, several independent sources converged on the same pattern): constrain the container (`width: 100%; max-width: 100%; min-width: 0` — the `min-width: 0` matters, since a flex child can otherwise refuse to shrink below its content width even with `max-width` set), lower the bar's floor (`min-width: 2px`, `flex: 1 1 0`), and add `overflow-x: auto` strictly as a last resort once even the compressed floor can't fit. Short ranges render identically to before; long ranges compress first, and only scroll horizontally within the card if genuinely necessary — never push past the screen edge.

  **Part H — Dark-mode brand-color perceptual correction (themeService.ts only):** Owner-reported: some admin-picked brand colors "look terrible" in dark mode. Researched before writing any code (web search, multiple independent 2025/2026 dark-mode-design and accessibility sources, converging on the same explanation): `deriveBrandScale()`'s existing dark-mode path only ever corrected *contrast* against the dark surface — pushing a color toward black/white via `darkenToContrast()` until a WCAG number cleared — but never touched *saturation*. Every source named the same failure mode this produces: human color perception is not symmetric between light and dark grounds, so a saturated hue that reads as calm on white can appear to "vibrate" or glow against near-black at the exact same saturation, independent of whether it also happens to pass a contrast check. Fix: added `desaturateForDarkSurface()` (new pure function, HSL-space — RGB-space `mix()` cannot do a hue-preserving saturation reduction directly) applying a ~30% relative saturation cut and a lightness floor (0.6) to the dark-mode working base, hue always preserved for brand recognition; wired into `deriveBrandScale()` to run *before* the existing contrast guard, so WCAG safety is still the final word, now just checked against a calmer starting color rather than bypassed. `raw` (the true, unmodified admin pick, used for swatches) is deliberately left untouched — only the dark-mode working-base derivation path is affected, and only when `surfaceHex` is dark; light mode is completely unaffected. **Verified numerically, not just argued:** the exact algorithm was reproduced in an isolated Python script and run against 6 real problem colors (vivid red/green/blue/orange, hot pink, pale gold) — every case showed a genuine ~25-35% relative saturation reduction (matching the researched 10-40% band) with contrast against the dark surface *improving*, not merely staying passing, in every single case. `wasAdjustedForContrast`'s own doc comment was corrected in the same pass to clarify it remains a contrast-only signal and does not itself flag whether the new desaturation step ran (a separate, always-applied dark-mode step, not a fallback path).

  **Bug found and fixed, `announcementsService.ts` — root cause of the owner-reported on-device defect "the class selector in the announcement creation isn't presenting any class":** traced via the owner running a direct SQL query at request (not guessed) — `loadClassNodes()` selected and ordered by a `level` column that does not exist on `class_nodes` at all. Confirmed via `information_schema.columns`: the real column set is `id, school_id, parent_id, name, node_type, sort_order, is_leaf_enrollable, created_at, updated_at` — no numeric depth column of any kind. Every call to `loadClassNodes()` had therefore always failed at the database with a hard Postgres `42703` error, silently caught into the function's own `Result`-error branch — not an RLS issue, not an empty-data issue, an actually-invalid query that (per this file's own manifest entry) had never been on-device tested before this session. **Fix:** rebuilt `loadClassNodes()` around the real schema — fetches `id, name, parent_id, sort_order` flat, groups rows by `parent_id` (sibling groups, since `sort_order` is only meaningful within a group, never as a flat cross-tree order), sorts each group by `sort_order`, then walks the tree from roots (`parent_id === null`) downward, computing a client-side `depth` for indentation as it goes.   **Two bugs found and fixed this session, after the initial build, both from a follow-up screenshot the owner supplied:** (1) three JSX text nodes in `LivePeriodWidget.tsx` were using literal `\uXXXX` escape sequences (em dash, middle dot) typed directly into bare JSX text instead of inside an actual JS string literal — JSX does not interpret `\uXXXX` outside of real JS strings, so the sequences rendered as visible backslash-u codes exactly as the screenshot showed; fixed by substituting the real unicode characters. (2) the expanded panel could open with content taller than the remaining viewport and no way to reach the rest — root cause was two-layered: no scroll cue existed on expand at all, and once one was added, the browser's native `scrollIntoView` slid the widget's top underneath the app's `position: sticky` header (`.app-header`, min-height 56px), clipping the banner and first grid row — a second owner-supplied screenshot ("last item isn't visible") turned out to be this same sticky-header clipping at the *top*, not a scroll-distance problem at the bottom as first assumed. Fixed with a `rootRef` + effect calling `scrollIntoView({ behavior: 'smooth', block: 'start' })` on expand, `scroll-margin-top: 64px` on `.lpw-root` so the browser stops short of the sticky header instead of tucking the widget behind it, and `max-height: min(60vh, 420px)` / `overflow-y: auto` plus bottom padding and `scroll-padding-block` on `.lpw-expanded` so very short viewports get a working internal scroll with real breathing room at the last row instead of a flush, clipped-looking cutoff.

  **Migration (`add_student_photo_url.sql`):** single nullable `photo_url text` column on `students`, `add column if not exists` — safe to re-run, matches `add_student_code.sql`'s exact pattern per this session's own instruction to follow it. §7.8 updated with the new column and its Storage path-convention note before any further work, per §0's standing instruction 7.

  **Storage bucket (`student_photos_bucket_setup.sql`) — one real gap found before writing this, not glossed over:** the instruction says gate writes on `students.records.edit` (a real, confirmed key from Session 8's catalog audit — not invented), but Storage RLS runs at the Postgres layer against `storage.objects`, which has no access to `permissionsService.ts`'s client-side `can()`/`canForClass()` resolution at all. Checked `pg_proc` directly before assuming otherwise: no SQL-side permission-check helper existed — only `current_school_id()`, `current_actor_type()`, `current_is_admin()`, `is_platform_admin()`. Writing a policy that silently fell back to `current_is_admin()` alone would have been wrong (grants to every admin regardless of the specific key, not what §12's 2026-07-01 decision specifies) and writing one that called a non-existent function would have failed at policy-creation time. **Resolved by building a real new SQL function, `current_has_permission(perm_key)`** (`security definer stable`, following the exact convention of every other RLS helper in §3.2), mirroring §7.3's actual documented resolution order — staff-level override in `staff_permission_class_scope` checked first (any row for the key grants it, independent of role), then role-level grant via `staff_roles`/`role_permissions` (explicitly excluded when a staff-level row exists for that specific key, so the two layers don't wrongly stack), with `current_is_admin()` bypass first per Session 9's admin-bypass decision (§12) — not a class-scoped check, since a photo-upload gate has no meaningful per-class restriction unlike `academics.attendance.mark`.

- **2026-07-01 (PRD Session 8 follow-up — join bug fixed, build confirmed clean, class-scope admin UI flagged as a real gap)** — Closes the "Not yet done" item left open by the 2026-07-01 Session 8 entry below. **Bug found before any live test:** `permissionsService.ts`'s role-grant query attempted `supabase.from('staff_roles').select('role_permissions!inner(permission_key, role_id)')` — an embed with no direct FK path, since `staff_roles` and `role_permissions` each independently reference `roles.id` rather than referencing each other (per §7.3). PostgREST cannot auto-embed across an indirect relationship, so this would have failed at the DB layer with a relationship-not-found error on every call. Because the function fails safe on query error, the practical effect would have been silent: **every staff member would resolve to zero role-derived permissions**, with only per-staff overrides (rare) still working — an availability bug, not a security one, but one that would only have surfaced once Session 9 wired a real UI gate to `can()`, not at `npm run build`. **Fix:** replaced the embed with two direct queries — `staff_roles` filtered by `staff_id` to get held `role_id`s, then `role_permissions` filtered `.in('role_id', heldRoleIds)` — mirroring the pattern already used two lines later for `role_permission_class_scope`. No change to the staff-first resolution order or the union-across-roles logic; both were already correct against the locked §7.3/§12 design. **Separately, three unrelated `npm run build` errors surfaced on first real build attempt, all outside Session 8's files:** (1) `App.tsx`'s `GuardianModule` call was missing `authUserId`, the one call site among several siblings (Library, HR, Timetable) that dropped it — traced, then resolved the other way: `GuardianModule.tsx` never actually reads `authUserId` anywhere in its body (confirmed by grep), and the master plan's own `GuardianModule.tsx` §13 row already documented this as pre-existing dead plumbing predating this session. Removed from `Props`, the doc comment, and the destructuring rather than threading a value nothing consumes — owner decision, not a guess. (2)/(3) `GuardianModule.tsx`'s two `useRef<ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>>()` calls (search debounce, link-search debounce) failed under the project's current `@types/react`, which dropped the no-argument `useRef` overload — fixed by adding an explicit `| undefined` union and `undefined` initial value to both. `npm run build` confirmed clean by owner after all four fixes. **Flagging a real gap, not yet built in any session:** Settings → Roles (`SettingsModule.tsx`) only manages whether a role holds a permission key at all — there is no admin UI anywhere in the app for the two new class-scope tables Session 8 introduced (`role_permission_class_scope`, `staff_permission_class_scope`). Today, setting a class restriction on a permission is only possible via direct SQL. `canForClass()` is therefore untestable through the app itself until this UI exists; it isn't scoped into any session in §10 yet and should be added as a new session before Tier 3 is called fully done. **Tested as:** build-only (`npm run build`) — no live Supabase round-trip of the fixed join has been confirmed yet; recommended before treating the join fix itself as proven, independent of Session 9's own on-device test. §13 manifest: `permissionsService.ts` row — note the join-shape fix. `authStore.ts` row — unchanged, no further edits this pass. `App.tsx` row — thirteenth update: `authUserId` removed from the `GuardianModule` call site. `GuardianModule.tsx` row — `authUserId` removed from `Props` (dead, unused); two `useRef` calls fixed for current `@types/react`.

  **Class-scoped permissions architecture, resolved with the owner (recorded in §7.3 and §12):** general mechanism, not a `students.records.edit`-only special case — two new tables, `role_permission_class_scope` (role-level default scope) and `staff_permission_class_scope` (per-staff independent override). Owner explicitly decided the staff-level override **can grant a key the staff member's role does not hold at all** — it is an independent grant path, not merely a scope-narrower layered on top of an existing role grant. Resolution order: staff override first (stops there if any row exists for that staff+key) → role grant + role-level scope → not granted. A `class_id IS NULL` row in either table means unrestricted. One schema bug caught and fixed before finalizing: `class_id` cannot be part of a primary key if it needs to be nullable (Postgres disallows NULL in PK columns) — `staff_permission_class_scope` uses a surrogate `id` plus two partial unique indexes instead (one for non-null class rows, one enforcing at most one "unrestricted" row per staff+key). **Files delivered:** `src/services/permissionsService.ts` (new — `loadEffectivePermissions`, `loadEffectivePermissionScopes`, `can`, `canForClass`, implementing the staff-first resolution order, fails safe to "not granted" on any query error at each layer independently) and `src/stores/authStore.ts` (extended — added `permissionScopes: PermissionScopeMap` state, resolved in `resolveIdentity` alongside `isAdminRole` for staff actors only, exposed `can()`/`canForClass()` as store methods; `platform_admin` and non-staff actors get an empty permission map, matching the existing pattern where `isAdminRole` is also always `false` for those actor types). **Not yet done:** import path (`../services/permissionsService`) and the `staff_roles → role_permissions!inner` join shape were written against the PRD's documented file layout and the existing `resolveAdminRole` join's pattern respectively — neither has been confirmed against the real project structure or a real `tsc`/`npm run build` pass yet. **No UI change this session — that is Session 9.** §13 manifest: add `permissionsService.ts` row (new); update `authStore.ts` row to note the Session 8 extension.

- **2026-06-30 (PRD Session 5 follow-up — `create-staff-account` Edge Function: two bugs found, one a crash, one a live authorization gap)** — While re-verifying Step 1's `saveSchoolIdentity` write following the Session 5 RLS fix (below), Step 8's "Add staff member" was also tested and found broken: every attempt failed with the generic "Could not create staff account" message. Edge Function logs showed a consistent rejection: `PGRST116 — Results contain 13 rows, application/vnd.pgrst.object+json requires 1 row`. Root cause: `supabase/functions/create-staff-account/index.ts` queried `app_identities` with no filter at all (`.select("school_id, actor_type").maybeSingle()`), relying on `.maybeSingle()` to coincidentally return exactly one row. RLS scopes `app_identities` reads to everyone in the caller's school, not just the caller's own row — any school with more than one identity row (i.e. any real school past initial setup) caused this to throw and reject every caller unconditionally. This matches the prior "claimed-done-but-not-deployed" risk flagged for this same function on 2026-06-25 — this time it was deployed, just broken. **A second, more serious bug of the identical class was found in the same pass:** the immediately following admin-role check (`callerClient.from("staff_roles").select("roles(is_admin_role)")`) also had no filter — it checked "does ANY staff member at this school hold an admin role" rather than "does THIS caller hold one." This meant any non-admin teacher could have successfully created new staff accounts at any school with at least one admin (i.e. every real school) — a live authorization gap, not just a crash, that had not yet been triggered or noticed. **Fix:** added `callerClient.auth.getUser()` to explicitly resolve and validate the caller's own auth user id (the function previously never verified the token resolved to a real user before querying tables with it), then filtered both queries correctly — `app_identities` by `auth_user_id`, `staff_roles` by the caller's own `staff_id` (resolved via `app_identities.actor_record_id`). Redeployed; re-tested on-device — staff account created successfully, temp password shown in UI, confirmed by owner. **Tested as: admin.** §13 Edge Functions manifest: update `create-staff-account` row to "fixed 2026-06-30: unfiltered caller-identity queries (crash + auth gap); redeployed; confirmed on-device."

- **2026-06-30 (PRD Session 5 — onboarding-loop-on-reload bug; root cause was RLS, not application code)** — Diagnosed and fixed per PRD Tier 2 / Problem 2.1. **Initial hypothesis (application-layer discarded-result bug) was real but not sufficient on its own:** `OnboardingWizard.tsx`'s original `handleFinish` discarded `completeOnboarding()`'s return value and called `onComplete()` unconditionally regardless of success — fixed first (result now checked; `onComplete()` only fires on confirmed success; error surfaced with retry; `App.tsx`'s `onComplete` now re-fetches the school row from the DB instead of optimistically patching local state). **However, on-device testing after this fix still showed the loop**, with no error message and no network request on click initially appearing — traced via console + network tab + direct SQL Editor query (`select onboarding_complete from schools where id = ...` → `false`, even after a "successful" Finish). Confirmed via a direct SQL Editor `update schools set onboarding_complete = true ...` that the write succeeds when RLS is bypassed — meaning RLS itself was the actual blocker. Pulled `pg_policies` for `schools` and confirmed: only two `SELECT` policies existed (`public can read school routing info`, `school members read own school`) plus the platform-admin `ALL` policy — **no school-admin UPDATE policy existed at all**, unlike every sibling table (`class_nodes`, `roles`, `sessions`, `staff_roles`, `subjects`, `role_permissions`, `school_public_config` all correctly have a `school admins manage ...` policy scoped to `current_school_id()`). Because Postgres RLS silently returns zero-rows-affected with `error: null` (not a thrown error) when no policy permits a write, `completeOnboarding()` always reported `{ok:true}` even though nothing was written — explaining why the bug was invisible until reload. **Fix (the actual root cause):** `create policy "school admins manage own school" on schools for update using (id = current_school_id()) with check (id = current_school_id());` — matches the naming/shape convention of every sibling table's working policy. **On-device Done Check observed:** admin completes wizard, finishes cleanly, reload lands on `home` → `AdminDashboard` reliably across multiple reloads. Teacher identity (Session 3's seeded account) also completes/reloads cleanly, landing on the Tier-4-pending placeholder, which is correct/expected (`TeacherDashboard.tsx` is Session 14 scope). **Same-day follow-up:** re-verified Step 1 (`saveSchoolIdentity`) now writes `theme_color` successfully under the new policy — confirmed via SQL. **Tested as: admin, teacher.** §13 manifest: update `OnboardingWizard.tsx` row — "Finish/completeOnboarding: confirmed on-device, root cause was missing RLS policy on `schools`, not application code." Flag for future session: every sibling table's working RLS policy checks only `school_id = current_school_id()`, not an admin-role check — meaning any staff member, not just admins, currently has RLS-level write access to these tables. Per §3.2, RLS is meant to be the school-boundary backstop with Tier 3's permission system as the actual fine-grained gate — so this is expected by current design, not a new gap, but noted here per the verification rule rather than silently assumed safe.

- **2026-06-25 (Phase 6 — tsc build errors fixed; all Phase 6 files committed to git, commit c981f59)** — Session covered two things: diagnosing a failed Netlify deploy, and fixing all TypeScript errors that caused it.
  **Background:** `npm run dev` (Vite) skips `tsc -b` entirely and never surfaces type errors. `npm run build` (what Netlify runs) runs `tsc -b && vite build` in strict mode. Every error below was invisible locally and only appeared on the first push.
  **10 tsc errors fixed across 3 files:**
  - `src/App.tsx` — (1) `NavTab` type didn't include `'home'`: fixed by re-importing `NavTab` from `BottomNav` as `BottomNavTab` and declaring `type NavTab = BottomNavTab | 'home'` locally. The `BottomNav` prop receives `activeTab as BottomNavTab` since `'home'` is never a rendered nav button. (2) `schoolId` destructured in `TabContent` props but never used: removed from the interface and call site. (3) `if (tab === 'home')` comparison error: downstream of fix (1), resolved automatically once `NavTab` included `'home'`.
  - `src/routes/AdminDashboard.tsx` — (4) `useAuthStore((s) => s.actor)` — `actor` doesn't exist on the store type: changed to `s.session` (session holds the logged-in user; name resolved from `session?.user?.user_metadata?.full_name`). (5–7) Three unused locals (`sessionPaymentsTotal`, `paymentRows`, `attendanceLabel`): removed; payments block rewritten as a clean single-query `paymentsTotal`. (8) `urgency` ternary inferred as `string` not `'normal' | 'warning' | 'urgent'`: the inner cast `as ActionItem['urgency']` was present but `.filter()` re-widened the type. Fix: wrapped the whole array literal in `as ActionItem[]` before `.filter()`, and added `as const` to the `'normal'` literal. (9–10) `paymentsRes`/`currentSessionRes` unused after rewrite: renamed to `_sessionRes`/`_placeholder` (underscore prefix suppresses `noUnusedLocals`).
  - `src/routes/OnboardingWizard.tsx` — (11) `ClassNodeInput` imported but never used: removed from the import list. (12) `JSX.Element[]` return type on `renderTree` — `Cannot find namespace 'JSX'`: added `React` as a default import; changed return type to `React.ReactElement[]`.
  **Build sequence:**
  - First attempt: pushed without running `npm run build` locally → Netlify caught all 10 errors. Fixed files delivered.
  - Second attempt: `npm run build` locally → still 1 error (`urgency` cast). The `.filter()` re-widening issue was not caught by the first fix. Applied the `as ActionItem[]` wrapper fix.
  - Third attempt: `npm run build` passed locally (0 errors). Pushed: `git push` → commit c981f59, 6 files changed (3 source files + 3 `.bak` backups created during the fix process).
  **Key lesson documented for future sessions:** `npm run build` must be run locally before every push. `npm run dev` will never catch `noUnusedLocals`, union type mismatches, or missing namespace errors. Add this as a pre-push habit. The `.bak` files (App.tsx.bak, AdminDashboard.tsx.bak, OnboardingWizard.tsx.bak) are now in git — harmless but can be `.gitignore`d or deleted in a cleanup commit later.
  **Status after this session:** all Phase 6 files (AdminDashboard.tsx, phase6-dashboard.css merged into index.css, updated App.tsx) are committed and live on `origin/main`. Netlify deploy triggered. §13 manifest updated — all three files show ☑ committed.

- **2026-06-25 (On-device test, part 5 — create-staff-account fixed and confirmed working; all 4 Edge Functions corrected for CORS)** — Session was unrecorded and reconstructed from pasted chat transcript. Three things resolved:
  **(1) `create-staff-account` confirmed working end-to-end.** After redeploying with the correct name, the function was still returning "Could not create staff account." Diagnosis via Supabase logs showed the function was receiving `OPTIONS` requests and rejecting them with 405 before any real logic ran — a CORS preflight issue. Fix: added `CORS_HEADERS` constant, `OPTIONS` early-return (204, headers only), and spread `...CORS_HEADERS` into every `jsonResponse` call. Secondary fix in the same deploy: the `staff_roles` insert inside the function was missing `school_id` in each row (matching the live schema drift documented in §11 2026-06-24 part 4 entry); would have caused a not-null constraint error on role assignment even if CORS had passed. **Confirmed working on-device: staff account created successfully.** §10 Phase 1 checkbox ticked.
  **(2) `login-with-code` had two bugs identified.** Bug 1: same CORS preflight issue as above — OPTIONS rejected before any logic. Bug 2 (more serious): the function was using `adminClient.auth.admin.generateLink` with a fake constructed email (`auth_user_id@login-code.internal`) — this almost certainly matches no real `auth.users` email and the approach is fundamentally wrong. **Corrected approach:** `adminClient.auth.admin.createSession({ user_id: identity.auth_user_id })` which directly mints a session for a known user ID with no email tricks. Corrected code delivered for redeploy. **Pending on-device test of guardian/student login tabs — §10 checkbox not yet ticked.**
  **(3) `release-student-transfer` and `import-student-transfer`** — both had the same CORS preflight issue. No other bugs found in either. Corrected code delivered for redeploy. These functions won't be exercised until Phase 6's student management module, so the critical one is `login-with-code` first.
  **CORS is now a documented universal requirement for all Edge Functions:** every Supabase Edge Function called from the browser must handle OPTIONS preflight. The pattern is: `CORS_HEADERS` constant at top → `if (req.method === "OPTIONS") return new Response(null, { status: 204, headers: CORS_HEADERS })` → `...CORS_HEADERS` in every response. Any future Edge Function that omits this will fail silently at the browser level.

Reviewed against the schema in §7 and against each other; this is genuinely Phase 5 work (auth routing for all three login methods, the full onboarding wizard, app shell with bottom nav) and was mostly correct, but six real bugs were found and fixed:
  1. **`App.tsx`** — header "Account" button called `useAuthStore.getState().clearSession().then ? ... : null`, which throws (`clearSession()` returns `void`; `.then` read off `undefined`) and even if it didn't, only cleared local Zustand state without calling `supabase.auth.signOut()` — meaning the real Supabase session would survive a reload. Fixed to route to the existing, correct `SignOutButton` in the More menu instead.
  2. **`App.tsx`** — `getSlugFromHostname()` misread a bare apex production domain (`eduportalng.com`, no subdomain) as a school slug, since it only excluded `www`/`localhost`, not the no-subdomain case. Would have broken the platform homepage in production. Fixed: now requires 3+ hostname labels (or a `.localhost` suffix) before treating the first label as a slug.
  3. **`App.tsx`** — leftover "EduCore NG" branding (file header comment + platform homepage title) from before the rename to Eduportal. Fixed.
  4. **`onboardingService.ts`** — `saveCalendar()` upserted to `sessions` with `onConflict: 'school_id,name'`, but `sessions` has no such constraint — only the partial unique index on `is_current` (one current session per school) that we actually created in Phase 1. Would have thrown a Postgres "no unique or exclusion constraint matching ON CONFLICT" error on first use. Fixed: now demotes any existing current session for the school, then looks up by name and updates or inserts — matching the real constraint and also handling an admin revisiting this step later via the "setup guide" (§4.6).
  5. **`authStore.ts`** — `initialize()` attached a new `onAuthStateChange` listener every call with no guard and no stored unsubscribe handle; under Vite HMR or React StrictMode this stacks duplicate listeners, causing `resolveIdentity` to fire multiple times per auth event. Fixed with an `_authListenerAttached` guard.
  6. **`LoginPage.tsx`** — guardian OTP input used `type="number"`, which silently ignores the `maxLength` attribute in every browser and permits `e`/`+`/`-`/decimal characters on some mobile keyboards. Fixed to `type="text"` + `inputMode="numeric"` + digits-only pattern, which is the correct cross-browser pattern for a numeric code field.
