## 12. Key Q&A decisions (verbatim — do not re-ask these)

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Grading systems? | All systems + custom per school |
| Finance depth? | Full fee collection + full double-entry ledger; admin decides whether to activate ledger |
| Class hierarchy depth? | Unlimited — schools build their own tree, any number of levels |
| Academic calendar? | Completely custom; term concept is optional (switchable per school) |
| Staff roles? | Fully custom — admin defines role names and permissions per school |
| Timetable views? | Both (class view + teacher view) derived from one source table |
| Student promotion? | Automatic by grade; admin can override. **Tier 8 refinement (s50, 2026-08-26):** auto = at/above the class rule's `min_average_pct`, computed server-side from approved `subject_results`; below-cutoff students always land in an explicit manual-review list (never silently retained); top-down sequencing gate enforced by `apply_secondary_promotions()`; graduation only via a deliberately-NULL destination rule. |
| Score entry permissions? | Only the teacher assigned to that specific subject+class can enter scores (DB-level). **Tier 8 addition (s46):** entry additionally requires an OPEN assessment window covering that class+session+term (`enforce_assessment_window_scores()` trigger; legacy-tolerant while a school has zero windows). **Hotfix (owner report, 2026-08-26, §12-locked): admins are unrestricted on `scores`** — additive permissive policy `scores_admin_full` (`current_is_admin() or is_platform_admin()`) ORs in alongside the legacy assignment-only policy, which stays untouched as the teacher-path gate. Rationale: the Phase-2 policy had no admin carve-out and admins hold no teaching assignments, so approval was DB-blocked for exactly the role expected to perform it; permissive policies OR-combine, so the additive grant needs no knowledge of the legacy policy's text. The window-lifecycle trigger still applies to admins (a finalized window stays locked even for them — reopening is a deliberate lifecycle action they control). |
| Assessment Window lifecycle (Tier 8 s46, decided during build per owner's delegated authority)? | `draft → open → closed → finalized`, advanced manually from Settings > Assessments. `status` is what gates score entry; the three timestamp columns are displayed context, not enforcement. Legacy tolerance: a school with zero windows ever keeps pre-window behavior until it creates its first one. Overlapping windows covering the same class+term are an admin misconfiguration; resolution picks newest-first client-side and is otherwise undefined server-side (flagged, not silently blessed). |
| Class-teacher remark placement (Problem 8.4 left open "at build time")? | Own table `assessment_window_student_remarks`, keyed unique(window, student), school_id retained for simple [STD] RLS. Written by admins or holders of `academics.remarks.manage`. No form-teacher concept exists in this schema yet — modeling one is separate future scope, not silently built here. |
| Report card format (Session 49)? | jsPDF real-download (transcriptPdf precedent, not print-dialog). WAEC-style: brand band, student block with position + attendance summary, subjects table with dynamic per-component columns ("1st CA (20)") + total + grade + subject position, overall-average box with aggregate remark band, class teacher's remark paragraph, signature lines. Every number read off `loadReportCardData()` — no recomputation in the PDF layer. |
| Exam timetable surface (Session 48)? | Read-only inside `TimetableModuleSecondary` as a current-week banner strip + tap-for-detail modal (Problem 8.4 required visibility inside the module itself); authoring lives Settings-side (Assessments > Exams & venues). Per-day-column grid annotation deferred — needs TimetableGrid prop/date-mapping changes, flagged not silently dropped. Clash checks run client-side at save (class/venue/invigilator overlap blocks save), matching Problem 8.4's "checked at save rather than hard schema constraints for v1". |
| Secondary grade bands vs higher-ed bands (Session 49)? | Same `grade_scales` table; secondary rows keep `grade_point`/`scale_max`/`is_passing` NULL. New secondary-safe write pair (`assessmentService.saveGradeBand`) writes ONLY the five secondary columns — never reuses `upsertHigherEdGradeBand`, whose payload would corrupt semantics of those columns on secondary rows. |

| Class-scoped permissions architecture (PRD Tier 3 / Session 8, decided 2026-07-01)? | General mechanism, not a `students.edit`-only special case. Two layers: `role_permission_class_scope` (role-level default class restriction for a granted key) and `staff_permission_class_scope` (per-staff independent override — **can grant a key the staff member's role doesn't hold at all**, by explicit owner decision). Staff-level override, if any row exists for that staff+key, fully replaces the role-level scope for that person (never merges/unions). A `class_id IS NULL` row in either table means "unrestricted." Resolution order: staff override first (stop if found) → role grant + role-level scope → not granted. |
| Attendance mark vs. edit — one permission key or two (PRD Tier 3 / Session 9, decided 2026-07-01)? | One key, `academics.attendance.mark`, covers every status tap and batch mark, whether first-time or a correction. `academics.attendance.edit` is not used in Session 9 — the code has no "already marked vs not" distinction to hang a second key on without new detection logic. |
| Attendance class-list filtering scope (PRD Tier 3 / Session 9, decided 2026-07-01)? | Deferred. `loadAllLeafClasses()` stays unfiltered this session — every staff member sees every class. `academics.attendance.view_all` and `canForClass`-based class-list filtering are logged as a known gap (§11), not wired in Session 9. Revisit in a future session once prioritized. |
| Does admin bypass permission checks, or does admin also need explicit keys like any other role (PRD Tier 3 / Session 9, decided 2026-07-01)? | Admin (`is_admin_role: true`) always bypasses `can()`/`canForClass()` checks entirely — not implemented yet as of this decision, belongs in `permissionsService.ts`/`authStore.ts` (one fix, applies to every module), not patched per-module. An admin role can legitimately hold an empty `permissions` array once this is implemented. |
| Where should staff role assignment/reassignment live (PRD Tier 3 / Session 9, decided 2026-07-01)? | `HRModule.tsx`'s existing staff edit form (extend `StaffEditForm` + `handleSaveStaffEdit`), not `SettingsModule.tsx`'s `StaffTab`. `StaffTab` stays read-only per its own stated intent; HR already owns staff-record edits. |
| Default password: viewable/regeneratable, or hashed-and-gone (PRD Tier 3 / Session 9, decided 2026-07-01)? | Viewable/printable by admin until claimed, and admin-regeneratable. Store `staff.default_password` + `staff.default_password_set_at`, written once by `create-staff-account/index.ts` (plaintext already transits that function for `createUser()`; today it is simply discarded after the one-time response). Auto-clear via **both** a 7-day time limit and first real login (`auth.users.last_sign_in_at` populated) — not either alone. Surfaced a new, previously unlogged requirement: a staff self-service password-change screen does not exist yet and is now required scope, not a deferred gap. |
| Default-password auto-clear mechanism — cron/scheduled job vs. check-on-read (PRD Session 10b, decided 2026-07-02)? | **Check-on-read**, not cron. This app has zero scheduled-job infrastructure anywhere (confirmed by grep before deciding) — building one for a single 7-day expiry check would be new, first-of-its-kind infra for a problem that doesn't need it; nobody is harmed if an expired value sits unexercised in the column for a few extra hours, since RLS/the admin-only view already prevent it from being shown or honored past expiry. Expiry is computed fresh on every read in `loadStaffDefaultPassword()`, never stored or cron-cleared. **Only partially delivers the original "both conditions independently clear it" requirement above:** the 7-day path is real; the login-based path is not — `auth.users.last_sign_in_at` is Auth-Admin-API-only (service-role, server-side) and `app_identities` (§7.2) has no mirrored column for it. Rather than invent a column, `claimed` is typed and always returned as `false`, honestly documented in `hrService.ts` as a named gap, not silently faked. A future session could close it with a small Edge Function or a login-trigger mirror column — not scoped into any session number yet. |
| Staff self-service password-change screen — where in the app's navigation (PRD Session 10b, decided 2026-07-02)? | The account popover, as a new "Account preferences" item between the existing Language row and the Audit log button — not a Settings/profile area, which doesn't exist for non-admin staff/guardians/students. Built as `AccountPreferencesScreen.tsx` (after one mid-session rename from an initial `ChangePasswordScreen.tsx`), deliberately scoped wider than password change alone, on the owner's explicit direction: it's the intended future home for theme, language, font size, and alarm settings too, each as its own section on the same screen using a shared placeholder shell — avoids a rename/re-route churn when those land later. The account popover's own separate, pre-existing "Language" row (a disabled quick-glance display) is unrelated and stays as-is; the future *live* Language control will live inside this new screen's own Language section. |
| Grade/position computation? | Fully automatic — computed views, not stored columns |
| Teacher assignments? | Many-to-many — one teacher can teach multiple subjects across multiple classes |
| Fee discounts/installments? | Full support: discounts, waivers, scholarships, installment plans |
| Ledger scope? | Full double-entry: income, expenses, payroll, assets |
| Platform billing tables? | Build structure now, no enforcement automation yet |
| Notification channels at launch? | In-app + email only; schema reserves SMS/WhatsApp for later |
| Library scope? | Physical per-school (fines, barcodes, multiple copies) + platform-wide digital resources |
| Authentication methods? | Email+password, phone+OTP, login-code — admin assigns per role per school |
| Subjects across classes? | Can differ per class; default is same list with elective override option |
| Score breakdown? | Fully custom components and weights per school |
| Guardian → student link? | Multiple guardians per student; only one gets platform access (partial unique index) |
| Attendance granularity? | Both daily and per-period; setting per class node |
| Report card formats? | Both tabular CA and WAEC-style; template assigned per class_node |
| Alumni/historical records? | Kept forever; `alumni` status, never deleted |
| Inter-school transfer? | Consent-gated handoff; two separate student rows; history stays at releasing school |
| Audit trail? | Universal — every sensitive edit anywhere: who/when/what |
| File storage split? | Supabase Storage (small auth-scoped), Cloudflare R2 (bulk/library) |
| Documents (report cards, receipts)? | Generated client-side on demand; not stored as files |
| Staff HR depth? | Leave requests/approval and payroll runs as real modules |
| Developer device? | Android phone — Termux for local dev, browser for Supabase/GitHub |
| Typing preference? | Almost never hand-type code — prompt-driven AI generation is the plan |
| Languages? | English + Arabic + Hausa; English is system default |
| School name in i18n? | Never translated, never passed through any translation function; always rendered as-entered |
| Frontend state management? | Zustand — platform-agnostic, works identically in future React Native app |
| Future native app? | Planned — every frontend decision accounts for React Native port; business logic in service files, Zustand for state, no browser-only APIs in shared logic |
| Design reference for UI/visual pass? | Read-only port from the old Dilimi madrasah app's `index__17_.html` (design DNA only — token architecture, layout patterns, icon style, component behavior — never its live-project code or data; see continuity prompt) |
| Icon system? | Inline monochrome SVG (`viewBox="0 0 24 24"`, `stroke="currentColor"`), **originally specified as a port from the reference app's ~45-icon set — superseded 2026-07-09, see the dedicated Session 25 icon-source decision row below; the reference app file is no longer available to this project.** Extended with newly authored icons in the same style for any concept the chosen source set doesn't cover — no icon library added as a runtime dependency. |
| Icon source for Session 25 (PRD Tier 6 / Problem 6.3), decided 2026-07-09, BEFORE any Session 25 code was written | **Reference app (`index__17_.html`) is no longer available — owner confirmed it cannot be supplied.** Session 25 was originally scoped as "port the reference app's `ICONS` object," which is no longer literally possible; this is a genuine, logged scope substitution, not a silent one. Owner directed research into the most appropriate substitute rather than defaulting to guesswork. **Researched and decided: [Lucide](https://lucide.dev), sourced as copied raw SVG markup, not the `lucide-react` npm package.** Reasoning, in order of weight: (1) **Shape match is exact, not approximate** — Lucide's default convention is `viewBox="0 0 24 24"`, `stroke="currentColor"`, `stroke-width="2"`, rounded line caps — the identical convention this project's own §12/§13 already specify as the target, and very likely the same convention the reference app's own hand-authored icons followed (a 24×24/stroke/currentColor icon set is a near-universal choice for this visual style, not unique to either project). (2) **Coverage** — 1,600+ icons (per Lucide's 2026 v1.0 release), comfortably covering every concept a school-management app needs (calendar, bell, printer, edit, trash, settings, users, book, wallet/money, graduation cap, etc.), with headroom for anything genuinely novel to author in the same style, matching the PRD's own "floor, not ceiling" instruction. (3) **License** — ISC, functionally equivalent to MIT for this purpose: free for commercial and personal use, no in-UI attribution required, only the copyright notice needs preserving in whatever source file the icons are copied from/into. (4) **Real React Native finding that changed the sourcing method, not just the icon choice:** `lucide-react` (the standard npm package for web) renders a DOM `<svg>` and does not run in React Native at all — a separate package, `lucide-react-native`, exists, built on `react-native-svg`. Per §5 (every frontend decision must account for the future native-app port), importing from `lucide-react` now would mean a second, avoidable import-path swap at native-port time. **Resolution:** icons are not installed as an npm dependency at all — individual icons' raw SVG path data are copied from Lucide's open-source repository directly into this project's own hand-authored `src/components/icons/index.ts` module (or `Icon.tsx`), matching the project's pre-existing "no external icon library" convention from the row above and sidestepping the web/native package split entirely — the same bare-SVG-string approach works unchanged if/when this app is ported to React Native, consistent with §5's "no browser-only APIs in shared logic" principle. **This decision is logged here, before any Session 25 code was written, per this document's own standing discipline of recording locked decisions in §12 before the session that depends on them proceeds.** |
| Brand color token architecture? | Full derived shade scale (a color-math helper computes `-950`→`-50` off the admin-set `--color-brand-600` hex) — not a hardcoded palette. Gold stays a fixed accent color, not derived from the brand color |
| Design-port scope (Problems 6.8–6.11)? | Not limited to the original seven named widgets — extends to the app's entire structural/flow language: app shell (sidebar/header/bottom nav), and every module (Attendance, Students, Announcements direct-ported; Results/Finance/HR/Library/Guardian-Student Portal via applied pattern language, since the reference app has no equivalent screen for these five) |
| Guardian-name tap inside a student's Guardians subtab — cross-module navigation with a way back, or stay in-place (PRD SESSION 11, decided 2026-07-02)? | **Stay in-place.** No navigation-history stack exists anywhere in the app (confirmed by grep); building one to serve a single "go back to the student I came from" link was rejected in favor of not leaving the screen at all. Guardian-name taps open an in-place **guardian brief popup** inside `StudentsModule.tsx` (name, relationship, phone, email, all other linked students of that guardian) instead of jumping to `GuardianModule.tsx`. A deliberate one-way "Edit in Guardians module →" link remains inside the popup for real editing — an honest, chosen jump, not a mislabeled "back" button. Establishes the pattern for any future same-shape "peek at a related record without losing your place" need elsewhere in the app, rather than defaulting to cross-module navigation each time. |
| Teacher access to their own payslip — admin-controllable how, and how does hide/show work (PRD Tier 4 / Session 17, decided 2026-07-02)? | **Visibility control is school-wide, not per-staff.** One boolean (`schools.teacher_payslip_visibility_enabled`, admin-controlled, default true) — not a `hr.*` permission-catalog key, since a live catalog query confirmed no matching key existed and this isn't role-shaped the way other HR permissions are. **Hide/show is asymmetric by design, not an oversight:** a teacher can hide their own "My Payslip" card from `TeacherDashboard.tsx` freely, no re-auth — hiding is the safe direction. Showing it again requires re-entering the current password first (`AccountPreferencesScreen.tsx`'s `PayslipVisibilitySection`, verified via `supabase.auth.signInWithPassword()`), a deliberate speed bump on the one direction that re-exposes payroll data — not a hard security boundary, since the data was never actually inaccessible; the teacher chose to hide it and has to mean it a second time to bring it back. Data itself (`loadMyPayslips(staffId)`) is staff-scoped at the query level regardless of either flag's state; the flags gate visibility, not access. **Session 18 correction:** the card must never link out to the admin HR module (`onNavigate('hr')`) regardless of any data-scoping correctness underneath — a teacher's own dashboard should show what they need inline, full stop, not act as a doorway into admin-facing surfaces. |
| Scheme of work — approval workflow required, or teacher self-publish (PRD Tier 8 / Problem 8.6, decided 2026-07-12)? | **Submit → approve/return workflow required**, not self-publish — matches researched Nigerian norm (schemes submitted to HOD/principal at start of term, not self-certified) and gives admin/HOD a real review gate before a scheme counts as live. `status` lifecycle: `draft → submitted → approved`, with `returned` as a revise-and-resubmit path (not a terminal rejection) — `review_note` required by the UI whenever status is set to `returned`, same "never silent rejection" discipline as Problem 8.4's promotion flow. |
| Scheme of work — weekly coverage tracking in scope for first launch, or static term plan only (PRD Tier 8 / Problem 8.6, decided 2026-07-12)? | **In scope.** Per-week `coverage_status` (`planned`/`covered`/`partially_covered`/`not_covered`) on `scheme_of_work_weeks`, not a single blanket flag — this is the difference between a static submitted document and a live pacing signal, per research on comparable SIS platforms (SOW broken into weeks, coverage tracked against it, visible to admin). Teacher marks weeks as the term progresses; admin gets a coverage-at-a-glance view across teachers/subjects. |
| Scheme of work — sequenced before/alongside or after Assessment Windows, Problem 8.4 (PRD Tier 8 / Problem 8.6, decided 2026-07-12)? | **After.** No technical dependency either way — the two table families are deliberately decoupled (content pacing vs. scoring/weighting), so this could have run in parallel with 8.4's Sessions 46–50. Owner elected to sequence it after 8.4 closes anyway, since 8.4 is the bigger, already-moving critical path and splitting attention across both risks landing both late — a resourcing decision, not a technical one. |
| Modules with no reference-app equivalent (Problem 6.11)? | Apply the pattern language established by Problems 6.1/6.8–6.10 (card shape/shadow, list-row height, form-sheet behavior, button/badge treatment, empty-state layout) rather than inventing independent per-module styling |
| Term/session end-date extend/revert mechanism — resolves the previously-open §7.4/Session 29 question (PRD Problem 6.7, decided 2026-07-04, folded into Session 18 early) | **Live-computed, never stored.** `getEffectiveTermEndDate(baseStartDate, baseEndDate, schoolId)` in `attendanceService.ts` computes `base_end_date + count of qualifying school-day holidays`, iterating since an extension can pull a later holiday into the window — nothing is written back to `terms`/`sessions`, so delete-to-revert is automatic and never drifts. **Owner refinement over the original PRD spec:** extension is a **per-entry choice** (`school_calendar_days.extends_term`), not a blanket rule — a single stray public holiday can be left non-extending, a planned break can be marked to extend. Only dates that would otherwise have been real school days (per `school_week_days`) count toward the extension, regardless of how they were entered (single-date or bulk-range). Session 29 (Tier 6, `TermProgressCard.tsx`) inherits this working computation rather than needing to resolve the mechanism itself. |
| Should bulk-range calendar entry pre-filter or skip weekends automatically (Session 18, decided 2026-07-04)? | **No.** Owner correction: don't reason in terms of "weekend," since some schools run a Fri/Sat week, Sun-only week, etc. — `school_week_days` is what defines a school day per-school, and calendar-day bulk entry has no business guessing which dates in a range "matter." `bulkUpsertCalendarDays()` marks every date in the given range with the same type/label/extends_term, full stop; `getEffectiveTermEndDate()` and the attendance calendar-awareness logic are what correctly recognize the already-non-school dates within that range as not qualifying (for extension) or not counting as a miss (for attendance). |
| Where do holiday/exam/break calendar entries live in Settings, and what happens to the existing "Calendar" tab (Session 18, decided 2026-07-04)? | **Inside the existing "Schedule" tab**, as a new section below Periods — not a new top-level tab. Reasoning: Week Days (recurring weekly pattern) and calendar-day entries (specific-date exceptions to that pattern) are the same underlying question — "is this a school day, and how is it structured?" — at two different resolutions, so they belong together rather than split across two tabs or added to the pre-existing "Calendar" tab (which is unrelated: sessions/terms). The existing "Calendar" tab's **visible label was changed to "Sessions"** to remove the naming collision — its internal tab id (`calendar`) was deliberately left unchanged to avoid touching every reference to it, only `TABS`'s `label` field was edited. |
| Should the Week Days chip-toggle section be collapsed by default in Settings (Session 18, decided 2026-07-04)? | **Yes, always collapsed on load** — not just for new/unconfigured schools. Owner's stated reasoning: too much depends on this setting (attendance's school-day logic, calendar-day extension math, analytics denominators) for it to be a casual one-tap change; a deliberate "Edit week days" click is the right amount of friction. A one-line summary of the currently-saved days (or "Not set") shows in the collapsed header so the setting is still visible at a glance without being open. |
| Dark mode — in scope at all (Session 23, decided 2026-07-09)? | **Yes, in scope** — resolves the previously-open question below. Full dark-theme token block (`[data-theme="dark"]`) and its storage/persistence mechanism are **deferred as one bundled decision to Session 28**, alongside the settings-persistence-model question (per-device vs. per-account) — not decided piecemeal here, since dark mode's storage question and the rest of the settings bundle's storage question are the same underlying question asked twice if split across two sessions. Session 23 itself ships light-theme tokens only; zero dark-mode CSS, schema, or toggle code exists yet. |
| Gold accent contrast values (Session 23, decided 2026-07-09) | `--color-gold-on: #1a1200` — verified with real WCAG math (not asserted): clears 4.5:1 against both `--color-gold-500` (7.68:1) and `--color-gold-600` (5.29:1); pure white fails against both (2.42:1 / 3.51:1). |
| Motion scale values (Session 23, decided 2026-07-09) | `--motion-fast: 0.1s`, `--motion-base: 0.15s`, `--motion-slow: 0.3s` — chosen from a real grep of the file's own existing transition-duration usage (0.15s dominant at 88 occurrences), not invented. Declaration-only this session; existing hardcoded-duration rules were not rewritten to consume these. |
| Wrong-school error message wording (Session 23, decided 2026-07-09) | Kept deliberately generic — never names the person's actual correct school. Rendered as a `topLevelError` banner on the ordinary `LoginPage`, not a separate dedicated page — the normal login form stays usable underneath so a person with a second, genuinely valid set of credentials for this specific school isn't stranded. |

Two options considered: (a) a direct `students.programme_level_id` FK, matching the existing `class_node_id` precedent exactly — `class_node_id` is itself just overwritten each session with no history table behind it anywhere in §7.5; smaller change, but loses "what level was this student in last session" the moment it's overwritten; (b) a join/history table. **Owner confirmed (b) is the real need** — retroactive per-session lookups are a known requirement for this school, not speculative. | The self-read RLS policy on `student_programme_placements` (§7.27.1a) referenced `current_actor_id()`, which does not exist anywhere in this codebase — how was this caught, and does the same bug exist elsewhere (found 2026-07-13; both instances FIXED)? | **Fixed in both places — §7.27.1a at migration time, §7.27.2 pre-emptively before its first migration.** `current_actor_id()` was written into §7.27.1a's self-read policy by copying the *shape* of `course_registrations`' self-read policy (§7.27.2) without verifying the function it names actually exists. Confirmed against §3.2's real helper-function list: only `current_school_id()` and `current_actor_type()` exist anywhere in this schema — no `current_actor_id()`, ever. Caught for real, not by inspection: `student_programme_placements`' migration was run and Postgres rejected it with `ERROR: 42883: function current_actor_id() does not exist`. The correct, already-established pattern for "does this row belong to the logged-in actor" is a lookup against `app_identities` (`auth_user_id = auth.uid()` → `actor_record_id`), the same shape used by every other self-read policy in this schema (payslips, notifications). §7.27.1a's policy corrected and re-migrated successfully. **§7.27.2's documented policy had the identical bug** — corrected in its schema text at the start of SESSION 56, before `course_registrations` was ever migrated, so that table never hit the error directly; it simply never shipped with the bug. |
| The course-catalogue form's "Credit units" field couldn't be edited past the default `1` — any input starting with `1` was also unenterable (PRD Problem 8.7 / SESSION 56, found and FIXED 2026-07-13 during on-device testing)? | **Fixed — the field now holds a raw string during editing, coerced to a number only at save time.** Root cause: `cCreditUnits` was `number`-typed, driven by `onChange={v => setCCreditUnits(Number(v) || 1)}`. `Number('') === 0`, which is falsy, so the instant the field went empty mid-edit (e.g. deleting the default "1" to type a new value) the `|| 1` fallback fired and silently reset it to `1` before a second keystroke could register — the same trap caught anything beginning with "1" (10, 12, 100), since backspacing through it passed through the same empty-string state. This was a UI-only bug, not a schema or RLS issue like the two rows above, but recorded here for the same reason: found during real on-device use, not anticipated by the session card. Fixed by changing `cCreditUnits` to hold the typed string as-is (digits only, via input filtering) with no per-keystroke coercion, and moving numeric validation (`Number.isInteger`, `≥ 1`) into `handleSaveCourse` at save time, surfacing a real error message instead of a silent default. See PRD SESSION 56's card and Log row 56 for the on-device confirmation. |
| SESSION 57 on-device Scenario A verification query returned 3 courses for a student registered into only 2 — schema/insert bug, or something else (PRD Problem 8.7 / SESSION 57, found and FIXED 2026-07-14 during on-device testing)? | **Fixed — the bug was in the verification SQL's join, not in `registerStudent()`, `course_registrations`, or any shipped code.** A raw, unjoined read of `course_registrations` confirmed exactly 2 rows existed for the student/session — the insert was correct from the start. The 3-row result came from the verification query's `left join programme_curriculum pc on pc.course_id = cr.course_id`, scoped to `course_id` alone with no `programme_level_id`/`term_id` condition: when a registered course's `course_id` appeared in more than one `programme_curriculum` row (e.g. listed under more than one level/term), the join fanned that single registration out into multiple result rows, each carrying a different `requirement_type`. This reproduces the exact same class of bug as the SESSION 56 row directly above — a query built without checking the real join cardinality first — except here it was in an ad hoc verification query, not shipped code, so no app behavior was ever wrong. Fixed by joining `programme_curriculum` through the student's actual `student_programme_placements` row (`is_current = true` → `programme_level_id`) and matching `term_id`, the same resolution path `loadCurriculum()` already uses in `courseRegistrationService.ts` — re-run, returned exactly 2 rows. **Recorded as a general lesson, not just a one-off fix:** any future query joining `programme_curriculum` on `course_id` alone, without also scoping to the student's placement, is subject to the same fan-out if that course is ever reused across more than one level or term. No code changes were required in `courseRegistrationService.ts` or `CourseRegistrationModule.tsx` — both were already correct. See PRD SESSION 57's card and Log row 57 for the full on-device confirmation (Scenarios A and B). |
| SESSION 58 (PRD Problem 8.7): `course_attendance_records`' self-read policy — follow §7.27.2's student-only precedent, §7.13's guardian-only precedent, or something else? What about `marked_by` and a uniqueness constraint, both absent from the original §7.27.3 spec? Decided 2026-07-14, before migrating. | **Both self-read audiences, not one precedent picked over the other — owner's explicit direction: "I think both. But prioritise best ux for the industry."** Reasoning: a higher-ed student is an adult and the platform's primary user for their own exam-gating attendance percentage (matching §7.27.2's own precedent, reversed from §7.13's secondary-school/guardian-only world), so student self-read is the primary path; several real Nigerian tertiary institutions (this school's own NMCN-regulated context among them) also give parents/sponsors visibility, so guardian self-read is added as a genuinely secondary, additive policy — scoped through `student_guardians` (§7.5, confirmed as a general-purpose link table, not secondary-specific) and gated on `has_platform_access = true` (a real partial-unique-index-enforced constraint, checked directly rather than assumed, and initially missed on a first draft of the policy before being caught and fixed pre-migration). **`marked_by uuid not null references staff(id)`, added** — the original spec had no lecturer/staff attribution at all; without it there is no audit trail for a disputed mark and no way to confirm the mark was entered by the lecturer actually assigned to that `course_offering`. **`unique (course_attendance_session_id, student_id)`, added** — the original spec had no DB-level uniqueness at all, which would have broken `onConflict`-based retap-to-update (the same class of gap, though not the identical mechanism, as §7.13's own documented nullable-`period_id` uniqueness bug). **A fourth, related gap found later the same day, after the original migration was already live:** `course_attendance_sessions` itself had no uniqueness on `(course_offering_id, session_date)` — found while writing `ensureCourseAttendanceSession()`, closed via a genuine follow-up migration (`migration_session_58b.sql`), not a silent edit to already-shipped SQL. All four decisions recorded in §7.27.3 before/at the point each was made, not reconstructed after the fact. |

| SESSION 61 (PRD Problem 8.7): the write-gate RLS policies for `academic_standing_rules`/`academic_standing_events` (§7.27.5) referenced `current_staff_id()`, which does not exist anywhere in this codebase — how was this caught, and what's the correct mechanism (found and FIXED 2026-07-16, before migrating)? | **Fixed before running — a first migration draft (from a since-recovered, previously-unrecorded session) resolved §7.27.5's "write access gated on `academics.academic_standing.review`" note by inventing a `current_staff_id()`-based identity join, the same class of mistake as the `current_actor_id()` row above (copying a plausible-looking shape without verifying the named function actually exists).** Caught before anything was run, not after a failed migration this time: the live helper set was queried directly (`select proname, ... from pg_proc where nspname = 'public' and proname ilike '%current_%'`) and confirmed to be exactly `current_actor_type()`, `current_has_permission(perm_key text)`, `current_is_admin()`, `current_school_id()` — no staff-identity resolver of any kind exists. Re-reading §7.27.5's own text confirmed it never actually called for a staff-identity join in the first place — "gated on `academics.academic_standing.review`" is a permission-key check, which `current_has_permission()` (a real, live function) does directly; no join was ever needed. The correct shape, confirmed against the one other place in this codebase already combining "row-scope + permission key" (the storage-bucket write policy), is: `[STD]`-equivalent scope for reads, plus `current_is_admin() or current_has_permission('academics.academic_standing.review')` on writes. `promotion_history` — the nearest audit-trail precedent by table shape — was re-read directly and confirmed to use plain `[STD]` with no permission-gated write at all (`decided_by` is an unenforced audit column there, not an RLS join target), so it was **not** a valid template for this specific question, despite being the right template for `academic_standing_events`' general audit-trail shape otherwise. Migration corrected to use only the confirmed-live helpers and run successfully; all 7 policies independently verified via `pg_policies`. §7.27.5's RLS note corrected in place to state the actual mechanism, not just the general intent, so this ambiguity cannot recur the same way on a future table. See PRD SESSION 61's card and Log row 62 for the full account, including the second, smaller `module`-column omission also caught before running. |
| SESSION 62pre (PRD Problem 8.7): should carryover status auto-flag on finalize, or go through a human-reviewed queue like `academic_standing_events` — and separately, is "failing" ever anything other than `grade_point <= 0` (found and CORRECTED 2026-07-16, before first real use)? | **Auto-flag on finalize, researched against real institutional practice before deciding, not assumed:** UTS/Melbourne/APU all record a fail deterministically the moment a grade is finalized — the human-reviewed step in every real system found is about the *consequences* of a fail (progression, exclusion, a Return-to-Good-Standing plan), never about whether the fail itself gets recorded. Gating the flag itself behind review would have meant reviewing the same fact twice: once pointlessly (is this a fail? — deterministic, not a judgment call) and once meaningfully (does this pattern of fails warrant probation/spillover? — already correctly gated by SESSION 61/62's `academic_standing_events`). **Separately, "failing" was initially — and wrongly — inferred as `grade_point <= 0`, caught by the owner's own on-device testing, not by design review:** the owner set a `0–49` band to `grade_point = 0`, confirmed the flip worked, then asked directly whether an institution could ever want a *positive*-grade-point band to still count as failing. Researched rather than guessed at: UNC Law's own published grade scale runs bands below its passing line at nonzero grade points (a `D` at `grade_point ≈ 1.0` can be a technically-passing course grade while still failing a program's own higher minimum) — confirming `grade_point <= 0` is a narrower rule than real institutions use, not a safe universal default. Corrected before this shipped anywhere: added an explicit `is_passing boolean` per grade band (`grade_scales`) and per finalized attempt (`course_results`, persisted once at finalize so it can't silently drift if the scale is edited later) — `apply_carryover_status()` takes `p_is_passing` directly from the caller's resolved band, never inferring from the numeric grade point. See §7.27.4's SESSION 62pre amendment above, and PRD SESSION 62pre's card / PRD Log row 62pre for the full account, including a `create or replace function` parameter-rename error (Postgres `42P13`) hit on re-applying the corrected migration, and a second, independently-hardcoded `gradePoint > 0` site (`courseResultsService.ts`'s admin-view live CGPA computation) that a real `npm run build` failure — not the original plan — surfaced and required the identical fix. |

| SESSION 70 (PRD Problem 8.7a): what is a "fee" for this school in the higher-ed context — per session, per semester, per course, flat, or programme-dependent? | **Flat per programme/level per session/term — researched before deciding, not assumed.** Every real Nigerian university example found (FUTA, UNN, NOUN, KWASU, NDU, Nile) bills a flat total per level/session/semester; none charge per individual course registered. `fee_assignments.target_type` gains `'programme_level'` alongside the existing `school_wide`/`class_node`/`student`, with `programme_id`+`programme_level_id` added (both travel together, matching `course_offerings`/`programme_curriculum`'s own established pairing convention, confirmed via a live schema query before choosing this over a bare `programme_level_id`-only FK). One assignment row = one flat fee for everyone in that programme/level for a session/term. Per-student variation (scholarships, negotiated part-payments) is handled entirely by the existing `fee_discounts`/`installment_plans` mechanism — no new per-student amount override field, no parallel schema. This is an extension of the existing secondary-school fee model, not a second one; `fee_assignments` was already generic enough (`target_type` already supported `school_wide`, and `term_id` was already the same nullable/terms pattern higher-ed uses everywhere else). |
| SESSION 70 (PRD Problem 8.7a): is Remita multi-tenant across schools, and whose bank account should receive a school's tuition payments? | **Each school owns and registers its own Remita merchant account; money goes straight to that school's own account, the platform is never a money-in-the-middle party.** Remita's own onboarding is one merchant profile per institution (confirmed across official docs/SDKs) — this is not something Remita's API itself makes multi-tenant, so the platform's own schema carries the tenancy: `payment_methods_enabled.config` (already a jsonb column, already keyed per `school_id`+`method`) stores each school's own Remita reference, not one shared platform-level merchant account. |
| SESSION 70 (PRD Problem 8.7a): how sensitive should each school's Remita API secret be treated, and what storage mechanism? | **Supabase Vault, not a plain jsonb column and not custom envelope encryption — researched and compared explicitly before deciding.** Threat model reasoned through plainly: Vault (encryption at rest via `vault.secrets`/`vault.decrypted_secrets`, `select` revoked from `authenticated`/`anon`, only a narrow `security definer` function callable by the service role can ever read a decrypted value) defends against a curious/malicious staff member with ordinary DB access, an RLS bug, or a leaked read-only credential — but, like every alternative considered (including application-level envelope encryption and an external KMS/HSM), it does **not** defend against a compromised Edge Function itself, since the function necessarily holds the plaintext at the moment it calls Remita — the same trust boundary every payment integration has (Stripe/Paystack SDKs on a server can always see the secret key). Envelope encryption was rejected specifically because it would make this codebase own key management/rotation/nonce-handling correctness forever, for a stack with no dedicated security engineer — real, ongoing self-inflicted-crypto-bug risk for only a narrow additional guarantee (protection against a DB-level compromise reading `vault.decrypted_secrets` directly). An external KMS/HSM was rejected as infrastructure disproportionate to this project's actual stack (Supabase, no dedicated KMS layer). `payment_methods_enabled.config` for `method='remita'` stores only a `vault_secret_id` (Vault's own returned uuid) plus non-secret fields like `merchant_id` — never the plaintext key/token. The admin-facing settings form is write-only, matching `staff.default_password`'s own "shown once" precedent: an admin pastes the key in once, it's stored, and the form never redisplays it on reload. |
| SESSION 70 (PRD Problem 8.7a): should the payment trigger be student self-service ("Pay Now"), admin-triggered ("send payment link"), or both? | **Student self-service only — researched against real precedent before deciding.** Every real example found (Oregon State, Essex County College, University of Edinburgh, and vendor platforms Global Payments/Paymentus/PayMyTuition) has the student initiate payment 24/7 from their own account view; none use admin-triggered initiation as a primary pattern — admin-side tools in every real example are for visibility/reconciliation, not for starting a payment on a student's behalf. This app's own decision to also support bank-teller/USSD/card payment against a self-generated RRR (see the row below) is the real-world equivalent of every real institution's own manual fallback, and doesn't require an admin-initiation path to exist alongside it. |
| SESSION 70 (PRD Problem 8.7a): support only online card payment for v1, or also the real-world "generate RRR, pay at a bank counter/USSD later, portal shows pending until reconciled" flow? | **Build both now — this is standard real Nigerian institutional practice** (bank teller, USSD, and card are all valid ways to settle a real Remita RRR, not just online checkout), and it maps cleanly onto fields `payments` already has with no new state machine needed: `status: 'pending'` the moment an RRR is generated (works identically whether paid online or offline), `provider_reference` holds the RRR immediately, and `paid_at`/`status: 'completed'` flip only once server-side verification succeeds against Remita's own status endpoint — whether that verification is triggered by a webhook (online payment) or a manual "check status" re-trigger (since Remita's own status endpoint is polling-based, not push-only, per research; the same action serves a student or admin re-checking after paying at a bank). |
| SESSION 70 research note — Remita's real integration shape, confirmed across official docs/SDKs/working samples, not a single blog post | RRR-based flow: every real integration generates a Remita Retrieval Reference (RRR, a unique invoice number) server-side first, before any money moves; the payer then settles that RRR via card, bank transfer, USSD, or in-person at a bank teller — confirmed universal across every real Nigerian university integration found. Auth is a request hash (`SHA512(merchantId + serviceTypeId + orderId + amount + apiKey)`, sent via an `Authorization: remitaConsumerKey=...,remitaConsumerToken=...` header) in the most-documented flow; newer docs also show HMAC-SHA256 and OAuth2 for a newer API tier — Remita is visibly mid-migration between two auth generations, to be confirmed against whichever generation the school's real sandbox credentials actually use, not assumed. Status/verification is a separate, independently-callable endpoint (`.../status.reg` or `/payment/query/{transactionId}`) — the correct pattern is generate RRR → payer settles elsewhere → independently re-verify by calling Remita's own status endpoint server-side before ever trusting a client-side "payment succeeded" redirect. A confirmed payment carries a real receipt/notification payload (RRR, amount, channel, teller name where relevant) sufficient to generate a real receipt, not just log a boolean. |
| SESSION 71 (root-cause finding, PRD Problem 8.9 — new): why has a student-self login never been able to load the Guardian/Student portal, at any point since it was first built? | **Root-caused via direct SQL, not guessed at — a systemic missing-policy pattern, not one broken table.** `pg_policies` read against every table `GuardianPortal.tsx`/`portalService.ts` reads directly confirmed: `students`, `attendance_records`, `fee_assignments`, `fee_discounts`, `payments`, and `scores` (which `subject_results` — a plain view, not a table — reads from) each carry a `_guardian_select` and/or `_staff_all`/`_staff_read` policy, but **no student-self `SELECT` policy at all**. A signed-in student's own session therefore silently returns zero rows on every one of these tables (RLS default-deny, not an error) — `loadChildRecord()` (the very first real query `boot()` makes) returns `null`, `loadPortalIdentity()` resolves to `{ kind: 'none' }`, and `GuardianPortal.tsx` falls into `bootState === 'error'`, exactly matching the owner's report and screenshot. This has been true since student-self login was introduced — never a regression, and independent of anything in SESSION 70's own Remita work. **By contrast, `course_registrations` and `student_programme_placements` (both built in SESSION 55/69, specifically for higher-ed student self-service) already carry correct, working student-self policies** — confirming the gap is specifically in the tables built for the original guardian-first portal, where student-as-self was added at the app layer later without the matching RLS ever being written. **`subject_results` checked specifically, since a `false` `relrowsecurity` reading could mean either "blocked" or "a real leak" and the difference matters:** confirmed via `pg_class`/`reloptions` that it's a plain view (not a base table, so `relrowsecurity=false` is normal/expected for it, not itself a red flag) reading from `scores`, and `scores` itself has real RLS with the identical gap (guardian/staff covered, no student-self policy) — so this is the same missing-piece pattern, not a leak. `security_invoker` was never explicitly set on the view (`reloptions` is `null`), which is a second, independent thing worth confirming before relying on the view for student-self reads once the underlying `scores` policy is added — flagged, not yet resolved. **Scoped as its own session (SESSION 71), not folded into SESSION 70,** since the root cause and fix (RLS policy additions) are unrelated to Remita/payments and this blocks the on-device student-side test SESSION 70's own Done Check still needs. |

(2) `PayslipVisibilitySection` given the same collapsed-by-default treatment — its password confirmation form was rendering open whenever the section was visible at all; now behind the same header-click pattern as Password, nothing typed into until clicked. (3) New shared `PasswordInput` component (eye-icon show/hide toggle) used by all password fields on the screen. Visibility is a *group*, not per-field, concept within `PasswordSection` — one `passwordsVisible` boolean shared across Current/New/Confirm, so toggling any one field's eye icon reveals or hides all three together (a person checking what they typed means "all of it"); the payslip section's single password field manages its own local visibility since there's nothing else in that form to stay in sync with. `PasswordInput` accepts optional `visible`/`onToggleVisible` props for this — falls back to fully independent local state when omitted. | ☑ `npm run build` confirmed clean by owner, 2026-07-02. The weekday-eligibility filter narrowing the list itself (`wouldHaveBeenSchoolDay()`, formerly `isRealSchoolDay()`) was confirmed correct as originally written, just re-commented for clarity on why it doesn't reuse `getSchoolDayMap()`. **Corrected again, same day (calendar-vs-school-day counter mismatch):** `totalDays`/`elapsedDays`/`remainingDays` renamed to explicit `totalCalendarDays`/`elapsedCalendarDays`/`remainingCalendarDays` (a genuine ambiguity bug — these were calendar-day counts, but the card displayed them as a bare "Day X of Y" with no unit, disagreeing with the attendance card's own school-day count for the same term); real `totalSchoolDays`/`elapsedSchoolDays`/`remainingSchoolDays` added via the same `getSchoolDayMap()` `loadAttendanceSummary()` already uses, so the two cards can never drift apart again; `schoolDaysPerWeek` added (`schoolWeekDaySet.size`, already in scope, real per-school data — not a hardcoded ÷5/÷7) to support `TermProgressCard.tsx`'s new Weeks display option. `percentElapsed`/`positionPercent` deliberately kept calendar-based, unaffected by this fix — the bar's fill/notch positioning must stay real-time-proportional, only the plain-text counters needed the school-day correction. **Real bugs found and fixed (2026-07-04, Session 15 arc):** (1) `fee_heads` and 4 other PostgREST embeds were cast assuming "always returns an array," confirmed false for at least one embed via a live debug log (`fee_heads` came back as a plain object) — fixed at all 5 sites with a shape-agnostic `unwrapEmbed()` helper rather than patching just the one that broke. (2) `loadAttendanceSummary()`'s `totalSchoolDays` was counting distinct dates-with-a-record, not real school days — now uses `attendanceService.ts`'s real `countSchoolDaysInRange()`/`getSchoolDayMap()` (imported, not duplicated), so guardian and staff views never show two different denominators for the same range. (3) `loadAttendanceCalendarStrip()` now walks every calendar date and tags `unmarked` vs `no_school` distinctly, matching the staff-side fix. **New, owner-requested — class-average attendance comparison:** calls a `SECURITY DEFINER` RPC (`get_class_attendance_average`, see migration) rather than querying `attendance_records` directly, since `attendance_records_guardian_select`'s real RLS (confirmed via `pg_policies`) only permits a guardian to read their own linked child's rows — a direct classmates query would have silently returned nothing rather than erroring. The RPC derives `school_id` from the caller's own session and verifies real class enrollment before returning a single aggregate percentage; confirmed this cannot leak data across schools or across classes within a school. One real bug in the RPC itself (`attendance_records.class_node_id` doesn't exist — class linkage is via `students.class_node_id` only) caught via the owner's own network trace and fixed. No browser-only APIs — React Native safe. **CORS is mandatory for all Edge Functions.** Every function called from the browser needs: `CORS_HEADERS` constant + `OPTIONS` early-return + `...CORS_HEADERS` spread in every response. Omitting this causes silent browser-level failure (405 before any logic runs).

- **2026-06-26 (Timetable module — edit mode, conflict detection, print functions — fully built; planner updated)** — Continuation from the prior session's cut-off point. Three pieces completed this session:

  **(1) Admin edit mode (tap-to-select / tap-to-place).** `TimetableModule.tsx` rewritten with `{ schoolId, schoolName, isAdmin }` props — replacing the old no-prop signature and removing the stale `useAuthStore` internal lookup (replaced by the `isAdmin` prop, same pattern as the rest of the app). Edit mode activates via a header "Edit" button (admin-only). The assignment tray renders below the class selector: one chip per `teaching_assignment` row for the selected class (loaded via `loadTeachingAssignments()`), plus a permanent "Free period" chip. Tap a chip to arm it; tap a grid cell to write/overwrite; tap the same chip again to de-arm. Tapping a filled cell with no chip armed shows an inline "Remove / Keep" confirmation overlay (no modal). Saving uses `upsertTimetableEntry()` with optimistic update — cell shows a spinner during the async call, error badge on failure (auto-clears after 3 s). Teaching-assignment chip for the class must exist before a lesson can be placed — if `teaching_assignments` is empty for the class, the tray shows a plain-English gap message ("Assign teachers to subjects first"). `loadState` is forced to `'ready'` when entering edit mode even with zero entries, so the grid renders and the admin can start filling it in. `schoolId` is passed through to `upsertTimetableEntry()` to satisfy the `with check` RLS clause on `timetable_entries`.

  **(2) Conflict detection.** `findConflictingEntryIds()` (pure in-memory function added to `timetableService.ts` in the prior session) is called on every render from the full `ttData.entries` array — school-wide, not filtered by the current class/teacher view. This means a teacher double-booked across two different classes will show ⚠ badges on both cells simultaneously, even if only one of those classes is currently selected in the view. No write is blocked — conflicts are informational per owner's decision. Badge is amber (color `#d97706`), positioned top-right of the cell.

  **(3) Print function.** New file `src/services/printTimetable.ts`. Pure utility: `printTimetable(opts)` takes the already-loaded `TimetableData` (no extra network query), builds a self-contained HTML document (school name + session name + view label + generation date in the header; full period×day grid as an HTML `<table>`; `@page { size: A4 landscape }` for print), and opens it in a new tab via a Blob URL. **Critical implementation note:** `document.write()` on a blank `window.open('')` is silently blocked by Android Chrome (cross-origin sandbox restriction). The correct approach is `Blob → URL.createObjectURL → window.open(url)` — this is same-origin to the creating page and loads reliably. The object URL is revoked after 60 s. A `window.addEventListener('load', () => window.print())` in the generated page auto-opens the print dialog. The print button (🖨) appears in the header whenever `ttData.entries.length > 0` and edit mode is off; it is hidden in edit mode and on the empty state. `schoolName` was added as a third prop to `TimetableModule` (alongside existing `schoolId` and `isAdmin`) and threaded down from `App.tsx` via `TabContent` — same pattern as `schoolId`.

  **(4) Bug caught and fixed same session.** Print opened a blank tab on first test. Root cause: `document.write()` blocked by Android Chrome. Fixed immediately by switching to the Blob URL approach described above.

  **(5) CSS additions.** `phase6-timetable-editmode.css` (appended to `index.css`) adds: `.tt-tray-*` (assignment tray), `.tt-chip` / `.tt-chip--armed` / `.tt-chip--free` (tappable lesson chips with armed-state ring), `.tt-cell--droppable` / `.tt-cell--clearable` / `.tt-cell--saving` / `.tt-cell--error` / `.tt-cell--pending-clear` (grid cell states), `.tt-clear-confirm` (inline clear confirmation overlay), `.tt-conflict-badge` (amber ⚠ positioned top-right), `.tt-print-btn` (print icon button), and `@media print { .app-header, .app-bottom-nav, .tt-header { display: none } }` (hides chrome if user prints the main app page directly). Also defines `.tt-grid--skel` (previously referenced in skeleton markup but not defined — cosmetic gap now closed). `.tt-grid--edit` adds a faint amber outline to the grid while edit mode is active, making the editing context visually clear.

  Load state machine: `LoadState = 'booting' | 'ready' | 'loading' | 'empty' | 'error'` — two parallel state machines (one for the class selector, one for the register body), same discipline as `TimetableModule`. `loadState` is forced to `'ready'` whenever students load successfully (even with zero attendance records) so the register renders and marking can begin immediately without waiting for records.

  Boot flow (one parallel `Promise.all`): `loadCurrentSession()` + `loadAllLeafClasses()` → sets session name in header + populates class selector. Class change triggers `loadStudentsForClass()` + `loadAttendanceSettings()` in parallel; if `per_period`, also `loadPeriods()` (sequential after settings — can't run parallel since granularity is unknown). Records load whenever `selectedClass`, `selectedDate`, or `selectedPeriod` changes (via `useCallback` + `useEffect` on `loadState === 'ready'`).

  Optimistic UI: every status button tap fires `handleStatusTap()` — updates `attMap` immediately (Map key swap), marks `savingIds` (disables buttons + shows ⟳ spinner), calls `saveAttendanceRecord()` in background. On success: clears `savingIds`. On queued: adds student to `queuedIds` (shows ☁ badge). On error: reverts `attMap` to previous value, adds to `errorIds` (shows ✕ badge with error tooltip), auto-clears after 3 s via `setTimeout` + `useRef` timer map (clears any previous timer for same student before setting a new one).

  Batch mark-all: `handleBatchMark(status, markedBy)` — updates all rows in `attMap` optimistically in one pass, then calls `saveBatchAttendance()`. On failure: reverts `attMap` to pre-batch snapshot. On queued: adds all student IDs to `queuedIds`.

- **2026-06-26 (Session 18 — Finance module runtime bugs fixed; payment notes + fee head editing added)** —

  Four bugs reported after on-device testing of the finance module. All fixed this session.

  **(1) Bug: `fee_assignments.currency does not exist` — permanent error on Assignments tab.**
  `loadFeeAssignments()` was selecting `currency` from `fee_assignments`, but that column does not exist on that table (only `fee_heads` and `payments` have it — confirmed against §7.16). The INSERT-side fix from session 17 correctly removed `currency` from the insert payload, but the SELECT was never updated. Fix: removed `currency` from the `.select()` string; the mapper now hardcodes `currency: 'NGN'` instead of reading `r.currency`. This unblocked the Assignments tab — it was showing a Postgres error on every load and silently succeeding on write (hence assignments appearing on the Balances page but never in the Assignments list).

  **(2) Bug: Fee head dropdown empty in payment form + "student or fee assignment no longer exists" error.**
  Two distinct root causes:
  - **Empty dropdown:** `assignments` state was only populated when the user visited the Assignments tab (lazy-load on tab switch). Opening a student detail from the Balances tab without ever visiting Assignments left `assignments = []`, so the payment form had no options. Fix: assignments are now loaded eagerly during boot in parallel with the other boot data (`loadFeeAssignments()` added to the `Promise.all` alongside `loadLeafClasses`, `loadFeeHeads`, `loadCurrentSession`). They remain available for the Assignments tab render with no extra round-trip.
  - **FK error:** `payments.received_by` is a FK to `staff.id`, but the code was passing `auth.users.id` (the `auth.uid()` from the session), which is a different UUID stored in `app_identities.auth_user_id`. Fix: `recordPayment()` now accepts `authUserId` (the session's `user.id`) and resolves the correct `staff.id` itself by querying `app_identities` (`select actor_record_id, actor_type where auth_user_id = authUserId`). If `actor_type = 'staff'`, `actor_record_id` is the `staff.id`; platform admins without a staff row get `received_by: null` (the column is nullable). Same fix applied to `createDiscount()` / `approved_by` (same FK, same wrong value, same resolution pattern). `handleRecordPayment` and `handleApplyDiscount` in `FinanceModule.tsx` updated to pass `authUserId` instead of the old `staffId`.

  **(3) Feature: payment notes field.**
  `payments` table has no `notes` column in the §7.16 schema. Migration added (`migration_add_notes_to_payments.sql` — safe to re-run, uses `IF NOT EXISTS` guard). `recordPayment()` now accepts `notes?: string | null` and inserts it. `loadStudentPayments()` selects and returns `notes`. `PaymentForm` interface gains a `notes: string` field. Payment form UI gains a textarea below the date field (3 rows, placeholder "e.g. Part payment — balance of ₦5,000 expected by end of term"). Payment history rows show notes in italic below the "Recorded by" line when present. `Payment` interface updated with `notes: string | null`. CSS: `.fin-payment-notes` and `.fin-textarea` classes added to `phase6-finance.css`.

  **(4) Feature: fee head editing.**
  `updateFeeHead()` added to `financeService.ts` (updates `name`, `is_recurring`, `default_amount`; no `currency` change — that stays `NGN` at the DB default). `editingFeeHeadId: string | null` state added to `FinanceModule`. `openFeeHeadFormForEdit(fh: FeeHead)` function pre-fills the fee head form and sets `editingFeeHeadId`. `handleAddFeeHead()` branches on `editingFeeHeadId` to call `updateFeeHead` vs `createFeeHead`. An "Edit" button (admin-only, `fin-feehead-edit-btn` class) added to each fee head row in the Fee Heads tab. Form sheet title and save button label update dynamically ("Edit fee head" / "Save changes" vs "Add fee head"). Close and cancel handlers reset `editingFeeHeadId` to null. CSS: `.fin-feehead-edit-btn` added.

  **7 tsc errors fixed in `libraryService.ts` across two `npm run build` passes.**

  *Pass 1 — 5 errors, all the same root cause:* Supabase's PostgREST client always returns joined relations as `T[]` (arrays), even for logically one-to-one joins using `!inner` or `.single()`. The casts were written as if the relations were single objects, which tsc correctly rejects as non-overlapping types. Fix pattern in every case: cast through `unknown` first to break tsc's overlap check, then to the target array type and pluck `[0]`.
  - Line 153: `(r.subjects as { name: string }).name` → `(r.subjects as unknown as { name: string }[])[0]?.name ?? null`
  - Line 183: same pattern on `data.subjects` in `addBook()` result mapping
  - Line 501: `f.borrow_records as Record<string, unknown> | null` → `(f.borrow_records as unknown as Record<string, unknown>[] | null)?.[0] ?? null`
  - Line 536: `data.book_titles as { title: string } | null` → `(data.book_titles as unknown as { title: string }[] | null)?.[0] ?? null`
  - Line 577: `(r.digital_resource_tags ?? []) as { resource_subject_tags: ... }[]` → cast through `unknown` to break the nested-array incompatibility

  *Pass 2 — 2 errors:*
  - Line 106: `todayISO()` function declared but never called anywhere → deleted entirely. The function body was also broken: `d.toFullYear` doesn't exist on `Date` (typo for `getFullYear`), and the conditional was nonsensical (checking whether a method exists on a class instance is always true). Dead code, deleted. If a today-ISO string is needed at a call site, `new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)` is the inline form.

  This session addressed three bugs surfaced after Session 26 browser testing, plus one deferred feature (student code). Work was performed in the previous session chat and is recorded here retroactively.

  **(1) `authService.ts` — `loginWithCode` fully fixed (raw fetch + trim/uppercase).** The prior raw-fetch rewrite (Session 25) was confirmed correct in structure but two additional gaps caused "Invalid login code" to persist:
  - `supabase.functions.invoke()` had already been replaced with raw `fetch` (Session 25); the fix was in-place but had not yet been browser-tested.
  - Added `.trim().toUpperCase()` on the `code` argument before sending — so `guard001`, `GUARD001`, and `" Guard001 "` all normalise to `GUARD001`, matching the uppercase-generated code stored in `app_identities`.
  - Added explicit null-check: if `access_token` or `refresh_token` are absent from the Edge Function response, a user-readable error is returned instead of a silent crash.
  - Added top-level `try/catch` for network errors (offline, DNS failure) with a plain-English message.
  - Diagnosis note recorded: the STU-PCGZF2 / PCGZF2 "Invalid login code" errors seen in screenshots were expected — those were student codes generated by the new auto-generate button, not guardian login codes. Guardian login codes come exclusively from the provision flow. The seeded `GUARD001` code remains valid.

  **(2) Phone OTP — "Unsupported phone provider" root cause identified.** This is a Supabase project configuration issue, not a code bug. Supabase phone OTP requires a Twilio (or equivalent SMS provider) account configured under Authentication → Providers → Phone in the Supabase Dashboard. On the current project this is unconfigured. Fix: connect a Twilio account (Account SID, Auth Token, Message Service SID or From number). Until configured, the Parent tab (phone OTP) will always fail with this error. The Code tab remains the practical guardian login method in the interim. **No code change needed — Supabase Dashboard action required by owner.**

  **(3) Phone E.164 normalisation — `StudentsModule.tsx` + `GuardianModule.tsx`.** When `login_method = 'phone_otp'`, the phone number must be in E.164 format (`+2348012345678`) for Supabase Auth to accept it. No normalisation was happening. Fixed in two layers:
  - **Client side:** `normalisePhone()` helper added to both `StudentsModule.tsx` and `GuardianModule.tsx`. Handles Nigerian numbers: 11-digit local (080… → +234…), 10-digit (no leading 0), 13-digit starting with 234, and already-formatted (+…). Returns `null` for invalid input. `handleProvision` in both files now calls this before invoking the Edge Function; invalid input surfaces a user-readable error before any network call.
  - **Edge Function side:** `provision-guardian-access/index.ts` already had a regex guard (`/^\+\d{10,15}$/`) documented in the plan — confirmed present; no change needed.

  **(4) Student code — new field added to `students` table and `StudentsModule.tsx`.** The `student_code` field was previously deferred. Now fully built:
  - **Migration (`add_student_code.sql`):** adds `student_code`, `blood_group`, `address`, `medical_notes`, `emergency_contact_name`, `emergency_contact_phone` to `students` (all nullable). Partial unique index `students_school_code_unique` on `(school_id, student_code) where student_code is not null`. Safe to re-run (`add column if not exists`). **Must be run in Supabase Dashboard → SQL Editor before the updated code is used.**
  - **`StudentsModule.tsx`:** `student_code` added to `FormState`, `EMPTY_FORM`, `openDetail` pre-fill, `handleSubmit` params, and the optimistic update object. UI: text input (auto-uppercased on input via `toUpperCase()`) with a "Generate" button (`generateStudentCode()` produces a `STU-XXXXXX` random alphanumeric code). Field appears in both the Add Student form and the Info tab edit form. Brief tab's "More details" section shows the code in monospace when present. Student list row shows the code in the meta sub-line when present.
  - **`generateStudentCode()` helper:** random 6-char suffix from `ABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZ23456789` (same ambiguous-char-free alphabet as guardian login codes), prefixed `STU-`. Not collision-checked client-side (the unique index on the DB will reject duplicates; user retries or edits manually).
  - **CSS (`stu-code-additions.css` → append to `src/index.css`):** `.stu-code-row`, `.stu-input--code`, `.stu-code-gen-btn`, `.stu-field-hint`, `.stu-brief-code`.
  - **`studentsService.ts`:** `student_code?: string | null` needs to be added to the `Student` interface and the `createStudent`/`updateStudent` function signatures and select strings. **Not yet patched — owner to provide `studentsService.ts` file or confirm shape so this can be completed.**

Any signed-in actor reaching the grid could edit scores.   **Owner's clarifying question, resolved before writing the fix:** confirmed the intended design is (a) a staff member can only edit scores for classes they're actually assigned/scoped to, not just "any class with an assignment," and (b) an admin can grant a specific staff member an override for any class without changing their role. Checked this against the already-built (Session 8) class-scoped permissions architecture — `canForClass(key, classId)` in `permissionsService.ts`/`authStore.ts` was built for exactly this: staff-level override (`staff_permission_class_scope`, can grant a key the staff member's role doesn't hold at all — explicit owner decision from Session 8) checked first, then role-level default scope (`role_permission_class_scope`), `class_id IS NULL` meaning unrestricted. This mechanism existed but had never actually been used by any converted module yet — `ResultsModule.tsx` is the first to call `canForClass()` rather than plain `can()`.

  **Mapping:**
  - Score-entry cells (`renderScoreCell`'s `readOnly`, `handleScoreSave`) → `canForClass('academics.scores.enter', selectedAssign.class_node_id)` — class-scoped, not a flat check, per the owner's confirmed design. Gated at both the UI (`readOnly` + explanatory `title`) and the handler itself (visible per-cell error message, reusing the existing `errorKeys`/`errorTimers` auto-clear-after-3s pattern already built for save failures) — not just the visible control, per §4.12's "fail gracefully with a clear message" principle.

  - **Bug A, "the back button need to actually return to where you come from":** root cause traced to a genuine mechanism confusion, not a mislabel. `detailTab` (local subtab state inside the student detail sheet: `'brief' | 'info' | 'guardians' | 'status'`) and `onNavigate` (app-level module routing, confirmed via grep to have no navigation-history stack anywhere in the app) are two unrelated systems — the button was labeled "back" but called `onNavigate('guardians')`, which abandons the student's detail sheet entirely and jumps to the separate top-level `GuardianModule.tsx`.   - **Bug B, "even if a Guardian has a login code, the card... persists... one may easily regenerate the Guardian code":** root cause was a fetch-timing bug, not stale UI. `identities[link.guardian_id]` was only populated on-demand (granting access, or opening the provision form), so any already-provisioned guardian's entry sat at `undefined` on a fresh detail-sheet open. The "not yet provisioned" branch checked `identity === null || identity === undefined`, collapsing "never fetched" and "genuinely no login" into one UI path — so an already-provisioned guardian showed the unprovisioned card, and "Set up login →" routed into the same create/regenerate call as "Change / regenerate," but without that button's confirm gate. **Fixed:** `fetchGuardians()` now eagerly calls `fetchGuardianIdentity()` for every guardian already flagged `has_platform_access: true`, immediately after the list loads, so `identities` resolves to its real value before the card renders — closes the accidental-regenerate path structurally, not with a second confirm gate bolted onto a still-wrong card.

The guardian-facing piece surfaced a real, owner-flagged security question — **checked, not assumed:** the initial implementation queried `attendance_records` directly filtered by `class_node_id`, which `attendance_records_guardian_select`'s real RLS policy (confirmed via `pg_policies`) does not permit — a guardian can only read their own linked child's rows, not classmates'. This would have shipped as a silent dead feature (no error, `classAveragePercent` always `null`) rather than a visible bug. Fixed properly, not by loosening RLS: a `SECURITY DEFINER` Postgres RPC (`get_class_attendance_average`) that derives `school_id` from the caller's own session (`current_school_id()`, never a client-supplied value), verifies the caller is a guardian genuinely linked to an enrolled student in the requested class, and returns only a single rounded percentage — no per-student rows ever reach the client. Explicitly checked and confirmed this design cannot leak data across schools or across classes within the same school, per the function's own two-part authorization check. **One real bug found and fixed in the RPC itself, caught via the owner's actual on-device network trace, not assumed correct from code review:** the aggregate query referenced `attendance_records.class_node_id`, a column that does not exist on that table (confirmed via `information_schema.columns` — class linkage exists only via `students.class_node_id`, joined through `student_id`) — Postgres error `42703`. Fixed by joining through `students` in the aggregate query (the authorization check's own query already did this correctly; only the final aggregate was wrong). **✅ Confirmed working on-device by the owner** after the join fix — no console errors, class-average comparison visible and correct.
