  **Part B — unplanned: subdomain/identity mismatch, a real auth-boundary gap (found via the Part A Done Check itself):**

  While running the two-school side-by-side check, owner discovered that a staff account for School A could log in successfully under School B's subdomain — and would land inside the app seeing their own (School A) data, but wrapped in School B's name/logo/brand color as shell chrome.

  **Root cause, confirmed by reading the actual files, not assumed:** `authStore.ts`'s `resolveIdentity()` looks up `app_identities` by `auth_user_id` alone — it never checks which subdomain the browser is currently on. `App.tsx` resolves the subdomain's school independently (`getSlugFromHostname` → query `schools` by slug) and hands `schoolId={school.id}` — the **subdomain's** school — to every module, with no comparison anywhere against the authenticated identity's own `schoolId`. Confirmed this is *not* an RLS/data-leak issue: RLS keys off `auth.uid()` regardless of what `schoolId` prop a component receives, so the person's own data was always what came back underneath — but that RLS was the only thing preventing an actual leak here is not a design to lean on, and the auth boundary itself was making a promise ("you are logging into School B") that nothing enforced.

  **Fix implemented in `App.tsx`:** an `isWrongSchool` check, computed unconditionally alongside the component's other hooks (not after an early return — this file's own existing comment already warns about the exact hook-order hazard that would cause), comparing the authenticated identity's `schoolId` against the subdomain-resolved `school.id`. `platform_admin` is exempted (that actor type is legitimately `schoolId: null` by design per `authStore.ts`). A `null` identity (no resolvable `app_identities` row) is treated as a mismatch, not waved through — an unresolvable identity is not evidence of belonging, and the first draft of this check got this backwards (guarded the check on `!== null`, which silently passed broken identities through) before being caught and corrected. On mismatch: `supabase.auth.signOut()` fires from a `useEffect`, and a sticky `wrongSchoolBlock` state flag (not derived from `session`, specifically so it survives the session going `null` a moment later) keeps the correct branch showing.

  **Two further self-corrected bugs during this fix's own iteration, recorded honestly:** (1) first version called `signOut()` directly inside the render body rather than an effect — unsafe (violates render purity) — restructured into the `useEffect` above. (2) the wrong-school render check was initially placed *after* the `if (!session)` early-return check — meaning once `signOut()` resolved and `session` cleared, the `!session` branch won the race every render and silently swapped the message for the login page before the person could read it (the "blinking" the owner reported). Fixed by reordering the wrong-school check to run first. Also added a reset case (`wrongSchoolBlock` clears once a genuinely matching session exists) so a correct login right after a wrong-school attempt, on the same mounted `App` instance, doesn't stay stuck on a stale message.

  **UI iterated per two rounds of owner feedback:** originally a full dedicated "Wrong school" page; owner asked for the copy to actually explain what happened (both messages rewritten to state that the login *worked*, that they were signed out deliberately for safety, and what to do next — kept generic, no naming of the person's real school, owner's explicit call after discussing the trade-off: naming it would hand real information to an unverified caller for free, and doesn't help the legitimate case either); owner then asked to collapse the separate page entirely into a banner on the ordinary `LoginPage`, form still usable underneath (owner's explicit preference after being shown the alternative of hiding the form). Implemented via a new `topLevelError` prop on `LoginPage.tsx`, rendered as a banner between the brand strip and the card — sized to the card's own 400px max-width, token-based danger colors, left-aligned icon + text. Final copy, per owner's explicit final instruction to keep it generic regardless of which of the two failure cases (mismatch vs. unresolvable identity) triggered it: *"This isn't your school — check the URL or link your school gave you."*

  **Second, previously-unnoticed duplicate found and fixed while building the banner (owner approved fixing it same-pass):** `.form-error` was declared twice in `index.css` (once token-based, once with hardcoded hex/border) — the later, hardcoded declaration was silently winning the cascade everywhere the class was used. Checked all usages first (`LoginPage.tsx`'s two forms, identical class usage, no site relying on the second block's specific look) before removing the hardcoded duplicate and keeping the token-based one.

  **Verified:** brace/paren balance and a real `esbuild` TSX parse (not just brace-counting) on `App.tsx` and `LoginPage.tsx` at every edit checkpoint, confirmed `--color-danger-200` doesn't actually exist in the token set before a first draft used it (swapped to the real `--color-danger-100` rather than ship a silently-always-falling-back reference), confirmed `.school-not-found` CSS class is still legitimately used by the genuine "school not found" (unregistered subdomain) branch elsewhere in `App.tsx`, confirmed `identitySchoolId` remains meaningfully referenced (not orphaned) after the copy was simplified to generic wording. **Owner confirmed the fix works on-device** across both the original blink and the final banner-on-login-page version.

  **New open question surfaced, not yet resolved (owner testing, not this session's scope to fix):** owner attempted to register the same staff email across two different schools and it failed. Confirmed why, not assumed: `auth.users.email` is unique project-wide in Supabase (not per-school) — this is Supabase Auth's own global constraint, not something this schema controls — and `app_identities` is designed around exactly one row per `auth_user_id` (`resolveIdentity`'s `.maybeSingle()` would itself throw on a second match). So one email can only ever belong to one school's identity, permanently, under the current design. A real person genuinely on staff at two schools has no path today except using a distinct email per school. Supporting true one-person/multi-school identities would be a materially bigger change — dropping `app_identities`'s uniqueness, changing `resolveIdentity` to fetch and filter by subdomain instead of assuming a single match, and turning today's wrong-school rejection into a school-selector instead — **flagged for an explicit owner decision, not attempted**, since it's a real product-shape question, not a bug.

  **Four real bugs found and fixed this session** (owner follow-up requests surfaced the last two, which weren't visible until the rebuilt CSS was actually used):

  3. **Day-header contrast bug** (new finding, introduced by this session's own header restyle): the solid `--color-brand-800`/`-700` day-header fill was reusing `--color-brand-on`, which `deriveBrandScale()` computes only against the working *600* shade. For gray/mid-tone or legibility-corrected pale brand picks, this let black text land on an 800-shade background at ~2.4:1 contrast — well under WCAG AA's 4.5:1. **Fixed at the root, not patched in CSS**: added real `on700`/`on800` fields to `deriveBrandScale()` and `applyBrandTheme()` in `themeService.ts`, computed independently per shade rather than inherited from `on`. Verified with a 5,000-sample random-hex-color scan — zero AA failures across the full range, including near-black and legibility-corrected pale picks.

Root cause: `.tt-grid` and `.tt-col--periods` both carried `overflow: hidden`, which made *them* — not the real scroll container `.tt-grid-wrapper` — the nearest ancestor `position: sticky` binds to. Both `overflow: hidden` declarations were removed; `.tt-grid-wrapper`'s existing `overflow: auto` now correctly owns scrolling and the rounded-corner clipping that `.tt-grid`'s removed rule used to provide. Verified no visual regression (hover-lift transforms still clip correctly against the wrapper).

Fixed with a shared deterministic, non-wrapping height on both `.tt-cell--break` and `.tt-cell--break-fill`. **The real fix — converting to true CSS Grid so row heights are always shared, fixing this bug class permanently rather than per-instance — is a named follow-up (~150-200 line rewrite of `TimetableGrid()`), not silently dropped.**

| SESSION 64 (PRD Problem 8.7a): what does `students.status` (`active`/`inactive`/`alumni`) mean for a higher-ed student — manual field like secondary, or derived from `student_programme_placements` (owner decision, 2026-07-17, before any code written)? | **`active` is derived, not manually toggled: a higher-ed student is `active` if and only if they have a current (`is_current = true`) `student_programme_placements` row — never set by hand for these schools.** This is a deliberate departure from secondary's model, where `status` is an independent manual field with no structural link to `class_node_id` — flagged as an intentional divergence, not an inconsistency, the same way SESSION 55 flagged `student_programme_placements` itself as a deliberate departure from the `class_node_id` precedent. `alumni` means the student has completed their final `programme_level_id` (graduation) — set once a promotion run (SESSION 69) advances a student off the last level of their programme, not by manual admin toggle. **Practical consequence for SESSION 64's own build:** `status` cannot be read as freestanding truth for a higher-ed student anymore — every call site must instead derive it from placement history (`is_current` for active; highest-`programme_level_id`-with-no-further-promotion for alumni) or, if `status` is kept as a stored column for query-performance/indexing reasons, it must be written *only* by the placement/promotion write paths (SESSION 64's placement changes, SESSION 65's admission, SESSION 69's promotion) and never exposed as an admin-editable field in `StudentsModule.tsx` for higher-ed students the way it is for secondary. **One thing this decision does not yet resolve, flagged rather than guessed:** `inactive` has no defined trigger yet for higher-ed (a secondary student going `inactive` is a manual admin action — e.g. suspension — with no higher-ed equivalent decided). Not blocking SESSION 64's own scope (active vs. not-yet-admitted is the only distinction that session's Done Check needs), but a real open question before `inactive` can be meaningfully surfaced anywhere for a higher-ed student; carried forward as a named gap, not silently resolved either way. |
| SESSION 64 (PRD Problem 8.7a): should a higher-ed student's derived `active` status (locked above) be stored on `students.status` and kept in sync by every placement-writing path, or computed live at read time with nothing stored (owner decision, 2026-07-17, "prioritise best practices")? | **Computed live, nothing stored — a value with no independent write path cannot drift, by construction, rather than by relying on every future write path remembering to sync it.** Reasoned directly from two prior, real incidents in this same codebase rather than a general preference: SESSION 62pre's `is_passing` gap (a second `ScoredAttempt[]` construction site silently kept using a stale inference after the first site was fixed correctly) and the repeated `current_staff_id()`/`current_actor_id()` invented-function pattern are both instances of the same failure class — one source of truth, accessed through more than one path, where only some paths get updated. Storing and syncing `students.status` from `upsertPlacement()` would create exactly this shape: SESSION 69's promotion flow would *also* need to remember to touch `status` on every level advance, and an alumni transition would need a third write path to remember it too — each new writer is a fresh chance to forget. **Concretely, for higher-ed students:** `students.status` is no longer read as ground truth anywhere in the higher-ed path. `loadStudents()`/`getStudentStatusCounts()` (`studentsService.ts`) gain a higher-ed query branch that joins/filters against `student_programme_placements.is_current` directly instead of the stored `status` column; `StudentsModule.tsx`'s Brief and Status tabs read the same derived value via a new `settingsService.ts` function (`loadStudentCurrentPlacement()`) rather than `detailStudent.status`. Secondary-school students are entirely unaffected — `status` remains the real, manually-set column for them, unchanged. `inactive`'s definition for higher-ed remains an open, explicitly-carried-forward gap (see the SESSION 64 row directly above) — not resolved by this decision, since a derived `active` doesn't by itself define what "not active but not yet alumni" should mean. |
| SESSION 65 (PRD Problem 8.7a, items 1/7): should the matric-number format be fixed per this school, or admin-configurable — and if configurable, which values can be used as components (owner decision, 2026-07-17, before any code written)? | **Fully admin-configurable, not fixed — confirmed against real research before designing, not assumed.** Web research on real Nigerian institutional practice (JAMB/NUC-adjacent sources, and this school's own hand-typed precedent `MED/NSC/26/001`) confirmed numbering conventions genuinely vary by institution in exactly the ways §7.27.1's own header note already flagged — component choice, ordering, and separators all differ school to school. This school's own example already uses two distinct code segments before the year (a programme-level code and a department-level code), directly evidencing that a flexible, ordered-component model is the right shape, not a fixed 3-part template. **Owner's explicit component list, going beyond the original card's own `{programme}/{year}/{sequence}` suggestion:** programme code, faculty code, department code, admission year/session, a free-text constant (e.g. a school abbreviation), and the sequence number itself — all selectable, all reorderable. **Real schema gap found while designing this, not before:** `programmes` has no `code` column at all today (only `faculties.code`/`departments.code` exist, per §7.27.1) — a small additive migration is required to support "programme code" as a real component, not an invented one. |
| SESSION 65 (PRD Problem 8.7a, items 1/7): should each component's separator and ordering be independently configurable, or is a fixed separator with configurable order sufficient (owner decision, 2026-07-17)? | **Separator is itself configurable per component, not fixed.** The admin builds an ordered list of components, and each component (other than the first) carries its own preceding separator (e.g. `/`, `-`, or none) — not one single separator applied uniformly across the whole format. This directly matches the owner's own stated goal ("which comes first... with slash in between or not") rather than a narrower "reorder only" interpretation. The sequence component additionally carries its own digit-count (zero-padding) setting, since the owner explicitly named "what's the digit count" as a required configurable dimension. |
| SESSION 65 (PRD Problem 8.7a, item 2): what should the matric sequence number's uniqueness/reset scope be — school-wide, per-programme forever, or per-programme-per-admission-year (owner decision, 2026-07-17, "prioritise best practice")? | **Per programme + admission year — the sequence resets to 1 for each programme at the start of each new admission year, matching real Nigerian institutional convention** (the researched precedent, e.g. NEGIS's own documented `YYYY/NNNN` shape, resets per year; this school's own `MED/.../26/001` example is consistent with a year-scoped low sequence rather than an accumulated running total). Implemented via a real counter table (`matric_sequence_counters`, keyed on `(programme_id, admission_year)`) incremented atomically at admission time — not a derived `max(matric_number) + 1` read, which would race under concurrent admissions and is also fragile against manually-entered historical numbers (like `MED/NSC/26/001` itself) that may not parse back into a clean integer. |
| SESSION 65 (PRD Problem 8.7a, item 7 — correction, owner walkthrough 2026-07-17, post-migration): should the admission screen live inside `SettingsModule.tsx`'s `InstitutionTab` (where it first shipped), or be relocated — and if relocated, where (owner decision: "prioritise UX best practices")? | **Relocated to a new top-level `AdmissionModule.tsx`, its own route/nav entry — not a Settings sub-screen, and not folded into `StudentsModule.tsx`'s per-student detail-sheet tab bar either.** Reasoned from three independent, concrete problems the original placement created, not just a tidiness preference: (1) **permission mismatch** — Settings' `InstitutionTab` and the admission action were both gated on the same `academics.institution_structure.manage` key, conflating "can redefine the faculty/programme hierarchy" (rare, high-trust, one-admin) with "can admit a student" (frequent, potentially multi-staff, lower-trust-per-action) — these need to be separable, which a shared tab makes awkward; (2) **state-lifecycle collision** — Settings tabs are built to load once and sit idle, while admission during a real admission period wants its own list state, refresh cadence, and a running "admitted today" count, which is exactly the "one shared load lifecycle, multiple callers with different needs" shape SESSION 64's own postmortem already flagged as a recurring defect class in this codebase; (3) **discoverability** — external research on comparable SIS platforms during a real admission period confirms admissions staff want a workflow "kept separate" from other roles' flows, and a separate SIS UX case study's core complaint was too many small tabs on one page making actions hard to find — both cut against burying a high-frequency operational action inside a rarely-touched config tab. `StudentsModule.tsx`'s existing detail-sheet tabs were considered and rejected too: that surface is scoped to one already-existing student's record, not a list-level "admit a new or existing student" operation. `AdmissionModule.tsx` reuses SESSION 64's programme/level picker component rather than duplicating it, and gets its own permission key (to be named when built) instead of continuing to share `academics.institution_structure.manage` with institution-structure edits. **Practical consequence:** the admission UI already shipped inside `SettingsModule.tsx`/`InstitutionTab` this session is superseded, not additionally correct — it must be removed from there once `AdmissionModule.tsx` exists, not left as a second, redundant entry point. |
| SESSION 65 (PRD Problem 8.7a, item 1 — correction, owner walkthrough 2026-07-17, post-migration): once real admissions exist against a matric-number format, should the format stay freely, silently editable (as shipped), or be protected — and if protected, by a soft-lock, by versioning, or both (owner decision: "both if possible, prioritise best practice")? | **Both, as one mechanism, not two competing ones — versioning is the actual data-integrity fix; the soft-lock is the UX surface a user experiences on top of it.** Root problem identified before deciding the fix: `matric_number_formats` shipped this session as a single upsert-in-place row per school, but `admit_student()` reads whatever that row currently says at call time — so an admin editing the format mid-year (reordering components, changing digit-padding, swapping a separator) silently changes the shape of every *subsequent* number under the same `(programme_id, admission_year)` counter scope, with zero record that a change ever happened and no way to explain, after the fact, why two students admitted months apart under the "same" programme/year have differently-shaped numbers. This is a genuine data-integrity gap, not a style concern, and matches this codebase's own established precedent for exactly this class of problem (`promotion_history`, `academic_standing_events` — audit trails that are appended to, never overwritten in place). **Decided:** `matric_number_formats` becomes append-only — each save inserts a new row (`is_active boolean`), the previously-active row is flipped to `is_active = false` rather than mutated, and `admit_student()`/`build_matric_number()` read whichever row is currently `is_active = true` for the school. Every generated matric number becomes traceable to the exact format version that produced it (a `format_id` reference, exact placement — on the placement row or a new column — to be finalized at implementation time, not guessed here). **The soft-lock is UI, not a second data mechanism:** once `matric_sequence_counters` has any row with `current_value > 0` for a school, saving a new format shows an explicit warning ("N students already admitted under the current format — saving a new one won't change their existing numbers, but every admission from now on will use the new one") rather than a silent overwrite — not blocked outright, since a school legitimately fixing a mistake before real admissions ramp up needs to still be able to, just no longer a casual, consequence-free edit once real numbers exist. **Practical consequence:** the plain-upsert `saveMatricNumberFormat()`/`matric_number_formats` shipped this session must be migrated to this versioned shape before being considered closed — the single-row version is superseded, not additionally correct. |
| SESSION 65a (PRD Problem 8.7a, items 1/7 — correction, owner walkthrough 2026-07-17): should the admission redesign include Direct Entry (DE) applicants now, or defer it as a later add-on (owner decision)? | **In scope now, not deferred.** `admission_applications`'s `entry_mode` column and its DE-specific fields (`de_*`) are part of SESSION 65a's own migration, not a follow-up session. Real Nigerian institutional practice (confirmed by research) treats DE as a parallel admission route with its own document set (A-Level/ND/NCE results, advanced-standing level placement) rather than a UTME variant — modeling it from day one avoids a second schema pass later to retrofit a route that's genuinely common at Nigerian higher institutions, not a rare edge case. |
| SESSION 65a (PRD Problem 8.7a, items 1/7 — correction, owner walkthrough 2026-07-17): how should rejected applicants' data be purged under NDPA retention expectations — a scheduled job, a manual admin action, or purge-on-next-login (owner decision: "scheduled job, if infra supports it")? | **Scheduled job, confirmed feasible before assuming it — not guessed.** Researched directly: `pg_cron` is available on all Supabase tiers, including free, enabled via a single SQL statement, no external infra required. The job hard-deletes any `admission_applications` row where `purge_at < now()` (`purge_at` set at rejection time from the school's own `rejection_retention_days` setting, default 90 — SESSION 65c). **One caveat recorded, not silently dropped:** free-tier Supabase projects auto-pause after 7 days of inactivity, which would silently pause the cron job too — flagged in the migration's own comment as a post-launch spot-check item (`cron.job_run_details`), not a blocker to shipping the job itself. |
| SESSION 65a (PRD Problem 8.7a, items 1/7 — correction, owner walkthrough 2026-07-17): should application fields (JAMB/O'Level/Direct-Entry data) be one shared field set for the whole school, or can different pipelines define their own distinct field set (owner decision)? | **One shared, school-wide field set — not per-pipeline.** `admission_field_settings` is a single row per school (enable/required per field, plus a `custom_fields` extension array), not one row per pipeline. A Direct-Entry-specific field simply sits unused/hidden for a UTME applicant rather than needing a second field-configuration surface per pipeline — avoids the same "one concern, N places" duplication this codebase has already caught itself on more than once (SESSION 62pre's `is_passing` gap, the `current_staff_id()`/`current_actor_id()` duplication, and SESSION 65's own admission/settings file-split reasoning). |
| SESSION 65a (PRD Problem 8.7a, items 1/7 — correction, owner walkthrough 2026-07-17): can a pipeline stage (e.g. Screening) be enabled with zero of its components checked, or must at least one component be checked for a stage to be considered "on" (owner decision)? | **At least one component required — a stage with zero components checked is not a valid enabled state.** Enforced at two levels, not just the settings UI: the Admission Settings form (SESSION 65c) must not allow saving a stage checked "on" with nothing under it selected, and the stage-advance function itself (SESSION 65a) treats a component-less stage as absent from the pipeline rather than as a pass-through no-op — the same "don't let the DB and the UI silently disagree about what's enforced" discipline already applied to the matric-format soft-lock (UI warns, DB is the real gate). |
| SESSION 65a (PRD Problem 8.7a, items 1/7 — correction, owner walkthrough 2026-07-17): should a pipeline's stage order be author-configurable per pipeline, or fixed for every pipeline (owner decision, resolving Claude's own flagged recommendation)? | **Fixed order for every pipeline: Application → Screening → Decision → Clearance.** Schools only choose which stages *appear* (by enabling/disabling them per pipeline), never their sequence. No real institutional precedent was found for running Clearance (confirming documents/fees for someone who already has an offer) before a Decision has been made — the flexibility would add real schema/UI/stage-advance-function complexity (an authored `sequence` column, reordering UI, out-of-order-transition validation) for a case that doesn't correspond to any actual admissions workflow. Reflected directly in schema: `admission_pipeline_stages` carries no `sequence` column — order is encoded once, in the stage-advance function itself, not authored per pipeline. |

### Feature 2: Scheme of Work — 🔄 In Progress (started 2026-08-27)

**Status:** Build clean, 15 audit fixes applied, two-kind template system implemented, session/class filters added.

**Design summary (from PRD §7.15a, Problem 8.6):**
- Teachers create/submit a scheme of work (structured term plan, broken down by week/topic, per subject and class)
- Teachers can adopt/adapt a standardized curriculum template (NERDC/WAEC placeholders) as a starting point
- Admins track each teacher's actual progress against their submitted/adopted scheme over the term
- Submit → approve/return workflow required, not self-publish
- Weekly coverage tracking in scope for first launch

**5 tables:**
- `schemes_of_work` — per-teacher, per-assignment scheme (draft → submitted → approved/returned)
- `scheme_of_work_weeks` — weekly/topic breakdown (week number, topic, objectives, activities, resources, coverage status)
- `curriculum_templates` — platform-level board templates (NERDC/WAEC), `is_placeholder` flag for unverified content
- `school_curriculum_templates` — school-owned reusable templates (name, optional subject/level plain-text labels)
- `school_curriculum_template_weeks` — weekly content for school-owned templates

**3 permission keys:**
- `academics.scheme_of_work.view_all` — admin/HOD see all schemes
- `academics.scheme_of_work.manage` — teachers create/edit/submit own schemes, manage school templates
- `academics.scheme_of_work.approve` — admin approve/return

**15 audit fixes (v2):**
- RLS on `curriculum_templates` for writes (admin only)
- `term_id` nullable on `schemes_of_work`
- `submitScheme` accepts draft|returned (not just draft)
- `loadCurriculumTemplates` accepts boardName filter
- `loadSchemeDetail` optimized (avoids N+1)
- Cascading dropdowns in import modal
- Coverage tracking for scheme owner
- Import warning for already-imported schemes
- Manage templates UI (CRUD on board templates)
- Real NERDC+WAEC template content (78 weeks across 6 subject sets)
- SQL apostrophe fix in set notation string

**3 migration files:**
- `migration_scheme_of_work.sql` — original schema
- `migration_scheme_of_work_v2.sql` — audit fixes + real template data
- `migration_scheme_of_work_v3.sql` — school template tables + `is_placeholder`

**UI (3 screens):**
- List: status tabs, session filter, class filter
- Templates: board templates (read-only adopt) + school templates (CRUD adopt)
- School template builder: name + optional subject/level + weeks

**Files to create:**
- `migration_scheme_of_work.sql`
- `migration_scheme_of_work_v2.sql`
- `migration_scheme_of_work_v3.sql`
- `src/services/schemeOfWorkService.ts`
- `src/routes/SchemeOfWorkModule.tsx`

**Files to modify:**
- `src/App.tsx` — route + More sheet entry
- `src/routes/AdminDashboard.tsx` — summary card
